The Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, September 2025. (Alex Brandon/AP)
Hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen.
In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it “does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.”
Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force’s IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay or logistics and maintenance.
Among them are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air defense radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 U.S. Air Force locations around the world.
SAIC was the prime contractor for Cloud One until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force.
Cloud One is among the U.S. military’s biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources.
“A breach here is a big deal,” one of the sources said.
Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the U.S. military’s cyber force, to assess the damage, one of the sources said.
Cyber Command did not respond to requests for comment.
The discovery of the hack led to a range of disruption. Two of the sources, along with a fourth person familiar with the matter, said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused.
Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked.
All five sources spoke on condition of anonymity.
One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. That person likened the control plane to a universal remote, as intruders in theory could leverage their access to check the operational status of military aircraft or the movement of spare parts, though it was unclear whether the hackers did so in this case.
Reuters could not identify the specific vulnerability exploited by the hackers.
News of the breach comes amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions, a particularly serious problem for cloud-based networks because of the ability of AI models to swiftly detect weaknesses across wide surface areas.
The U.S. government already has been dealing with the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a recent leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department.
Cloud One has long been in the crosshairs of hackers.
In a 2023 commentary carried by the online publication FedScoop, Cloud One’s leadership touted what they called a “100% success rate” in beating back what they said was a “staggering” number of attempts to penetrate the platform.
“There is no room for error when it comes to security,” Cloud One’s leadership wrote.
Mike Stone and Raphael Satter, Reuters

Memorandum of November 23, 2026
Expeditious Enforcement of Capital Sentences and the Pursuit of Justice for Victims of Heinous Crimes
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, I hereby direct:
Section 1 . Background. A prolonged delay in carrying out a death sentence is a grave offense to the justice system that denies a victim's family the closure they deserve. Yet capital sentences imposed upon the most vile criminals are too often frustrated by years, or even decades, of litigation. The Department of Justice must take every step to ensure that those who commit the most heinous crimes promptly face the full consequences of their actions.
Sec. 2 . Pursuing Capital Punishment for Heinous Federal Crimes. The Attorney General, when appropriate and consistent with applicable law, shall pursue Federal jurisdiction and seek the death penalty for particularly heinous and egregious Federal capital crimes, in addition to those identified in section 3(b) of Executive Order 14164 of January 20, 2025 (Restoring the Death Penalty and Protecting Public Safety), to include:
(a) murder in the first degree of a minor;
(b) murder committed in the course of rape, sexual abuse, sexual exploitation of a child, or sex trafficking; and
(c) murder committed in the course of kidnapping or human trafficking.
Sec. 3 . Expediting the Enforcement of Capital Sentences. The Attorney General shall take all lawful and appropriate measures to ensure that federally imposed sentences of death are carried out as expeditiously as possible. These measures shall include:
(a) prioritizing the prompt resolution of direct appeals, petitions for writs of habeas corpus, and other post-conviction proceedings;
(b) opposing dilatory litigation tactics;
(c) seeking expedited judicial consideration wherever appropriate; and
(d) eliminating unnecessary administrative delays.
Sec. 4 . General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this memorandum shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
(b) This memorandum shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
(c) This memorandum is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.
(d) The costs for publication of this memorandum shall be borne by the Department of Justice.
Washington, November 23, 2026

This proceeding involves efforts by the Lake Providence Port Commission (LPPC), a noncarrier political subdivision of the State of Louisiana, to acquire the portion of the McGehee-Tallulah rail corridor owned by Delta Southern Railroad, Inc. (DSRR), a Class III rail carrier, through a feeder line application under 49 U.S.C. 10907 and 49 CFR part 1151.[1] LPPC owns two other segments of the corridor (one, jointly with North Louisiana & Arkansas Railroad, Inc. (NLA)), and Southeast Arkansas Economic Development District owns a third segment. NLA holds operating authority over these three segments and has been designated by LPPC as the proposed operator of DSRR's segment if the feeder line application is granted. ( See, e.g., Am. Appl. 1, 19-20, 56, 58-59, Jan. 4, 2023.)
This decision provides notice of LPPC's amended feeder line application and adopts a procedural schedule for the submission of competing applications, comments and verified responses, and verified replies.
LPPC's initial feeder line application, which sought to acquire only part of the Line, was accepted and a procedural schedule established in early 2021. See Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La., FD 36447 (STB served Jan. 15, 2021). On August 23, 2022, the Board granted LPPC's request to file an amended application, see Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La., FD 36447 (STB served Aug. 23, 2022), which LPPC filed on January 4, 2023, seeking to acquire the entire Line. Following an unsuccessful challenge by DSRR to the completeness of the amended application and LPPC's satisfaction of certain technical requirements, see Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La. ( Nov. 2023 Decision), FD 36447, slip op. at 6-13 (STB served Nov. 20, 2023), LPPC's amended application was conditionally accepted, and LPPC was permitted to proceed with valuation discovery under the process specified in the November 2023 Decision. SeeLake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La. ( Dec. 2023 Decision), FD 36447, slip op. at 2 (STB served Dec. 11, 2023). In accordance with that process, LPPC notified the Board that it completed that valuation discovery on May 29, 2024, and submitted supplemental evidence regarding valuation of the Line, based on data provided by DSRR in response to LPPC's discovery requests, in July 2024.
Shortly thereafter, the Board placed this proceeding in abeyance pending resolution of state court litigation relating to LPPC's authority under Louisiana law to pursue the feeder line application. See Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La.August 2024 Decision), FD 36447 (STB served Aug. 2, 2024). In a decision served September 25, 2025, the Board, among other things, removed the proceeding from abeyance, noting that the question surrounding LPPC's authority had been resolved by the passage of new state legislation, and directed the parties to confer and submit a proposed procedural schedule by October 9, 2025. See Sep. 2025 Decision, FD 36447, slip op. at 6-8.
Thereafter, the parties submitted competing proposals for a procedural schedule, and DSRR filed a motion to strike or compel related to four of LPPC's shipper witnesses, to which LPPC and the shipper witnesses each filed a reply in opposition. In light of these unresolved issues and ongoing disputes, by decision served December 12, 2025, the Board assigned an administrative law judge (ALJ) to handle all remaining discovery matters. See Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La. ( Dec. 2025 Decision), FD 36447, slip op. at 3 (STB served Dec. 12, 2025). Between December 31, 2025, and July 2, 2026, the ALJ issued several decisions addressing discovery disputes.
By decision served May 27, 2026, the Board directed LPPC to file by June 16, 2026, any revisions to its valuation calculations and supporting evidence that LPPC believed were warranted based on the updated information DSRR provided in discovery. See Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison(May 2026 Decision), FD 36447, slip op. at 2-3 (STB served May 27, 2026). The May 2026 Decision also set a deadline of July 6, 2026, for the close of discovery and stated that notice of the amended feeder line application would thereafter be published in the Federal Register and a procedural schedule set. Id. at 3. On June 16, 2026, LPPC filed and served various revisions to its valuation calculations and supporting evidence.
On July 2, 2026, the ALJ denied a DSRR motion to compel NLA to respond to certain discovery. See Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La. ( July 2026 Decision), FD 36447 (STB served July 2, 2026). On September 2, 2026, the Board denied DSRR's appeal of two aspects of the ALJ's July 2026 Decision. SeeLake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La. ( Sep. 2026 Decision), FD 36447, slip op. at 3-6 (STB served Sep. 2, 2026). ( printed page 76864) The Board also authorized DSRR to reopen two depositions for the limited purpose of examination pertaining to an unwritten modification agreement between LPPC and NLA. See id. at 7-8. By letter dated September 30, 2026, DSRR informed the Board that it had conducted the reopened depositions. ( See DSRR Letter, Sep. 30, 2026.) [3]
On October 30, 2026, DSRR filed a motion requesting that the Board issue a procedural schedule, along with a proposed schedule for filings. ( See DSRR Mot. for Procedural Schedule, Oct. 30, 2026.) LPPC replied to the motion on November 2, 2026. ( See LPPC Reply, Nov. 2, 2026.)
As explained in the December 2023 Decision, the Board's acceptance of the amended application was conditional to permit LPPC to seek discovery of DSRR and to file revised valuation calculations and supporting evidence. Dec. 2023 Decision, FD 36447, slip op. at 2. Discovery has been completed, and LPPC has filed its updated valuation calculations and supporting evidence. Accordingly, notice of LPPC's amended application will be published in the Federal Register .
The September 2025 Decision directed the parties to confer and submit (jointly, if possible) a proposed procedural schedule that took into account a reasonable period of time for DSRR to complete discovery and the general timeline for record-building contemplated by the Board's regulations at 49 CFR 1151.2(c), (e), and (f). Sep. 2025 Decision, FD 36447, slip op. at 8. The parties submitted separate proposals on November 19, 2025.[4] ( See DSRR Mot. for Procedural Schedule, Nov. 19, 2025; LPPC Response, Nov. 19, 2025.)
DSRR included a new proposed procedural schedule with its October 30, 2026 motion. DSRR proposes 30 days—the time period specified by 49 CFR 1151.2(c)—for the filing of competing applications. (DSRR Mot. for Procedural Schedule 3, Oct. 30, 2026.) DSRR proposes that verified statements and comments addressing both the amended application and any competing applications be due 60 days thereafter—more than the 30 days contemplated in 49 CFR 1151.2(e). (DSRR Mot. for Procedural Schedule 3, Oct. 30, 2026.) DSRR states it “expects its filing to be extensive and robust given the substantial record.” ( Id. ) DSRR also argues the record will show LPPC has failed the public convenience and necessity (PC&N) test [5] so substantially that the Board could benefit from bifurcating the PC&N analysis from consideration of the constitutional minimum value (CMV) of the Line.[6] Finally, DSRR proposes 20 days for the filing of verified replies to responses to the amended application and any competing applications. (DSRR Mot. for Procedural Schedule 3, Oct. 30, 2026.)
In reply, LPPC states that it supports issuance of a procedural schedule and responds to various assertions in DSRR's motion. ( See LPPC Reply, Nov. 2, 2026.) LPPC generally does not oppose the schedule DSRR proposes; however, LPPC requests 30 days (rather than 20) to file its verified reply, given the anticipated length of DSRR's response to the amended application. ( Id. at 3-4.) LPPC objects to DSRR's suggestion that the Board consider only whether LPPC has satisfied the PC&N test and delay determining the CMV of the Line. ( Id. at 2-3.)
DSRR's proposed schedule, modified to permit 30 days for the filing of verified replies, is reasonable and will be adopted. However, to avoid unnecessary delay, DSRR's request to bifurcate will be denied. Accordingly, all filings should address the PC&N standard, the CMV of the Line, and financial responsibility.
For the reasons discussed, DSRR's October 30, 2026 motion for issuance of a procedural schedule will be granted in part, and the following procedural schedule will be adopted for this proceeding:
Competing applications by other parties seeking to acquire all or any portion of the Line are due by December 28, 2026.
Verified statements and comments addressing the amended application and competing applications must be filed by February 25, 2027.
Verified replies by applicants and other interested parties must be filed by March 29, 2027.
1. Notice of LPPC's amended feeder line application will be published in the Federal Register .
2. DSRR's October 30, 2026 motion for issuance of a procedural schedule is granted in part, as explained above.
3. The schedule set forth above will govern this proceeding.
4. This decision is effective on its service date.
Decided: November 24, 2026.
By the Board, Anika S. Cooper, Chief Counsel, Office of Chief Counsel.
1. The McGehee-Tallulah rail corridor extends from milepost 408.9 in McGehee, Ark., where it connects with Union Pacific Railroad Company, south to milepost 498.44 in Tallulah, La., where it connects with Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited (CPKC). DSRR owns and operates the southernmost segment of the corridor, from milepost 471.0 at Lake Providence, La., south to the connection with CPKC at milepost 498.44 in Tallulah (hereinafter, the Line).
2. A more detailed description of the procedural history and background of this proceeding is provided in the Board's decision served on September 25, 2025. See Lake Providence Port Comm'n—Feeder Line Appl.—Line of Delta S. R.R. Located in E. Carroll & Madison Pars., La. ( Sep. 2025 Decision), FD 36447, slip op. at 2-6 (STB served Sep. 25, 2025).
3. LPPC also filed a letter on September 30 noting that the reopened depositions had concluded and requesting that the Board “promptly issue a procedural schedule.” (LPCC Letter, Sep. 30, 2026.) On October 13, 2026, LPPC informed the Board, among other things, that corrected transcripts for the reopened depositions had been served on DSRR's counsel but stated it is not necessary to delay issuance of the procedural schedule to allow time for DSRR to provide those transcripts to the Board. (LPPC Letter, Oct. 13, 2026.) DSRR filed the corrected transcripts with the Board on October 22, 2026.
4. Because of a lapse in the Board's appropriation, the initial October 9, 2025 deadline for proposals was extended to November 20, 2025. See Materials Due to Be Submitted During the Fed. Gov't Shutdown, EP 751, slip op. at 1 (STB served Nov. 13, 2025).
5. Under 49 U.S.C. 10907, a financially responsible party may obtain a Board order requiring the sale of a rail line in two situations, only one of which is applicable here: when the PC&N require or permit the sale. 49 U.S.C. 10907(b)(1).
6. To be an eligible purchaser under the feeder line program, an applicant must show it is financially responsible. 49 U.S.C. 10907(b)(1)(B). To be considered financially responsible, the purchaser must be able to (1) pay the CMV for the line and (2) cover the expenses of operating on the line for at least the first three years. Id. 10907(a).

Notice, request for comments on this collection of information.
The Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS), as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, conducts a pre- ( printed page 76793) clearance consultation program to provide the general public and Federal agencies with an opportunity to comment on proposed and/or continuing collections of information in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA). The PRA ensures that data requested by the Federal Government can be provided in the desired format, reporting burden (time and financial resources) is minimized, collection instruments are clearly understood, and the impact of collection requirements on respondents can be properly assessed. This notice informs the public of the agency's intent to request renewal of the clearance for the IMLS Grants to States Five-Year State Plan Guidelines for State Library Administrative Agencies. The current five-year period covers fiscal years (FYs) 2022-2027. The upcoming five-year period will cover FYs 2028-2032, with Five-Year State Plans due to IMLS on June 30, 2027. A copy of the proposed information collection request can be obtained by contacting the individual listed below in the ADDRESSES section of this notice.
Written comments must be submitted to the office listed in the addressee section below on or before January 26, 2027.
Send comments to Sandra Narva, Lead Senior Grants Management Specialist, Office of General Counsel, ATTN: Grants Management, Institute of Museum and Library Services, 200 Constitution Ave. NW, Suite N-3629, Washington, DC 20210. Ms. Narva can be reached by telephone, 202-653-4634, or by email at snarva@imls.gov. Office hours are from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., E.T., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
Teri DeVoe, Associate Deputy Director for Grants to States, Office of Library Services, Institute of Museum and Library Services, 200 Constitution Ave. NW, Suite N-3629, Washington, DC 20210. Ms. DeVoe can be reached by telephone at 202-653-4778, or by email at tdevoe@imls.gov. Office hours are from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., E.T., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
IMLS is particularly interested in comments that help the agency to:
Evaluate whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and
Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who respond, including through the use of appropriate automated electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques, or other forms of information technology,e.g., permitting electronic submissions of responses.
IMLS is the primary source of Federal support for the Nation's libraries and museums. The agency advances, supports, and empowers America's museums, libraries, and related organizations through grant making, research, and policy development. For more information about IMLS, visit www.imls.gov.
This action proposes clearance of the IMLS Grants to States Program Five-Year State Plan Guidelines for State Library Administrative Agencies for FYs 2028-2032.
The Grants to States program is the largest grant program administered by IMLS, providing Federal financial assistance to develop library services throughout the States, U.S. Territories, and the Freely Associated States. Title 20 of the United States Code (U.S.C.) § 9141, “Grants to States.” To receive funds under the Grants to States program, each established State Library Administrative Agency (SLAA) must submit to the Director of IMLS a Five-Year State Plan detailing certain goals, assurances, and procedures for a five-year period. 20 U.S.C. 9134(a), “State plans.” The upcoming five-year period will cover FYs 2028-2032, with Five-Year State Plans due to IMLS on June 30, 2027. The Five-Year State Plan identifies a State's library needs, sets forth the activities to be taken toward meeting the identified needs supported with the Federal funds made available under the Library Services and Technology Act (LSTA), and provides assurances that the officially designated SLAA has the fiscal and legal authority and capability to administer all aspects of an award issued under the Grants to States program. 20 U.S.C. 9122(5), “Definitions—State plan.” The Five-Year State Plan must also provide assurances for establishing the State's policies, priorities, criteria, and procedures necessary to the implementation of all programs under the LSTA. 20 U.S.C. 9122(5), “Definitions—State Plan.”
Authority for this action is provided by 20 U.S.C. 9134, “State Plans,” 20 U.S.C. 9141, “Grants to States,” and 20 U.S.C. 9103(h), “Regulatory authority.”

LISBON - Europe's largest utility, Iberdrola, has scrapped plans for a €427-million ($468-million) green ammonia plant in Portugal, following a review of its investment priorities, it said on Thursday.
The Green Ammonia Express plant in Sines, south of Lisbon, was announced in 2024 and was designed to produce green hydrogen using 137 MW of electrolyser capacity, enabling annual production of around 95 000 tons of green ammonia.
Liquefied green ammonia was expected to be transported to the port of Sines via pipeline and exported by sea to facilities where it would be used to produce agricultural fertilisers and other chemical products.
The Spanish utility company said in response to a question from Reuters the plant "was part of its green hydrogen project portfolio".
However, it said that "following a review of investment priorities, Iberdrola decided not to proceed with Green Ammonia Express, which was still at a preliminary stage of development".
The low-carbon ammonia industry, a cleaner alternative to conventional ammonia production using natural gas, has come under pressure from weak demand and high costs.
Germany's RWE withdrew from Namibia's $10-billion Hyphen green ammonia project in September 2025, citing slower-than-expected European demand for hydrogen and its derivatives such as ammonia.

台湾会投票恢复核电——为什么这对人工智能很重要？ |核能新闻|半岛电视台
台湾会投票恢复核电吗？为什么这对人工智能很重要？在社交媒体上
2021 年 12 月 4 日，台湾抗议者模仿逃离核爆炸 [Lam Yik Fei/Getty Images]
在最后一个运行的反应堆关闭 18 个月后，台湾选民将决定是否恢复核电。
关于这个问题的全民投票将于周六与地方选举同时举行。这是该岛在短短八年内第四次就核电进行投票。
列表 3 习近平称台湾将与中国“完全统一”
随着人工智能泡沫担忧加剧，亚洲股市下跌（共 3 个）中的 2 个
英伟达黄仁勋回归未能平息人工智能疑虑，亚洲市场跳水 3 个
与此同时，中国蓬勃发展的计算机芯片产业对电力的需求猛增，人们越来越担心，如果中国声称台湾是自己的领土，在紧张局势升级的情况下切断与台湾的联系，台湾将如何维持电力供应。
选民被问及政府是否应该恢复使用核电来提振经济。这将意味着废除该国长期以来的“无核家园”政策。
反对党国民党提出公投，台湾人民党也表示支持。立法院于8月批准了公投，中央选举委员会于8月28日签署。
要通过，“赞成”票数必须超过“反对”票数，并超过所有合格选民的四分之一。
长期以来一直奉行无核政策的执政党民进党（DPP）正在敦促“不”。民进党立委陈佩瑜称公投没有必要，并表示立法者可以通过修改现行法律来改变政策。
台湾曾经严重依赖核电。 1985 年，其三个工厂生产了全国 52% 的电力。
随后，核电成为台湾政治中党派偏见最严重的问题之一。台湾大学国家发展研究所助理教授列夫·纳赫曼表示，这种分歧可以追溯到民进党成立之初。
纳赫曼告诉半岛电视台：“党内有一个主要的环保主义者团体非常反核。”相比之下，核工业是在国民党的领导下建立和运营的。
纳赫曼说，两极分化将其变成了“一个非常绿与蓝的问题”，他指的是民进党和国民党的颜色。
安全担忧根深蒂固。纳赫曼表示，台湾非常密切地关注 2011 年邻国日本福岛核电站的熔毁事件。
“人们担心台湾发生的任何核反应都会摧毁整个岛屿，”他说。活跃的地质断层线横贯台湾，如何处置核废料的问题仍未解决。
民进党自 2016 年以来一直执政，部分原因是承诺逐步淘汰核电。去年5月，台湾关闭了位于屏东县马鞍山的最后一座反应堆。
为什么核电又重新提上议程？
在之前的三场公投中，公众意见不一。 2018年，选民选择取消逐步淘汰核电的法定期限。但在 2021 年，他们拒绝重新启动未完工的第四座核电站的建设。去年8月，重启马鞍山工厂的多数投票因投票率低而无效。

Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI? | Nuclear Energy News | Al Jazeera
Share Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI? on social media
Taiwanese protesters mimic escaping from a nuclear explosion, December 4, 2021 [Lam Yik Fei/Getty Images]
Voters in Taiwan are set to decide whether to bring back nuclear power – 18 months after its last operational reactor was shut down.
A referendum on the issue is being held alongside local elections on Saturday. It is the island’s fourth vote on nuclear power in just eight years.

list 2 of 3Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
list 3 of 3Asia’s markets dive as return of Nvidia’s Huang fails to quell AI doubts
It comes as demand for electricity to fuel the country’s burgeoning computer chip industry soars and concern grows about how Taiwan would keep its lights on if China, which claims the island as its own territory, cut it off amid escalating tensions.
Voters are being asked whether the government should return to using nuclear power to boost the economy. That would mean abolishing the country’s longstanding “nuclear-free homeland” policy.
The opposition Kuomintang (KMT) proposed the referendum and the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) is also backing it. The legislature approved the referendum in August and the Central Election Commission signed it off on August 28.
To pass, ‘yes’ votes must outnumber ‘no’ votes and exceed a quarter of all eligible voters.
The ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which has long had a policy of no nuclear power in its mandate, is urging ‘no’. DPP legislator Chen Pei-yu called the referendum unnecessary, saying lawmakers could change the policy by amending existing laws instead.
Taiwan once relied heavily on nuclear power. In 1985, its three plants produced 52 percent of the nation’s electricity.
Nuclear power then became one of the most partisan issues in Taiwanese politics. Lev Nachman, an assistant professor at the Graduate Institute of National Development at National Taiwan University, said the divide goes back to the DPP’s founding.
“There was a major group of environmentalists that were part of the party that were very anti-nuclear,” Nachman told Al Jazeera. The nuclear industry, by contrast, was built and run under the KMT.
Polarisation turned that into “a very green-versus-blue issue”, Nachman said, referring to the colours of the DPP and the KMT.
Safety fears run deep. Nachman said Taiwan watched the 2011 Fukushima nuclear plant meltdown in neighbouring Japan very closely.
“There is this sort of fear of any sort of nuclear reaction that would ever happen in Taiwan would just devastate the entire island,” he said. Active geological fault lines run across Taiwan and the question of how to dispose of nuclear waste remains unresolved.
The DPP has governed since 2016, partly on a pledge to phase out nuclear power. In May last year, Taiwan shut down its last reactor at Maanshan in Pingtung County.
Why is nuclear power back on the agenda?
Public opinion has been mixed in three previous referendums. In 2018, voters opted to scrap a legal deadline for phasing out nuclear power. But in 2021, they rejected restarting construction on an unfinished fourth nuclear plant. In August last year, a majority vote to restart the Maanshan plant was voided due to low turnout.
Now, nuclear power is back on the agenda because surging electricity demand from Taiwan’s semiconductor and AI industries, along with growing fears about energy security and over-reliance on imported fuel, have renewed the debate over how the island keeps the lights on in an emergency.
According to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan imports more than 97 percent of its energy. Natural gas generates about 43 percent of its electricity and coal about 35 percent. Both arrive by ship.
Taiwan only has about 11 days of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in reserve. Japan and South Korea hold between 14 and 20 days.
“There’s two sides to it,” Nachman said. The first is energy security: “If China actually blockades Taiwan and cuts off access to the outside world, then Taiwan only has so much energy it can rely on.”
The second is the chip industry, which requires huge amounts of power and “that’s only going to increase over time”, he said.
The war with Iran this year has added to the pressure by disrupting LNG shipments from the Middle East.
Will the ruling party change its stance?
The DPP has already started to shift. In March, President William Lai Ching-te said the government would begin the process of restarting the Maanshan and Kuosheng plants. He cited AI-driven demand and conflicts abroad causing disruption to energy supplies.
On September 24, the Nuclear Safety Commission approved state-owned Taipower’s restart plan for Maanshan. Further safety assessments are still needed before it can operate again.
Nachman said Lai has tried to push his party to rethink its “very dogmatic anti-nuclear stance”. The question is whether DPP voters have come around.
Nuclear power is not Taiwan’s first choice for filling the gap, however. “Investment in LNG – that’s still Taiwan’s kind of number one goal,” Nachman said.
How important is Taiwan’s microchip industry?
Taiwan is the most important link in the global AI supply chain.
It makes more than 90 percent of the world’s most advanced semiconductors, nearly all of them at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). TSMC has more than 60 percent of the global contract chipmaking market.
Its customers include Nvidia – the world’s most valuable semiconductor company – AMD and Apple. TSMC makes Nvidia’s Blackwell and Rubin AI processors, and Taiwanese firms such as Foxconn and Quanta build most of the world’s AI servers.
That uses huge amounts of electricity and water. In September, Taiwan’s semiconductor industry used more than 4.5 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity for the first time. That was up 11.55 percent from a year earlier, driven by AI demand.
S&P Global estimated that TSMC alone used about 8 percent of Taiwan’s electricity in 2023. That share could rise to almost 24 percent by 2030, it added.
Nachman cautioned against seeing the referendum only through the demand for microchips and semiconductors. “In today’s media, Taiwan has become a single issue, just about semiconductors,” he said. “For a lot of people in Taiwan, the semiconductors aren’t even the priority. It really is the security side.”
Will China object to Taiwan having nuclear power?
Probably not. Beijing does not appear to have commented on the referendum itself.
“The nuclear issue is a completely separate issue from anything related to China,” Nachman said. “It’s much more a matter of domestic politics.”
China has, however, used Taiwan’s energy weakness in its messaging. In March, Chen Binhua, a spokesman for China’s Taiwan Affairs Office, said closer integration with China could help solve Taiwan’s energy problems. He pointed to the island’s reliance on oil and gas from the Middle East.
Taipei rejects unification with Beijing. Analysts writing in The Diplomat called the offer an exercise in optics.
However, it remains a top priority for China. During a speech in Beijing on November 12, President Xi Jinping once again stated that Taiwan and China must be reunified.
The referendum is about civilian power reactors, not weapons. Asked whether Taiwan might seek a nuclear weapon, Nachman said: “No, of course not. This is just about nuclear power.”
Taiwan did secretly pursue nuclear weapons in the 1970s and 1980s. The programme was shut down in 1988 under US pressure, after a senior nuclear scientist, Chang Hsien-yi, defected to the United States.
Since then, Taiwan’s leaders have consistently stated that they will not seek nuclear weapons. Its nuclear facilities are inspected under an arrangement between Taiwan, the US and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
The bigger worry is a blockade by China if it seeks to press reunification in the future. Nachman said large military drills and naval patrols China has held around Taiwan since US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi’s visit in 2022 have all rehearsed one.
Will the referendum pass and what happens next?
Nachman said he is sceptical. “We keep doing it over and over again and it still doesn’t usually pass,” he said. “So my expectations are actually fairly low.”
The outcome will depend on DPP supporters. “It’s really more a matter of whether or not green voters have come around to it,” Nachman said.
If the referendum does pass, he said Lai and the DPP “would probably be largely okay with it”.
The restart process is already under way either way. Supporters say reactors could be running again within 18 months to three years. Opponents say a restart could take five to 10 years and cost several hundred billion New Taiwan dollars.
Results are expected on Saturday night.

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

content:
Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family
“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

content:
Fundraiser by Tarra Subhar Massallo : Immediate aid for families affected by the Nepal-Tibet Flood
This fund provides direct aid for shelter, food, and essentials to Nepal-Tibet families
Tarra Subhar Massallo is organizing this fundraiser.
After fleeing from the Chinese annexation of Tibet, many Kyirong Tibetan families crossed into Nepal believing their exile would be temporary. It was not. Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley had become their home instead- a place where hundreds of families had to rebuild from nothing, including my grandparents. Like many Tibetan refugees, they eventually moved on to build new lives in India. However, not everyone left. Some of their family stayed behind in Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley, carrying on the roots left behind by previous generations.
On August 26, 2026, a glacier collapse high in the Langtang Himal sent a wall of water and debris surging down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Bazaar: the towns where that branch of our family stayed and built their lives after losing everything once before. Four households in our family were directly affected:
Our cousin Dawa Dakpa (confirmed deceased) leaves behind a wife and two young children.
Aku Jangchup, his wife, and child (confirmed deceased)
Nama Nangsa Ghongma's family and relatives (missing)
Nama Karmo Subhar's family and relatives (missing)
Now, our families face rebuilding once again, with roads and homes submerged in mud. 100% of every contribution will go directly to these impacted families and the wider flood-affected communities as they recover together. The funds will be spent on various essentials based on each family's needs (including, but not limited to: temporary shelter, food, emergency medical care, and transportation costs). We invite you to help write the next chapter of this story. Please help support this fundraiser in any way that you can.
My name is Tarra Subhar Massallo. I am the granddaughter of Tibetan refugees who fled from Kyirong during the 1959 Chinese annexation of Tibet, and the daughter of a Tibetan immigrant mother who moved from India to the United States with her family in search of a better life. Growing up in a mixed household, I am surrounded by the importance of my many cultures and giving back to my respective communities.

content:
Fundraiser by Rohan Khadka : Support Geeta After Nepal-Tibet Flood Loss
Geeta’s fund covers funeral costs and long-term education for her son after Raj’s loss
Rohan Khadka is organizing this fundraiser.
Geeta Shrestha is Rohan’s longtime friend from kindergarten, and today Geeta is facing a heartbreaking loss that no family should have to endure. Geeta recently lost her husband, Raj Shrestha, in the Nepal-Tibet flood. Raj worked at the Rasuwagadhi Customs Office, and his sudden passing has left Geeta grieving while also caring for their young son on her own. After just welcoming a new baby boy, Geeta is now carrying the weight of loss, motherhood, and an uncertain future all at once.
This fundraiser is being organized so Rohan can collect support and send it to Geeta in Nepal. The funds will help cover Raj’s funeral costs and support Geeta’s son’s education and upbringing. These are not just immediate needs but ongoing ones, as Geeta now has to provide for her child over time without Raj’s support. Recurring donations can offer steady help for the continuing costs of raising her son and planning for his education, while one-time gifts will also make a meaningful difference during this painful time. Please help support Geeta, a mother of a 1-year-old baby, as she cares for her family and rebuilds after this devastating Nepal-Tibet flood loss. Every donation, share, and kind thought means so much.

Fundraiser by Tashi Gurung : Help Sumi Rebuild Her Future After the Tibet-Nepal Flood
Sumi and her brother rely on this fund for education and recovery after losing everything
Tashi Gurung is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Sumi. I am from Shyafru Besi, Rasuwa, and recently my family was victims of a very devastating Tibet-Nepal flood, due to which I lost my parents, almost all my relatives, and the village where I grew up. Currently, I can't explain the things that I am going through because, with my loved ones, I also lost everything my parents had worked for their entire life. Our parents are still missing, we have no financial support, and we have nothing left in our name, but all we have is hope that this fundraising can help us start a new life. With the money collected, we will be investing it in our education (me and my younger brother) and also with those siblings who lost their support due to this disaster.

Fundraiser by Hunter Ross : HELP NEPAL & TIBET FLOOD VICTIMS RECOVER AND REBUILD
This fund brings emergency supplies, shelter, and rebuilding to Nepal and Tibet communities
Inspire others and help Hunter build momentum.
Inspire others and help Hunter build momentum.
Hunter Ross is organizing this fundraiser.
Help Nepal Recover From Devastating Floods
My name is Hunter Ross, and I am from Dallas, Texas, USA. I am organizing this fundraiser to help provide relief to people and communities affected by devastating flooding in Nepal and Tibet.
Nepal has become much more than a country I visit. Over the years, I have developed a deep personal connection to Nepal through frequent travel, volunteering, environmental work, tourism development, and relationships with local communities.
I travel to Nepal approximately three times a year and have actively volunteered in efforts related to environmental conservation, sustainable tourism, and local community development. Through these experiences, I have met many wonderful people and developed relationships with individuals and communities who have welcomed me and shared their lives and culture with me.
I am not raising these funds because I am a government agency or large relief organization. I am an individual from Dallas who has spent years visiting Nepal, volunteering there, and building personal connections with people in the country. I want to use those connections and my experience in Nepal to help support people whose lives and livelihoods have been affected by flooding.
Severe flooding can have devastating consequences for communities in Nepal and Tibet.
Heavy rainfall, rising rivers, and flooding can damage or destroy homes, roads, bridges, farmland, businesses, and other essential infrastructure. Families can lose their possessions, crops, livestock, and sources of income.
In rural and mountainous areas, the consequences can be even more serious. When roads and bridges are damaged or washed away, entire communities can become isolated and difficult to reach. Access to food, clean drinking water, medical care, transportation, and other essential services can be severely disrupted.
Flooding can also create serious sanitation and health risks when drinking-water systems are contaminated or damaged.
The need does not end when the water recedes. Families and communities may require assistance for weeks or months as they clean their homes, replace essential belongings, repair buildings, restore access to roads and water systems, and rebuild their livelihoods.
My Relationship to the People I Am Raising Funds For
My relationship with the people I am trying to help comes from my years of travel, volunteering, environmental work, tourism development, and personal relationships in Nepal.
Because I regularly travel to Nepal and have spent significant time working with and learning from local communities, I have developed a strong connection to the people and places affected by these disasters.
I want to use this fundraiser to provide assistance to people who are directly affected by flooding, particularly vulnerable families and communities that may have difficulty accessing assistance.
I will be transparent with donors about where the money goes and will provide updates as the relief effort progresses.
How the $50,000 Will Be Spent
Our fundraising goal is $50,000.
The funds will be used for flood-relief and recovery needs. Depending on the circumstances and the most urgent needs identified on the ground, donations may be used for:
Emergency food and drinking water for affected families
Medical supplies and basic healthcare needs
Temporary shelter and essential household necessities
Clothing, blankets, and other emergency supplies
Assistance for families whose homes have been damaged or destroyed
Support for farmers and families who have lost crops, livestock, equipment, or other sources of livelihood
Transportation and delivery of relief supplies to affected communities
Repair or restoration of essential community resources and infrastructure where appropriate
Assistance to vulnerable families and remote communities that may be difficult to reach through traditional relief efforts
The exact allocation will depend on the needs identified in the affected communities at the time the funds are distributed.
I understand that I am accountable for using the money raised in the manner described in this campaign. I will make every effort to ensure that donations are used responsibly, transparently, and for legitimate flood-relief and recovery purposes.
Transparency is extremely important to me.
I want every person who contributes to understand who I am, why I am doing this, who the fundraiser is intended to help, and how the money will be used.
As the campaign progresses, I will provide updates regarding fundraising, relief efforts, and the use of donations whenever possible.
If circumstances change and a particular relief need is no longer present, funds may be directed toward another legitimate and urgent flood-recovery need within the affected communities rather than being left unused.
Nepal has given me incredible experiences, friendships, and memories. I have been fortunate to return to the country many times, and I have seen firsthand the generosity and resilience of the people there.
Now, I want to give something back.
A donation of $10, $50, $100, $500, or any amount you can afford can contribute to helping a family recover from a devastating event.
If you cannot donate, sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and social networks can be just as valuable. Reaching more people gives us a greater chance of reaching our $50,000 goal.
Fundraising Goal: $50,000
This campaign is about more than raising money. It is about standing with people who have lost homes, belongings, livelihoods, and a sense of security because of flooding.
I have spent years visiting and volunteering in Nepal, and I believe this is an opportunity to give back to communities that have given me so much.
Please consider donating and sharing this fundraiser.
Together, we can help provide immediate necessities while supporting the long process of recovery and rebuilding.
Thank you for taking the time to read my story, for caring about the people affected by these floods, and for supporting this effort.
Your donation starts Hunter’s journey to success by inspiring others to help.

Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

summary: Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser. What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex
content:
Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case
Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser.
What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.
（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）
With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.
（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）
In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.
（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）
Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.
（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。）
Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States.
（多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。）
Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.
（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）
After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.
（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。）
Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.
（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）
He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.
（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。）
The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.
（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）
We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.
（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）
The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.
（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。）
With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community.
（您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）
Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese:
https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole
(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)
（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）
http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641
(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)
（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金會”，每年頒發“推動中國進步獎”截至2019年已連續頒獎12屆。）
https://liuvswei.blogspot.com/2020/08/metoo.html
(by Lau Kayee, Chairwoman of Network for Women In Politics, Hong Kong; Spokeswoman of Hong Kong Civil Human Rights Front.)
（作者/劉家儀，香港婦女參政網絡主席，六四新生代秘書長，支聯會常委，香港市民捍衛人權陣線發言人。）
With your contributions, we will be able to set a positive example for #MeToo victims by raising awareness about women’s and children's rights, globally.
因您的資助，我們將能夠為#MeToo運動傷害者們建立一個積極的個案，為提高女性及孩童的權利意識而有所貢獻。

content:
Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!
在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！

Fundraiser by Alan Wan : Help Alan Navigate Life in Political Exile
Alan’s fund provides groceries and rent for a political dissident facing exile abroad
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Alan Wan is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Alan, and I am writing this with a sincere and humble heart.
I am a Chinese political dissident living in Houston, Texas. Because of my beliefs and my willingness to speak openly about freedom, human rights, and justice, I have faced serious threats and intimidation from the Chinese government. These pressures have made it impossible for me to safely return to China, where my family still lives. Every day, I carry the pain of being separated from my loved ones, uncertain when—or if—I will ever be able to reunite with them again.
Beyond the emotional suffering, I am now facing severe financial hardship. Due to restrictions and complications surrounding the transfer of my personal funds from abroad, I have been unable to access resources that I once depended on for survival. My savings are rapidly disappearing, and I am now struggling simply to cover basic daily necessities such as food, housing, transportation, and medical care.
This situation has left me feeling isolated and vulnerable. I never imagined that standing by my principles would lead to such profound personal sacrifice, but I continue to hold onto hope.
Today, I am reaching out with deep humility to ask for your support. Any assistance—whether financial help, practical resources, or connections to organizations that aid individuals in political exile—would mean more than words can express. Your kindness could help me maintain stability during this incredibly difficult chapter of my life and allow me to continue moving forward with dignity.
I am not asking for luxury, only for the chance to live safely and meet my most basic needs while I navigate these extraordinary challenges.
Thank you for taking the time to read my story. Your compassion, understanding, and support would be a lifeline during one of the hardest periods of my life.
Grocery and part of my rent.

Fundraiser by Pie Formosa : Support Pie Formosa’s Independent Work
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Pie Formosa is organizing this fundraiser.
I sometimes describe myself as a refugee from WeChat to Instagram — but I am also, quite literally, a refugee from China.
I am a political dissident, human rights activist, non-binary person and independent writer living with invisible disabilities, now continuing my work in Europe.
I write and create public work about censorship, authoritarianism, political memory, democracy, queer and trans freedom, refugee experiences, neurodiversity, and the cultural spaces where resistance survives.
For years, WeChat was one of the places where I published my work. Readers could easily support independent creators with small tips. Then the Chinese Communist Party shut down my account. I lost not only a platform, but also an audience, an archive, and a simple way for people to support my work.
This fundraiser is part of rebuilding that independence.
Living with invisible disabilities also means that conventional employment structures and constant high-intensity workloads are not always accessible or sustainable for me. I need a modest and stable income to make independent research, writing and human-rights work sustainable.
* research, writing and documentation
* travel to human-rights, democracy and civil-society events
* basic living costs that allow me to continue this work independently
If something I have written, documented or created has informed, helped or inspired you, even €1, €5 or €10 helps me keep this work alive. If donating is not possible, sharing this fundraiser also makes a real difference.
Authoritarianism depends on silence and forgetting. Independent voices survive because people choose to keep them alive.
Thank you for supporting my work.
