building resilience in the face of potential market manipulation. USA Rare Earth, another recipient of US government investment, has acquired a samarium production chain which relies on a British factory and a French stockpile with enough supply for between one and three years of US defense industry consumption. These types of industrial partnerships with Europe can fill American critical gaps. What Europe lacks in scale and investment, it makes up for in specialized expertise which is difficult, expensive, and time-consuming to replicate. Solvay, USA Rare Earth’s partner, has both a stockpile and rare-earth know-how. Its plant at La Rochelle, France, has been processing rare earths since 1948. Less Common Metals, a British metal and alloy producer, is now owned by USA Rare Earth and has a proprietary SmCo magnet production process that rivals China’s. Other German, Finnish, Swedish, and Estonian firms also have current or planned capacities across the rare earth permanent magnet supply chain—ranging from upstream mining and separation to SmCo magnet production. The European Union’s vast market offers a strong demand base for the expanding Western critical minerals production. Since adopting the Critical Raw Materials Act in 2024, the bloc has built a regulatory and policy framework for both internal investment and multilateral cooperation. The European Commission plans to establish a European Critical Raw Materials Center, designed to coordinate demand aggregation and project financing for minerals by drawing on some of the continent’s comparative strengths: market intelligence and cross-country coordination. The Center could provide a critical channel for information sharing and stakeholder mapping for US firms. This year, Washington and Brussels agreed to discuss border-adjusted price floors and offtake agreements. In addition, there are national initiatives; German companies, including BMW and Rheinmetall, said on November 23 that they planned a trading house to secure critical minerals. Europe is also widening its supplier base, and two partnerships stand out. The EU and Canada are pursuing multiple streams for critical mineral industry partnership, including closer cooperation on stockpiling and batteries, while in the longer run, the bloc’s relationship with Ukraine offers downstream demand. In July, the EU launched a defense industrial partnership with Kyiv covering drones, missile defense, artillery and other key components. Ukraine, which already mines titanium ore, has a critical minerals strategy and action plan and is actively seeking partners. No individual country has the scale or financing capability to build a fully self-reliant minerals supply chain to offset potential Chinese market manipulation. And time is short: China already dominates and has shown it is willing to restrict supplies, as it did to Japan in 2010 and to the US in 2025 , and has undercut competitors on price. Twelve NATO allies took an important step at this year’s NATO Ankara summit by formally launching a joint defense-critical raw materials initiative. The US, which is not a participant, should embrace this initiative and work with its allies to complement strategic reserves with long-term purchasing commitments and coordinated industrial investment. The immediate challenge is not to eliminate every dependency on China, but to ensure Beijing cannot interrupt essential Western defense production. The US should embrace Europe’s existing critical minerals capabilities as strategic assets, not simply temporary substitutes until American production comes online. Partnership on critical mineral supply chains both increases transatlantic security and serves as a nexus of transatlantic market growth and expertise-sharing that could move from catch-up to innovation and true resiliency. The goal should be to build a competitive allied industrial ecosystem that China cannot easily disrupt. Sharon Hudson-Dean is a Senior Fellow at the Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA) and an Associate Fellow at Chatham House in London. She is a veteran diplomat and senior foreign policy leader who has managed complex strategic, defense, and political policies throughout her career. Most recently, she served as US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Northern Europe, NATO, and Arctic Security (2024-25). Anping Zhu is a Yale University student majoring in global affairs, economics, and mathematics. He is a research assistant to CEPA Fellow Sharon Hudson-Dean for her expert comment series on critical minerals and the race to secure Western supply. He is a member of the Yale Foreign Policy Initiative and has worked as a policy research intern and adviser to the governments of Lesotho and Rwanda. 互动：追踪 COP31 气候峰会上的谈判文本 互动：谁在 COP31 气候变化峰会上想要什么 人们一直在互相指责，一些媒体将 COP31 的“崩溃”归咎于“石油资源丰富的国家”，而另一些媒体则指责欧洲“不愿”提供更多气候资金。虽然说 COP31 上“没有达成一致”的说法并不准确，但媒体的反应表明了分歧的复杂性。安塔利亚会议上展示的观点。在这篇文章中，Carbon Brief 汇集了世界各地媒体的反应，展示了对 COP31 结果反应的多样性。 COP31 发生了什么？对总统职位的反应是什么？石油资源丰富的国家的角色是如何描述的？发达国家的角色是如何描绘的？发展中国家的作用是如何描述的？中国的角色是如何描绘的？这对于共识进程和改革意味着什么？ COP31能否发出“积极信号”？ COP31 发生了什么？ COP31 结束时未能就土耳其和澳大利亚轮值主席国推动的拟议“安塔利亚协定”达成一致。最终文本被包括欧盟、英国和一些气候脆弱国家在内的至少 32 个国家否决，谈判拖延了两天，场面一片混乱。 《爱尔兰时报》的一篇社论称，这一结果是“在没有达成任何协议或前进路线图的情况下，缔约方会议以前所未有的方式结束”。
这种观点虽然在媒体上普遍表达，但却是不正确的。 正如资深“COP观察者”在CB Connect上的一篇文章中解释的那样，尽管总统的“掩护决定”失败了，但峰会就许多决定达成了一致。在谈到拒绝封面决定时，墨尔本大学气候研究人员杰奎琳·皮尔教授和凯瑟琳·鲍文教授在对话中写道，“这些文本一直是正式谈判过程的附加内容”。 .cb-membership-banner.alignfull { 框大小：边框框；宽度：var(--宽度--响应式--容器，计算(100% - 32px));边距：夹紧（24px，4vw，48px）自动；填充：20px 夹（16px、4vw、56px）；边框半径：5px；背景：

COP31 came to a dramatic close last weekend when a coalition of nations rejected the proposed “Antalya pact”, citing its failure to mention fossil fuels. The tense final moments and lack of a much-anticipated “pact” have sparked extensive media coverage around the world. Many commentators have rushed to label the COP31 outcome a “ failure ”, questioning what it means for the future of the UN climate process and a “ divided world ”. While it is not accurate to say there was “ no agreement ” at COP31, the media response demonstrates the complexity of the divergent views on display at the Antalya conference. In this article, Carbon Brief draws together media reactions from around the world to show the diversity of responses to the COP31 outcome. What happened at COP31? What happened at COP31?  COP31 ended without agreement on a proposed “Antalya pact”, which had been pushed by the Turkey-Australia presidency. The final text was rejected by at least 32 countries, including the EU, the UK and some climate-vulnerable countries, in chaotic scenes as the talks overran by two days. An Irish Times editorial said the outcome was an “unprecedented ending of a COP without any agreement or roadmap forward”.  This view, while commonly expressed in the media, is incorrect.  As veteran “COP-watchers” explained for an article on CB Connect , the summit reached agreement on many decisions, even though the presidency’s “cover decision” failed.  Referring to the rejection of the cover decision, Melbourne University climate researchers Prof Jacqueline Peel and Prof Kathryn Bowen wrote in the Conversation that “these texts have always been add-ons to the formal negotiation process”. .cb-membership-banner.alignfull { box-sizing: border-box; What has the reaction to the presidency been?  In the aftermath of COP31, commentators have critiqued decisions made by the presidency. An editorial in the Hindu noted that “usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations”, but said the COP31 leadership “thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings”.  Australian “president of negotiations” Chris Bowen has also faced criticism over how he managed competing interests at the summit. An editorial in the climate-sceptic Australian said: “One thing is clear: Chris Bowen, who presided over Australia’s $150m investment in the conference, has some explaining to do. International reporting has raised questions about Australia and Turkey, the two nations that co-hosted the summit. Similarly, climate-sceptic journalist Graham Lloyd wrote in the Australian that “globally, Bowen has embarrassed himself and diminished Australia’s reputation”.  For Australian news outlet Crikey , journalist Royce Kurmelovs said that Bowen “tried to run the world’s climate talks the way Labor [Australia’s ruling party] runs climate policy at home: quiet, pragmatic and without mentioning fossil fuels”, adding that “in Turkey, it didn’t work”. A commentary by journalist Xu Luyi in Chinese financial news outlet Caixin said that future COP presidencies should “distinguish achievable implementation measures from ambitions that lack a coalition capable of delivering them”. Separately, an editorial in the National – a UAE state-owned English-language daily newspaper – said “the next UN secretary general needs to restore the art of diplomacy”.  How has the role of oil-rich nations been portrayed?  In media coverage, much of the blame for the perceived failure of COP31 has been placed on oil-producing nations – particularly with the final cover decision draft containing no mention of fossil fuels.  Even before the summit had finished, Panama’s minister of environment Juan Carlos Navarro warned that the COP process was being “held hostage by the petroleum mafia”. After the talks had closed without a deal on the Antalya pact, a Guardian editorial said that responsibility lay with “petrostates resisting a transition away from fossil fuels”, along with a lack of climate finance . The “fossil-fuel backsliding” was being led by a “Saudi-Russian coalition”, it said. A Bloomberg editorial also noted that the omission of fossil fuels from the decision text came “amid pressure from Russia, Saudi Arabia and other fossil fuel producers”. A Times editorial described oil-rich nations, “led by Saudi Arabia”, as the “culprits” for the lack of an agreement, because they “insisted on dropping a reference to phasing out hydrocarbons”. In the i newspaper , David Shukman, a former BBC News science editor, described a “deception” at the “heart” of the COP process: “This pattern of lobbying by oil-rich nations has become increasingly blatant and aggressive over more than three decades.” Despite signing up to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) at the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, the participation of the “oil-rich minority” has been “in name only”, wrote Shukman: “At more than a dozen of the UN’s giant conferences, I’ve seen for myself the tactics of trench warfare and how well they’ve worked. It’s why fossil fuels remain so dominant and why the climate is turning so hostile.” Writing for the Guardian , University College London’s Prof Bill McGuire warned that the COP process had been “deeply compromised” by the “major fossil-fuel producers”. For Al Jazeera , York University’s Prof Ilan Kapoor added that “fossil-fuel power operates well beyond the conference hall”. ( Reuters reported that, according to negotiators from Europe, small-island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa, Saudi officials had “regular access” to the summit’s presidents, “allowing them disproportionate influence”.) In Australian outlet Inside Story , the University of Sheffield’s Prof Michael Jacobs wrote that since “transitioning away from fossil fuels” language was included in COP28 , fossil-fuel producers “have been determined to ensure the phrase would never be used again”.  Nick O’Malley, national environment and climate editor for the Sydney Morning Herald , noted: “The tension between the action the world knows it must take on climate change and that which a handful of oil-rich nations will allow it to take has been growing for years.” At the summit itself, shortly after rejecting the cover decision on behalf of the EU, Irish environment minister Darragh O’Brien told Agence France-Presse that the talks had been “hijacked by some oil states”.  The Backchannel substack collated reactions from negotiators and observers. Among them, Dr Mary Robinson – former president of Ireland – warned of the “disturbing politicised attacks on [climate] science from those still clinging to fossil fuels and looking to sabotage climate action”. In contrast, an editorial in the National loosely described a failure of the talks to “bridge divisions over fossil-fuel language, carbon capture and adaptation finance in the final draft”. It added: “Unfortunately, the gap between countries – major emitters, energy producers and the more vulnerable nations demanding accessible funding – proved too wide to close.” How has the role of developed nations been portrayed?  Much of the commentary about developed countries’ role at COP31 focused on the EU and the UK blocking the final “Antalya pact”, due to its lack of language about fossil fuels. A cover-decision text without such language was “vehemently opposed by dozens of countries, including the EU delegation strongly led by [Irish] minister for climate Darragh O’Brien”, according to the Irish Times .  Similarly, an editorial in the UK’s Times concluded that “several countries, including the UK, rejected a draft omitting the not insignificant matter of winding down fossil-fuel use”. Peter Prengaman, climate news director for the Associated Press , wrote that the EU and its allies “were no longer willing” to leave out fossil-fuel language. (He noted that “top polluter” the US was not present at the summit.) Other media outlets took a more balanced approach to the role of developed nations at COP31. A Guardian editorial concluded:  “European governments’ objection to fossil-fuel backsliding by a Saudi-Russian coalition was right, but they were wrong to rule out fresh EU funding for developing countries’ climate action.” Reflecting on the need for “funding to help the poorest countries adapt to global warming”, an editorial in Le Monde noted that “the most developed nations have been reluctant to increase their contributions, despite their historic responsibility for CO2 emissions”. An editorial in the Hindu stressed:  “It stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming.” Writing in US outlet Drilled , reporter Rishika Pardikar noted that “wealthy countries like Japan, the UK and Canada…largely aligned with the EU in opposing support mechanisms for developing countries like long-term finance, adaptation finance and just transition”. Climate campaigner John Gibbons wrote in the Irish Examiner that the EU was “right to reject” carbon capture and storage in the COP31 outcome, but accused O’Brien of “cosplay[ing] at being a progressive climate leader”, despite Ireland’s poor climate record. Many developed countries were not particularly vocal at COP31, and an editorial in Japan’s Yomiuri Shimbun lamented a general “low level of interest in and low priority given to global warming”. The editorial concluded: “It is hoped that Japan will continue to fulfill the practical roles expected of it and contribute to the international community in ways unique to Japan.” How has the role of developing nations been portrayed?  Equity, historical responsibility for climate change and a need for finance have all been portrayed at the centre of developing countries’ positions at COP31. A comment in the Hindu said that “India’s insistence on historical responsibility, climate finance and adaptation belongs at the centre of any credible plan to cut emissions”. It added that India had played a “constructive role” to “provide bridging language” in texts on adaptation and the just transition work programme. Down to Earth noted that “India has referred to historical responsibility in submissions at previous climate summits, but rarely with the emphasis evident” at COP31. Harjeet Singh, strategic adviser to the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative , told Radio France Internationale that those who criticise India’s opposition to fossil-fuel phaseout “need to acknowledge that there has been a lot of mistrust between India and developed countries”. Other developing countries also held firm, particularly on the issue of finance. Kenya’s the Star said the country had “drawn a firm line” at COP31 and would not “back down until an acceptable deal is secured on climate finance”. The outlet added that the country had “ruled out walking away from the negotiations”. Inter Press Service , a global south-focused news agency, noted that the “deadlock” at the talks leaves COP32 host Ethiopia “to pick up the pieces”. An editorial in the Mexican newspaper La Jornada called the failure to reach consensus “suicidal”, adding: “The conflict is far more complex than a mere opposition between the global north and south, or between hydrocarbon producers and consumers.” Indeed, some developing countries sided with developed countries in blocking the final passage of the Antalya pact.  The Fiji Times reported that Fiji “held the line in the final negotiating rooms”, joining the EU, the UK and several other Pacific countries in “refus[ing] to endorse a weakened compromise that avoided to mention fossil fuels [sic]”. It added: “Yet standing on principle carries heavy practical consequences…COP31’s breakdown is a sobering reminder that, while Fiji must keep fighting in global arenas, its sharpest shield remains regional solidarity and rapid, resilient action at home.” How has the role of China been portrayed? Major Chinese news outlets largely portrayed China as a constructive participant in the COP31 negotiations, a defender of multilateralism and an active advocate for international climate cooperation. State news agency Xinhua reported that “China acted responsibly and advanced the conference process, earning widespread recognition from all parties”. State broadcaster CCTV similarly said that the “international community recognised the positive role China played in addressing climate change”. People’s Daily , the official newspaper of the Communist Party of China, reported that China played a “constructive role” in building consensus and promoting cooperation. It quoted COP31 president Murat Kurum as saying that China was a “key participant” in the multilateral climate process and that its support was “crucial to the summit”. State news agency China News Service said that China demonstrated “ability to act” amid divisions at COP31, highlighting China’s participation in negotiations and initiatives on international cooperation in carbon credits and its climate actions in the global south.  Financial newspaper 21st Century Business Herald said that the Chinese delegation “actively participated in negotiations across all agenda items” and highlighted China’s efforts to advance practical cooperation on climate change.   Three of China’s main state media outlets, Xinhua , CCTV and People’s Daily , covered the COP31 outcome.  Xinhua said that climate multilateralism “moves forward under pressure” as COP31 concluded without a deal. Citing Chinese experts, Shanghai-based outlet the Paper reported that China, the African group and south-east Asian countries were among the parties “willing to accept a compromise [deal] to uphold multilateralism, despite being dissatisfied with the draft text”. CCTV reported that, although COP31 ended without adopting an “outcome document”, this did not mean international climate action had “come to a halt” or that previously agreed climate agreements and international promises would “automatically become invalid”.   State-run newspapers China Daily and the Global Times both published editorials on COP31.  China Daily argued that the COP31 “impasse” underscored the “need to strengthen multilateral cooperation”. It continued that China was “committed to addressing the climate crisis through real action.”  The Global Times editorial, meanwhile, responded to criticism that China was “unwilling to take the lead”. It said: “With its own climate governance arrears unpaid, how can western media expect China to ‘pick up the tab’?” Regarding China’s role at COP31, several western news outlets’ coverage focused on its approach to climate diplomacy, trade and the proposed final agreement.  Ahead of the summit’s conclusion, Reuters cited diplomats and observers in reporting that China’s envoys to COP31 stuck to the country’s “accustomed low-key playbook”.  The Financial Times reported that China used the climate talks to “complain about tariffs on EVs and green energy products”.  On the final day of the summit, the Guardian said that China was among the parties that “did not object to the deal”.  Bloomberg also reported that while Chinese diplomats maintained a “relatively low profile”, its “world-leading” companies featured in China pavilion events.  Bloomberg continued: “At a United Nations climate conference that was low on delivery and high on dysfunction, China’s clean-technology companies showed that some aspects of the green transition are persevering despite geopolitical tensions.” What does this mean for the consensus process and reform?  In the aftermath of COP31, many commentators have called for a reform of the COP process. The European Commission is “drawing up plans to overhaul the UN climate summit process, warning that the current negotiating system risks becoming ineffective because a single country can block an agreement among nearly 200 parties”, according to Euronews .  Many other commentators shared the view that the COP process must be reformed. Marco Lambertini, convenor of the Nature Positive Initiative, said in Reuters : “We must be clear: reform remains essential. COPs are cumbersome, expensive, bureaucratic, environmentally unfriendly and frustratingly slow. The consensus rule – adopted in the climate and nature conferences – allows a handful of countries to dilute ambition in the main plenary deliberations. Too often, fossil fuel and agrochemical lobbies interfere with negotiations and obstruct progress. This must change.” Similarly, York University’s Kapoor said in Al Jazeera that the current system results in “an international forum in which the most reluctant participants can limit what everyone else is allowed to say, let alone do”.  The Associated Press ’ Prengaman wrote that “reforms floated over the years include shortening the conference from its current two weeks, limiting it just to delegates and reducing its overall size”. The Independent ’s climate correspondent, Nick Ferris, said the “collapse” of the talks “represents a shocking nadir in the history of COPs”, adding that “the process requires urgent reform”.  Similarly, Pilita Clark, the Financial Times associate editor and business columnist, said “the disaster that was the climate gathering in Antalya should prompt overdue reform”.  Justin Worland, a senior correspondent at Time , likened this year’s summit to the 2009 COP in Copenhagen. He added: “Following the defeat, negotiators went back to the drawing board and created the architecture that led to the Paris Agreement. Today, there’s another opportunity for reinvention.” (For more on COP reform, see Carbon Brief ’s interviews with 16 experts on the topic.) Could COP31 send a ‘positive signal’?  While many editorials lamented the failure of COP31 to agree on the Antalya pact, there were various articles that highlighted a more positive view.  In the Guardian , Dr Bill Hare , chief executive of Climate Analytics , wrote that COP31 was “a line in the sand moment, a victory for multilateralism as countries stood up to the big fossil fuel producers and said no”. He continued:  “The [cover decision that parties] rejected barely recognised the catastrophic climate emergency we’re facing, let alone signalled a definitive move away from fossil fuels.” Others shared the view that numerous countries rejecting the cover decision due to its failure to mention fossil fuels could be seen as a significant moment of pushback. In an interview in Le Monde , Prof Johan Rockström , director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany, said that it is “better to have this kind of crisis and to do something good with it, rather than having a watered-down agreement”. He added:  “It will have a very positive signal: It means that the world is taking risks seriously. The world is taking science seriously.” An editorial in Bloomberg stated that COP31 should “serve as a call for action”, pushing like-minded governments to continue working together to make progress. It added:  “The outcome at COP31, discouraging as it was, strongly suggests that much of the world remains committed to fighting climate change. More than 100 governments, led by the EU, opposed a final declaration that – amid pressure from Russia, Saudi Arabia and other fossil-fuel producers – omitted any reference to the transition away from fossil fuels.”  In Reuters , columnist Antony Currie wrote that the failure to adopt the cover decision could in fact be “healthy”. Elsewhere, in Inside Story , the University of Sheffield’s Jacobs argued that “this COP’s failure might have been what the world needed”.  Related ‘Sinking’ African megacities will expose seven million people to flooding by 2050 27.11.2026 Rainfall and flooding CB Live: Carbon Brief journalists discuss key COP31 outcomes 24.11.2026 COP31 Antalya COP31: Key outcomes for food, forests, oceans and nature at the UN climate talks in Antalya 24.11.2026 COP31 Antalya COP31: Key outcomes agreed at the UN climate talks in Antalya 23.11.2026 COP31 Antalya The post Media reaction: Who is to blame for COP31 ‘failure’? appeared first on Carbon Brief .

summary: 澳大利亚悉尼——陆军对话是一个定期举行的论坛，使参与国能够协调竞选工作、讨论行动优先事项并寻找加强合作的机会。该论坛包括高级领导人参与活动和工作组，以推动整个印太地区的陆军活动。太平洋陆军在悉尼举行的陆军对话技术工作组期间加强合作 来自澳大利亚、美国、日本和菲律宾的高级领导人和代表团成员出席了破冰活动
content:
澳大利亚悉尼——

陆军对话是一个定期举行的论坛，使参与国能够协调战役工作、讨论行动优先事项并确定加强合作的机会。该论坛包括高级领导人参与活动和工作组，以推动整个印太地区的陆军活动。

太平洋陆军在悉尼举行的陆军对话技术工作组期间加强合作 摄影：CPL Hamid Farahani

2026 年 11 月 17 日，陆军对话 - 技术工作组期间，来自澳大利亚、美国、日本和菲律宾的高级领导人和代表团成员出席了在悉尼维多利亚军营军官食堂举行的破冰活动。*** 本地字幕 *** 参加陆军对话 - 技术工作组的高级军事领导人和代表在正式讨论之前出席了在悉尼维多利亚军营举行的破冰活动。该活动为来自澳大利亚、美国、日本和菲律宾的代表提供了建立专业关系并讨论共同安全利益的机会。陆军对话-技术工作组是参与陆军的一个重要论坛，旨在加强合作并改善整个印太地区未来行动、活动和投资的同步性。
澳大利亚陆军主办了为期四天的论坛，汇聚了代表四个盟国和伙伴国的六个军种的人员：澳大利亚陆军、日本陆上自卫队、菲律宾陆军、菲律宾海军陆战队、美国太平洋海军陆战队和美国太平洋陆军。与会者的重点是在 2027 年及以后调整战略态势、提高作战持久力以及增强多边地面力量能力。

> “我们通过陆军对话等论坛建立的关系增强了我们在最重要的时候共同行动的能力，”

美国太平洋海军陆战队副司令马修·T·莫厄里少将说道。

> “将四个国家和六个军种聚集在一起，使我们能够更好地调整优先事项，提高互操作性，并在共同计划下作为一支统一的力量开展行动。这种合作加强了我们的集体准备，并加强了我们对自由开放的印太地区的承诺。”

太平洋陆军在悉尼举行的陆军对话技术工作组期间加强合作 摄影：CPL Hamid Farahani
2026 年 11 月 17 日，陆军对话 - 技术工作组期间，来自澳大利亚、美国、日本和菲律宾的高级领导人和代表团成员出席了在悉尼维多利亚军营军官食堂举行的破冰活动。*** 本地字幕 *** 参加陆军对话 - 技术工作组的高级军事领导人和代表在正式讨论之前出席了在悉尼维多利亚军营举行的破冰活动。该活动为来自澳大利亚、美国、日本和菲律宾的代表提供了建立专业关系并讨论共同安全利益的机会。陆军对话-技术工作组是参与陆军的一个重要论坛，旨在加强合作并改善整个印太地区未来行动、活动和投资的同步性。

陆军对话为持续参与共同问题提供了一个论坛

【原文 English Original】
SYDNEY, Australia --

Land Forces Dialogue is a recurring forum that enables participating nations to coordinate campaign efforts, discuss operational priorities and identify opportunities to enhance cooperation. The forum includes senior leader engagements and working groups that advance land force activities across the Indo-Pacific.

Pacific Land Forces Strengthen Cooperation During Land Forces Dialogue Technical Working Group in Sydney Photo by CPL Hamid Farahani

Senior leaders and delegation members from Australia, the United States, Japan and the Philippines attend an ice-breaker function at the Victoria Barracks Officers' Mess, Sydney, during the Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group on 17 November 2026. *** Local Caption *** Senior military leaders and delegates participating in the Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group attended an ice-breaker function at Victoria Barracks, Sydney, ahead of formal discussions. The function provided an opportunity for delegates from Australia, the United States, Japan and the Philippines to build professional relationships and discuss shared security interests. The Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group serves as a key forum for participating land forces to strengthen cooperation and improve synchronisation of future operations, activities and investments throughout the Indo-Pacific region.

The Australian Army hosted the four-day forum, which brought together personnel from six military services representing four allied and partner nations: the Australian Army, Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, Philippine Army, Philippine Marine Corps, U.S. Marine Corps Forces Pacific, and U.S. Army Pacific. Participants focused on aligning strategic posture, improving operational endurance, and enhancing multilateral land power capabilities through calendar year 2027 and beyond.

> “The relationships we build through forums like the Land Forces Dialogue strengthen our ability to operate together when it matters most,”

said Maj. Gen. Matthew T. Mowery, deputy commander, U.S. Marine Corps Forces, Pacific.

> “Bringing together four nations and six military services allows us to better align priorities, improve interoperability and campaign as a unified force under a shared plan. That cooperation strengthens our collective readiness and reinforces our commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific.”

Pacific Land Forces Strengthen Cooperation During Land Forces Dialogue Technical Working Group in Sydney Photo by CPL Hamid Farahani

Senior leaders and delegation members from Australia, the United States, Japan and the Philippines attend an ice-breaker function at the Victoria Barracks Officers' Mess, Sydney, during the Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group on 17 November 2026. *** Local Caption *** Senior military leaders and delegates participating in the Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group attended an ice-breaker function at Victoria Barracks, Sydney, ahead of formal discussions. The function provided an opportunity for delegates from Australia, the United States, Japan and the Philippines to build professional relationships and discuss shared security interests. The Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group serves as a key forum for participating land forces to strengthen cooperation and improve synchronisation of future operations, activities and investments throughout the Indo-Pacific region.

The Land Forces Dialogue provides a forum for sustained engagement on shared military priorities. The dialogue enables participating nations to coordinate campaign activities, align operational priorities and identify opportunities for future cooperation.

Participants reaffirmed their commitment to synchronize multilateral training objectives, increase operational effectiveness and enhance crisis-response capabilities. By building on established relationships and routine multinational training opportunities, the four nations continue to advance practical military cooperation and strengthen their ability to respond to shared security challenges.

The United States International Trade Commission.
Request for comments regarding International Trade Commission's Economic Analysis, Investigation No. MISC-054.
Pursuant to Section 332 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the United States International Trade Commission (Commission) is seeking information from the public on its economic analysis, including its methodology and areas of focus.
To ensure consideration, written comments must be submitted on or before March 25, 2027.
Lisa R. Barton, Secretary to the Commission, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436, telephone 202-205-2595. General information concerning the Commission may be obtained by accessing its internet server at https://www.usitc.gov. Hearing-impaired persons are advised that information can be obtained by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal on (202) 205-1810.
You may submit comments, identified by docket number MISC-054, by any of the following methods:
Agency Website: https://www.usitc.gov. You may submit comments on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov. For help accessing EDIS, please email EDIS3Help@usitc.gov.
Email: Submit comments via to Secretary@usitc.gov. Include docket ( printed page 76266) number MISC-054 in the subject line of the message. Comments submitted by email must be: in letter format and double-spaced (unless the document is less than two (2) pages); in portable document format (PDF); and signed with either a typed or written signature. All comments received will be posted without change to the agency's public record, including any personal information provided.
Instructions: All submissions received must include the agency name and docket number (MISC-054, along with written comments addressing the topics on which the USITC seeks information. All comments received will be posted without change to https://www.usitc.gov, including any personal information provided. Written comments filed on EDIS must conform to the provisions of section 201.8 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.8).
Docket: For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to https://www.usitc.gov and/or the U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Room 112, Washington, DC 20436.
Jennifer Andberg, Office of External Relations ((202) 205-3404, or Jennifer.Andberg@usitc.gov). Hearing-impaired individuals may obtain information on this matter by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal at 202-205-1810. General information about the Commission is available by accessing the Commission website at www.usitc.gov. Persons with mobility impairments who will need special assistance in gaining access to the Commission should contact the Office of the Secretary at (202) 205-2000.
1. Relevant Statutory Authorities
Pursuant to section 332 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1332 (“section 332”)), whenever requested, the Commission submits to the President, and, by delegation, the United States Trade Representative (USTR); the Senate Finance Committee (SFC); or the House Ways and Means Committee (HWM) information and analysis on any matter related to tariffs, international trade, and industry competitiveness. Additionally, the President or Congress can task the Commission with factfinding investigations on various topics, which the Commission can also institute on its own initiative. Other statutes such as section 131 of the Trade Act of 1974 and statutes for specific trade agreements also provide authority to conduct factfinding investigations.
The Commission's work under section 332 and these other authorities utilize some degree of economic analysis. In such investigations, the Commission often analyzes the ways that trade and trade policy affect U.S. workers, producers, consumers, and the U.S. economy as a whole. The analysis helps inform policymakers' decisions on trade policy and international trade negotiations. In conjunction with other factfinding tools such as public hearings and written submissions, the Commission often uses analytical approaches including quantitative models, which are simplified, mathematical representations of an economy or industry using certain real-world data, to help isolate—and thereby understand—the impact of a past or future change when many factors could affect the outcomes.
To ensure that the Commission can meet the challenges posed by changing global and economic circumstances that are highly relevant to trade, it has decided to evaluate on an ongoing basis its analytical tools, data sources, and methodologies to ensure its work remains accurate, relevant, and responsive to its stakeholders.
2. Commission Analytical Approaches and How They Are Used
Given the variety of topics the Commission is obligated to analyze, the Commission uses a variety of analytical techniques, which can be combined to suit the topic(s) to be examined, including qualitative analysis, quantitative analysis without modeling, and quantitative analysis with economic modeling, which, as mentioned, can help assess the impact of a policy change by filtering out other factors, with important caveats.
The Commission's models vary by technique and scope. Major simulation models are built at the level of an industry or the entire economy. At the economy-wide level, the main modeling approach at the Commission has historically been the computable general equilibrium (CGE) model, based on the Global Trade Analysis Project (GTAP) database. This approach has been deployed numerous times in both factfinding investigations, such as in the evaluation of the likely impact of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) that the Commission published in 2019 (Inv. No. TPA-105-003, U.S.-Mexico-Canada Trade Agreement: Likely Impact on the U.S. Economy and on Specific Industry Sectors). Meanwhile, industry-level partial equilibrium models focus on a single economic sector without modeling the interactions between economic sectors, such as in the Commission's regular assessments of the USMCA automotive rules of origin (Inv. No. 332-600, USMCA Automotive Rules of Origin: Economic Impact and Operation, 2025 Report).
Although less frequently deployed in factfinding investigations as stand-alone models, econometric models have been used, for example, to measure the extent of “pass-through” from tariffs to U.S. prices in the Commission's analysis of the impact of the tariffs imposed in 2023 under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 (Inv. No. 332-591, Economic Impact of Section 232 and 301 Tariffs on U.S. Industries). More recently, in place of a CGE model, the Commission used an econometric “gravity” equation as part of a general equilibrium gravity model in a 2026 study on the impact of revoking China's permanent normal trade relations status (Inv. No. 330-609, Effects on the U.S. Economy of Revoking China's Permanent Normal Trade Relations Status).
In addition to the above trade models that have generally been focused on medium- and long-run outcomes, such as by assuming the entire U.S. labor force is employed and can move freely across sectors, the Commission is considering how to develop and deploy economic models that are more equipped to look at short-term outcomes before employment, wages and other aspects of the economy fully adjust to any policy change.
Because models cannot capture every feature of the real world, they necessarily rely on assumptions and simplifications. Different modeling approaches may also emphasize different channels through which policies affect economic outcomes. Economy-wide simulation models, such as CGE models, have been subject to criticism regarding certain assumptions, including assumptions about full employment and worker mobility across sectors, particularly when used to analyze the effects of trade policy changes.
II. Topics on Which USITC Seeks Information
The Commission seeks information from the public on any of the following topics. After the comment period concludes, the Commission intends to produce a report that includes a summary of comments. The comments will also inform how the Commission moves forward with its factfinding Section 332 and related responsibilities. ( printed page 76267)
1. Do you think the Commission currently has the right analytical tools, including economic models, to address major trade policy questions over the next 5-10 years? Why or why not?
a. What non-modeling approaches should the Commission's analytical toolkit include?
b. What is the full suite of models ( e.g., industry-specific versus economy-wide; short-term versus long-term) that the Commission should have available for use in its analysis?
2. What factors or topics should the Commission's economic analysis be able to consider? Would they include, but not be limited to, the following:
a. Effect of trade on labor markets
i. Short-term effect on workers
ii. Long-term effect on workers ( e.g., changes in workforce capacity or skill sets in certain industries)
iii. Effect on the quality of jobs available for workers, including any shifts in wages, benefits, or job security
b. Effect of trade on investment
c. Effect of hostile trade actions, including boycotts, export controls, or other trade sanctions placed on the United States or U.S. persons
d. Effect of trade on distribution of wealth/income within the United States, including across geographic regions and demographic groups
e. Effect of trade on the environment
f. Effect of trade on immigration
g. Interaction of trade policy with domestic policies and regulations ( e.g. intellectual property, environmental regulations, labor regulations, tax policy, immigration policy)
h. Interaction of trade with domestic and international protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights
i. Interaction with trade imbalances
j. Interaction with market concentration
k. Other topics you believe would be useful for the Commission to consider
3. Given the Commission's statutory obligations, which of the above topics should the Commission prioritize?
4. Please discuss what trade questions are well suited to modeling, and which are better served by a different sort of analysis, such as descriptive trend analysis, legal analysis, or other analytical approaches.
5. How effective have the Commission's models been at evaluating the effects of major trade policy changes in past years? Please reference specific examples.
6. How can the Commission best engage in quality control of its modeling prospectively and evaluate the accuracy of its modeling retrospectively? Should the Commission regularly and publicly undertake model validation to evaluate the accuracy of its models?
7. Are there existing alternatives to Commission models that are more accurate, or that would capture factors that the Commission should consider? What trade-offs, if any, might such other models have?
8. Are there other branches of economics or disciplines outside of economics that might be useful in helping the Commission improve its modeling and other analytical techniques? Please provide specific examples of techniques, papers, authors, or other details to help the Commission identify these items.
9. How can the Commission incorporate or improve any of the following practices, and are there examples of best practices from a Commission report or external report:
a. Sensitivity analysis to test the importance of assumptions on model outcomes
b. Indications as to the level of certainty of model estimates
c. Plain narrative explanation and data visualization
d. Transparency of model assumptions and limitations
e. Replicability of model releases
10. Should the Commission attempt to quantify the impact of nontariff measures (NTMs) on trade? If quantification is appropriate, how should this be conducted? How should the Commission account for the potential non-trade-related impacts of NTMs ( e.g., on public health and the environment)?
11. What datasets should be created, refined, or expanded upon for the Commission's use on understanding the effects of trade policy?
12. How can the Commission make the best use of AI tools for quantitative analysis?
13. Are there any ways in which the Commission's information-gathering techniques such as public hearings, field visits, written submission periods, or surveys can be improved?
14. From whom ( e.g., the public and/or technical experts) should the Commission receive input regarding its analytical approaches, and with what frequency and in what manner should the Commission solicit such input? Would the Commission benefit from establishing a public advisory council for economic modeling?
15. Anything else that the submitter believes would help the Commission improve its modeling.
III. Submission Instructions
Written submissions: Interested persons are invited to file written submissions and other information concerning the matters to be addressed in this request. All written submissions should be addressed to the Secretary, and should be received no later than 5:15 p.m., March 25, 2027. All written submissions must conform to the provisions of section 201.8 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.8). Filings must be made through the Commission's Electronic Document Information System (EDIS, https://edis.usitc.gov) or via email. Persons with questions regarding electronic filing should contact the Office of the Secretary, Docket Services Division (202-205-1802), email EDIS3help@usitc.gov, or consult the Commission's Handbook on Filing Procedures.
Any submissions that contain confidential business information (CBI) must also conform with the requirements in section 201.6 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.6). Section 201.6 of the rules requires that the cover of the document and the individual pages be clearly marked as to whether they are the “confidential” or “nonconfidential” version, and that the CBI is clearly identified by means of brackets. All written submissions, except for CBI, will be made available for inspection by interested persons.
All information, including CBI, submitted may be disclosed to and used: (i) by the Commission, its employees and Offices, and contract personnel (a) for developing or maintaining the records of this or a related proceeding, or (b) in internal investigations, audits, reviews, and evaluations relating to the programs, personnel, and operations of the Commission including under 5 U.S.C. Appendix 3; or (ii) by U.S. government employees and contract personnel for cybersecurity or other security purposes. The Commission will not otherwise disclose any CBI in a manner that would reveal the operations of the firm supplying the information.
By order of the Commission.
Issued: November 23, 2026.
Secretary to the Commission.

美国以产能过剩为由对中国和欧盟征收新关税
资料照片：中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于 2026 年 5 月 14 日参观北京天坛。BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/Pool via REUTERS/资料照片
美国以产能过剩为由对中国和欧盟征收新关税
作者：艾丽西亚·迪亚兹（彭博社）——在唐纳德·特朗普总统推动恢复全面的全球进口税的推动下，美国宣布计划对来自中国、欧盟和其他十几个经济体的商品征收新一轮关税，最高法院认为这些关税违宪。
根据美国高级官员的说法，根据中国之前与特朗普政府达成的协议，从中国的进口税率将升至 20%，不过，如果两国谈判破裂，这一税率可能会翻一番，达到 40%。在周三宣布这一消息之前，这位不愿透露姓名的官员向记者做了简报。
根据美国贸易代表办公室的说法，根据美国与欧盟的协议，来自欧盟的产品将被征收 15% 的税，不过税率也可能升至 20%。
关税将适用于特朗普政府指责某些国内行业生产过剩并损害美国公司利益的经济体的产品。它们仍需接受公众意见征询，并且可能会发生变化。这位官员表示，最终行动最早可能在一月份采取。
新的征税措施标志着政府为恢复广泛的关税议程而做出的最新努力，其中包括利用紧急权力实施的逐国征税。今年二月，这些提议被高等法院法官否决，迫使特朗普援引其他法律权威来推进他的议程。
这是一个具有政治风险的举动。民主党在本月早些时候的中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，部分原因是选民对生活成本的愤怒以及对总统处理经济的不满。
中国和欧盟也可能进行报复，尽管它们最初发出的信号比较平静。
中国外交部发言人郭家琨周三早些时候在新闻发布会上表示，美国对其出口产品征收新关税的前景是“政治操纵”，并表示两国应共同努力维持贸易休战。
该公告似乎符合美国和欧盟之间的 2025 年贸易协定，该协定将欧盟大部分出口产品的关税上限限制在 15%。因此，此举目前可能不会激怒跨大西洋关系。欧盟委员会发言人奥洛夫·吉尔表示，“我们强烈反对欧洲是结构性产能过剩根源的前提”，并补充说欧盟预计新征税将遵守关税协议。
美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔表示，新关税旨在保护现有交易，同时解决产能过剩问题。
格里尔周三在 CNBC 上表示：“我们达成的许多交易实际上解决了我们在产能过剩方面看到的很多问题，或者可以解决这个问题。” “我们已经与我们的贸易伙伴讨论了这个问题。他们知道我们的提议。我认为其中很多内容都是经过深思熟虑的。”
来自日本、韩国、瑞士——所有美国主要贸易伙伴——的进口将受到 15% 的关税打击。美国贸易代表办公室表示，韩国的这一数字可能高达 25%，其他两个国家的这一数字可能高达 20%。如果与华盛顿的贸易协定最终确定，印度产品将面临 17% 的关税，不过这一税率可能会增加到 25%。
亚洲几个较小的国家也受到打击。针对墨西哥和挪威的类似预期措施并未包括在内

U.S. Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
FILE PHOTO: China's President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump visit the Temple of Heaven in Beijing on May 14, 2026. BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/Pool via REUTERS/File Photo
U.S. Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
By Alicia Diaz (Bloomberg) –The US announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional.
The rate for imports from China would rise to 20%, in line with the country’s prior agreement with the Trump administration — though that rate could double to 40% if talks between the two countries fall apart, according to a senior US official. The official briefed reporters on condition of anonymity ahead of Wednesday’s announcement.
Products from the EU will be taxed at 15% in compliance with the US’s deal with the bloc, though that could also rise to as much as 20%, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative.
Tariffs will apply to items from economies the Trump administration accuses of overproduction in some domestic industries and hurting American companies. They are still subject to a public comment process and could change. A final action could come as early as January, the official said.
The new levies mark the latest effort by the administration to reinstate an expansive tariff agenda that included country-by-country levies implemented using emergency powers. Those were struck down by high-court justices in February, forcing Trump to invoke other legal authorities to advance his agenda.
It’s a politically risky move. Democrats swept to a landslide victory in the midterm elections earlier this month thanks in part to voter anger over the cost of living and disapproval of the president’s handling of the economy.
China and the EU could also retaliate, though initial signals from them were muted.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a briefing earlier Wednesday that the prospect of new US tariffs on its exports was “political maneuvering” and said the two nations should work together to maintain their trade truce.
The announcement appears to comply with the 2025 trade agreement between the US and EU, which capped tariffs at 15% on most of the bloc’s exports. As a result, the move likely won’t antagonize transatlantic relations for now. European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said “we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity” and added the bloc expects new levies to abide by the tariff agreement.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the new duties were designed to preserve existing deals while addressing overcapacity concerns.
“A lot of these deals we made actually solve a lot of the problems we see in excess capacity or can go toward it,” Greer said Wednesday on CNBC. “We’ve talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we’re proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in.”
Imports from Japan, South Korea, Switzerland — all prominent US trading partners — would be hit with a 15% rate. The number could go up to 25% for Korea and 20% for the other two, USTR said. Indian products would face a 17% charge if a trade pact with Washington is finalized, though that could increase to 25%.
Several smaller nations in Asia were also hit. Similar expected measures aimed at Mexico and Norway were not included but remain under consideration, the official said. Greer said on CNBC the US has “had some very good conversations with Mexico” on the issue.
The tariffs follow a probe that began in March into alleged excess manufacturing capacity, utilizing Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a process seen as more resistant to legal challenges than Trump’s prior tariff wall. The tariff rates aren’t expected to surpass already agreed-upon levels in trade agreements with each economy.
The move will test the tolerance of economic partners, who have largely held back from retaliating, opting instead to negotiate deals with the US to minimize their tariffs. That dynamic could be on display next month, when Trump meets again with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Group of 20 summit. Their trade truce is set to expire in January unless the two powers agree to extend it.
“If we were to go beyond the 20% or something like that, they would view that as breaking our deal,” Greer said,
The trade ambassador said Washington and Beijing are also “proposing to implement” tariff reductions under its new board of trade on around $30 billion of non-sensitive exports.
Greer signaled that the new levy will not stack on top of existing duties of 10% or 12.5% under a separate investigation into negligent enforcement of forced-labor laws. “Those are not really additive,” he said on CNBC.
For products eligible to be hit by both sets of duties, only the higher rate would apply, the official said earlier.
The official added that there would be goods exempted from the tariffs, including oil and gas and food products that cannot be grown in the US. Other products that are already subject to sectoral duties, including tariffs on pharmaceuticals and critical minerals, are also exempted.
After the Supreme Court loss, Trump immediately announced plans to rebuild his tariff wall under a different legal authority. Under the Section 301 framework, the president can implement tariffs following an investigation into allegedly unfair foreign trading practices.
While Section 301 tariffs are seen as more legally sound and flexible than other powers Trump has eyed, they’re also more time-consuming. An earlier investigation under the same legal authority into policies around forced labor from US trading partners resulted in tariffs on some 60 economies. Those duties are currently facing legal challenges.
The new tariffs apply to Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.
USTR also announced it is raising tariffs on imports from Brazil, altering a previously-conducted trade investigation into the country’s digital policies and trade practices. The US is considering increasing the out-of-quota tariff rate on raw and refined sugar and proposing a 10% tariff on finished aircraft.
The increased levy on imports from Brazil comes weeks after Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro lost his presidential election bid to progressive incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

summary: 中国周四谴责澳大利亚和菲律宾之间的一项防务协议，称该协议将“加剧该地区的紧张局势”，该地区存在相互竞争的领土主张，并誓言“捍卫”其权利。菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗 (Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.) 和澳大利亚副总理兼国防部长理查德·马勒斯 (Richard Marles) 于 2025 年 8 月举行联合演习。照片：菲律宾武装部队﻿。澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞本月访问菲律宾首都期间，堪培拉和马尼拉之间达成的协议更新了数十年来的协议
content:
中国周四谴责澳大利亚和菲律宾之间的一项防务协议，称该协议将“加剧该地区的紧张局势”，该地区存在相互竞争的领土主张，并誓言“捍卫”其权利。菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗 (Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.) 和澳大利亚副总理兼国防部长理查德·马勒斯 (Richard Marles) 于 2025 年 8 月举行联合演习。照片：菲律宾武装部队﻿。堪培拉和马尼拉之间的协议是澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞本月访问菲律宾首都期间达成的，更新了长达数十年的备忘录。近年来，两国稳步加强防务合作，包括在具有重要战略意义的南海进行联合海上巡逻。尽管国际裁决认为北京的主张没有法律依据，但北京对南海的大部分地区拥有主权。美国的盟友菲律宾多年来一直因该航道争议地区与中国发生对抗。另请参阅：中国“爱好和平”，但与菲律宾的对抗可以“轻松取胜”——中国国防部发言人陈曦在周四的新闻发布会上被问及该协议时表示，“菲律宾某些政客出于一己私利，散布对中国的虚假言论，不断进行挑衅、滋事”。
他说，这些人“试图争取域外势力的支持，为自己壮胆，在南海制造事端”。 2019年5月14日，美国海岸警卫队快艇贝索夫号（左）与菲律宾海岸警卫队船只“八打雁”号（中）和“卡朗加曼”号在南海举行演习。照片：美国海岸警卫队，来自 Flickr。 “这只会加剧紧张局势并破坏地区稳定。”陈警告说，如果面临侵犯或挑衅，中国将“采取必要措施坚决回应”，以“坚决挫败任何使南海陷入混乱的企图”。堪培拉表示，澳大利亚和菲律宾之间的防务协议涉及加强海上活动、信息共享和国防基础设施发展等关键要素。

【原文 English Original】
China denounced a defence pact between Australia and the Philippines on Thursday, arguing it would “exacerbate tensions” in a region crisscrossed by competing territorial claims and vowing to “safeguard” its rights. Philippine National Defense Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr. and Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Richard Marles during joint exercises in August 2025. Photo: Armed Forces of the Philippines﻿. The agreement between Canberra and Manila, struck this month during a visit to the Philippine capital by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, updates a decades-old memorandum. The countries have steadily increased defence cooperation in recent years, including joint maritime patrols in the strategically vital South China Sea. Beijing claims most of the South China Sea despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis. US ally the Philippines has been engaged in years of confrontations with China over disputed areas of the waterway. See also: China ‘loves peace’ but could ‘easily win’ confrontation with Philippines – ambassador “Certain Philippine politicians, driven by their selfish interests, are spreading false narratives about China, constantly engaging in provocations and stirring up trouble,” Chinese defence ministry spokesman Chen Xi told a news conference on Thursday when asked about the deal. Those individuals are “attempting to enlist the backing of forces from outside the region to embolden themselves and create disturbances in the South China Sea”, he said. The US Coast Guard Cutter Bertholf (left) moves in formation with the Philippine Coast Guard vessels Batangas (centre) and Kalanggaman during an exercise on May 14, 2019, in the South China Sea. Photo: US Coast Guard, via Flickr. “This will only exacerbate tensions and undermine regional stability.” If faced with infringements or provocations, China will “take necessary measures to respond firmly”, Chen warned, in order to “resolutely thwart any attempts to plunge the South China Sea into chaos”. The defence deal between Australia and the Philippines involves enhanced maritime activities, sharing of information and defence infrastructure development as key elements, according to Canberra.

title: Ex-lawmaker William Wong sentenced to 120 hours of community service, fined HK$6k over drink-driving crash
zh_title: 前立法会议员黄威廉因酒后驾驶撞车被判120小时社区服务及罚款港币6,000元
summary: 前立法会议员黄威廉在承认酒后驾驶和其他三项交通违法行为后，被判处 120 小时社区服务，并罚款 6,000 港元。香港立法会议员黄威廉出席 2026 年 7 月 1 日庆祝回归周年纪念仪式。照片：黄威廉，来自 Facebook。据当地媒体报道，黄周四上午在沙田裁判法院受审。考虑到黄先生早年对酒后驾驶认罪，而且他之前的酒后驾驶罪行发生在十多年前，裁判官判处他
content:
前立法会议员黄威廉在承认酒后驾驶和其他三项交通违法行为后，被判处 120 小时社区服务，并罚款 6,000 港元。香港立法会议员黄威廉出席 2026 年 7 月 1 日庆祝回归周年纪念仪式。照片：黄威廉，来自 Facebook。据当地媒体报道，黄周四上午在沙田裁判法院受审。考虑到黄先生早年承认酒驾罪名，而且他之前酒后驾车的罪行发生在十多年前，裁判官判处他120小时社区服务，并取消他一年的驾驶资格。黄先生还被勒令在取消资格期的最后三个月内自费参加驾驶改进课程。黄先生还承认了另外三项指控：粗心驾驶、事故后未停车以及未报告事故，每项罪名被罚款港币2,000元。这位66岁的时任立法会议员因涉嫌酒后驾驶和其他三项与7月份在香港中文大学（中大）校园发生的车祸有关的罪行而被捕。警方称，黄某当晚撞倒了中大宿舍外停放的两辆汽车。事故发生后，他离开了现场，但后来返回接受调查，期间他未能通过酒精测试。
黄先生曾任香港中文大学工程学教授、沙田裁判法院系统工程与工程管理学系副院长。照片：Peter Lee/HKFP。被捕后，他辞去了立法会议员和中大的职务，为给社会带来“麻烦”而道歉。黄先生于2022年通过补选当选立法会议员，填补立法机构的四个空缺。此次补选是小圈投票，只有由政治精英组成的选举委员会成员才能投票。他在 2025 年立法会选举中再次当选。在香港，酒后驾驶最高可被罚款 25,000 港元和监禁三年。

【原文 English Original】
Former lawmaker William Wong has been sentenced to 120 hours of community service and fined HK$6,000 after he pleaded guilty to drink driving and three other traffic offences. Hong Kong lawmaker William Wong attends a ceremony to celebrate the handover anniversary on July 1, 2026. Photo: William Wong, via Facebook. Wong appeared at Shatin Magistrates’ Courts on Thursday morning for sentencing, local media reported . Taking into account Wong’s early guilty plea to drink driving and the fact that his previous drink-driving offence took place more than a decade ago, the magistrate sentenced him to 120 hours of community service and disqualified him from driving for one year. Wong was also ordered to attend a driving improvement course at his own expense during the final three months of the disqualification period. Wong also pleaded guilty to three other charges: careless driving, failing to stop after an accident, and failing to report an accident, for which he was fined HK$2,000 each. The 66-year-old, then a legislator, was arrested on suspicion of drink driving and three other offences linked to a car accident on the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) campus in July. Police said Wong hit two parked cars outside a CUHK residential hall that evening. He left the scene after the accident but later returned for an investigation, during which he failed a breathalyser test. Wong was an engineering professor at CUHK and associate dean of the Department of Systems Engineering and Engineering Management. Shatin Magistrates’ Courts. Photo: Peter Lee/HKFP. He resigned from the Legislative Council and his job at CUHK after the arrest, apologising for bringing “trouble” to society. Wong was elected to the Legislative Council in 2022 via a by-election to fill four vacancies in the lawmaking body. The by-election was a small-circle vote in which only members of the Election Committee, a body composed of political elites, could vote. He was re-elected during the Legislative Council elections in 2025. In Hong Kong, drink driving carries a maximum penalty of a HK$25,000 fine and three years in prison.

title: In Pictures: Hundreds gather for Catholic memorial mass on eve of Tai Po fire’s first anniversary
zh_title: 图片中：大埔火灾一周年前夕，数百人聚集参加天主教纪念弥撒
summary: 去年大埔致命火灾一周年纪念日前夕，数百人聚集在一起举行天主教弥撒，一名神父称这次仪式是与幸存者的陪伴，并宣读了 168 名遇难者的名字以示悼念。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。天主教香港教区周三晚上在中环圣母无染原罪主教座堂举行了追悼弥撒，有200多名死者家属参加。所有168名遇难者的名字都被展示在了现场
content:
去年大埔致命火灾一周年纪念日前夕，数百人聚集在一起举行天主教弥撒，一名神父称这次仪式是与幸存者的陪伴，并宣读了 168 名遇难者的名字以示悼念。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。天主教香港教区周三晚上在中环圣母无染原罪主教座堂举行了追悼弥撒，有200多名死者家属参加。所有 168 名遇难者的名字都陈列在圣所的中央，下面还放着一些遇难者的肖像。他们的名字也印在数字礼拜仪式小册子上。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。主持仪式的陈华明神父在讲道中表示，这场致命的大火是一次集体创伤，幸存者、他们的家人和公众都遭受了巨大的痛苦和悲伤。陈用粤语说：“追悼会聚集了分散的、独自悲伤的人们，让他们意识到他们并不孤单面对这一切。” 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
他还将这场悲剧描述为源于“人为错误和系统性故障”，这与一个独立委员会的调查结果相呼应，该调查将装修承包商和项目顾问列为“罪魁祸首”，并强调了政府监管的失误。“这项服务提醒我们，人的生命不是可随意处置的数字，而是来自上帝的珍贵礼物，”他说。 “这种对生命的坚韧应该转化为对真理和正义的追求。” 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港福音派信义会钻石堂牧师林珍妮在火灾中失去了三名亲戚，她也在弥撒中发表了讲话，当天恰逢她一位已故亲戚的生日。 “但我不能再亲自祝他们生日快乐了，”她用粤语说。林郑月娥表示，过去的一年对死者家属来说充满了挑战，并列举了葬礼安排方面的繁重行政职责以及悲剧造成的情感损失。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。她说，虽然时间并没有减轻痛苦，但她祈祷家人能够过上好日子，并保留对亲人的记忆。她补充说，这并不意味着忘记受害者，而是从创伤中治愈，同时为悲伤留出空间。
四名失去亲人的幸存者大声朗读了 168 名遇难者的名字，最后是在与大火搏斗中牺牲的消防员何伟豪。2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒悼念大埔火灾遇难者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾受害者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。宏福苑宏新楼居民大聪在葬礼结束后告诉记者，当受害者的名字被大声念出来时，她感到很安慰，并补充说，死者家属承受着无法用言语形容的痛苦。在大火中失去母亲的菲利斯·罗(Phyllis Lo)表示，当她听到母亲的名字时，她感到很平静，并想象着其他受害者的名字被读出时的生活。 2026 年 11 月 25 日，一场天主教弥撒纪念大埔火灾遇难者。

【原文 English Original】
Hundreds gathered on the eve of the first anniversary of last year’s deadly Tai Po fire for a Catholic mass, where a priest described the service as an act of companionship with survivors and the names of the 168 people who perished were read out in tribute. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Catholic Diocese of Hong Kong held the memorial mass on Wednesday evening at the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception in Central, with members of bereaved families among more than 200 attendees. The names of all 168 victims were displayed at the centre of the sanctuary, with portraits of some placed underneath. Their names were also printed in digital liturgy booklets. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Father Dominic Chan, who presided over the service, said during his homily that the deadly blaze was a collective trauma, and that survivors, their families and members of the public all suffered immense pain and grief. “The memorial mass brings together scattered people who grieve on their own, to make them realise that they are not alone in facing this,” Chan said in Cantonese. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. He also described the tragedy as one stemming from “human errors and systemic failures,” echoing an independent committee’s findings that named a renovation contractor and project consultant as the “main culprits” and highlighted lapses in government oversight. “This service reminds us that human lives are not disposable numbers, but cherished gifts from God,” he said. “This tenacity for life should be transformed into a pursuit for truth and justice.” A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Jenny Lam, a pastor at the Diamond Church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Hong Kong who lost three relatives in the fire, also spoke during the mass, which coincided with the birthday of one of her late relatives. “But I can no longer wish them happy birthday in person,” she said in Cantonese. The past year had been full of challenges for bereaved families, Lam said, citing the enormous administrative duties surrounding funeral arrangements alongside the emotional toll of the tragedy. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. While time had not dulled the pain, she said, she prayed that families would be able to live well and keep alive the memories of their loved ones. That did not mean forgetting the victims, but healing from the trauma while allowing room for grief, she added. The names of the 168 victims were read aloud by four bereaved survivors, ending with Ho Wai-ho, a firefighter who died in the line of duty battling the blaze. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Da Chung, a resident of Wang Fuk Court’s Wang Sun House, told reporters after the service that she felt solace as the victims’ names were read aloud, adding that bereaved families carry pain that words cannot describe. Phyllis Lo, who lost her mother in the blaze, said she felt calm when she heard her mother’s name, and imagined the lives of the other victims as their names were read out. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wednesday’s mass was overshadowed by controversy surrounding police enquiries into memorial events related to the Tai Po fire earlier this month. One church, the Immaculate Heart of Mary Church in Tai Po , has since replaced its anniversary mass with a general service for “the brothers and sisters who died in the past year.” A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Parishioners have criticised authorities for exerting pressure, but security chief Chris Tang has defended the move , saying it was necessary for authorities to assess risks for public events. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Agnes Ng, a Catholic who lost her mother in the blaze, told HKFP on Wednesday that she had helped organise the mass while residing overseas. She struck a defiant note when asked whether she perceived pressure from the authorities. A Catholic mass remembering Tai Po fire victims on November 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “They were being oversensitive… The fire occurred in Tai Po, and the Tai Po church was the most appropriate venue for a memorial service,” she said in Cantonese. “If police ask me, I will welcome them.” “[The blaze] is not just a Wang Fuk Court matter. It relates to all Hongkongers,” she added. “It’s sensible, lawful and reasonable for us to hold a mass to honour the dead. Why do we have to self-censor?”

title: Survivors battle pain, loss one year after deadly Hong Kong blaze
zh_title: 香港致命火灾一年后，幸存者与痛苦和损失作斗争
summary: 叶家驹在香港数十年来最严重的火灾中幸存下来，但他失去了家园和妻子。他们半融化的结婚戒指是他们生命中仅存的少数痕迹之一。 2025 年 11 月 26 日，香港一处住宅区发生毁灭性火灾，造成 168 人死亡，一年后，幸存者和失去亲人的家庭正在为失去亲人而苦苦挣扎。法新社采访了 1980 年以来世界上最致命的住宅楼火灾的幸存者：68 岁的叶家驹 (Yip Ka-kui Yip) 经常沿着他与结婚四十年的妻子白水莲 (Pak Shui-lin) 一起去的公寓大楼的路线走，他说，白水莲 (Pak Shui-lin) 已去世
content:
叶家驹在香港数十年来最严重的火灾中幸存下来，但他失去了家园和妻子。他们半融化的结婚戒指是他们生命中仅存的少数痕迹之一。 2025 年 11 月 26 日，香港一处住宅区发生毁灭性火灾，造成 168 人死亡，一年后，幸存者和失去亲人的家庭正在为失去亲人而苦苦挣扎。法新社采访了 1980 年以来世界上最致命的住宅楼火灾的幸存者：68 岁的叶家驹 (Yip Ka-kui Yip) 经常沿着他与结婚四十年的妻子白水莲 (Pak Shui-lin) 一起走过的公寓大楼的路线走下去，他说自己仍然“无法接受”她的去世。幸存者表示，朴通过敲邻居的门提醒他们发生火灾而挽救了生命。日常生活中的简单时刻让叶想起她的缺席。他说，就好像“她在家里等我回来”。他仍然向妻子的号码发送生活更新，例如孙女的成绩单。叶先生还送来了半融化的结婚戒指进行修复，希望从废墟中打捞出来的物品可以代代相传，以纪念这一事件。 2025年12月2日，香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑致命火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。他告诉法新社，政府的道歉“缺乏诚意”，并补充说他希望社会确保“正义得到伸张”。
38 岁的楚楚 (Chu Chu) 回忆起一名验尸官掀起覆盖着他 76 岁父亲烧焦遗体的布，他的遗体是从被掏空的公寓里找到的，骨灰在空气中翻滚。 来自 Getty Images 的嵌入 “感觉就像我的父亲真的消失在时间的沙子里一样，”他说。 “我觉得我还没有找到我的父亲。火灾发生前不久，我还能和他说话。我仍然无法理解我在太平间看到的实际上是他。”他 45 岁的姐姐也担心，在父亲的物品被毁后，她们对父亲的记忆可能会“消失”。她仍然保留着他在火灾发生前六天送给她儿子的生日牛奶糖。他们的父亲曾担任殖民时代英国驻军的车辆修理工和夜班出租车司机。兄弟姐妹说，他在火灾中幸存下来的物品包括一把军刀和一罐 50 美分的硬币——象征着他的勤奋精神和对家庭无条件的爱。 61岁的何贝蒂(Betty Ho Ho)在该住宅区居住了35年，并用了20年的时间还清了公寓的贷款。当她说火灾“夺走了我的一切”时，她刚刚开始享受退休生活。对于何来说，这场悲剧揭示了“整个体系和政府结构的问题”。她说，官员们在火灾发生前没有听取居民的投诉。她现在住在政府安排的临时住房里，但不愿意把它称为家。
与大多数其他居民不同，何女士没有接受政府买断，而是要求在同一地点重建住宅区，这一提议被当局拒绝。“那所房子离得很近，但你不能回去，”她在现在的住所说，从那里她可以看到她的旧公寓。何说，灾难发生一年后，她感到“无助”。 “未来五年是不可能的，我什至无法想象。” Harry Leung Leung 是最后一批逃离火灾的居民之一。 “我们没有好好地告别我们住了这么久的地方，”20多岁、从小就住在公寓里的梁说。他说他走了

【原文 English Original】
Yip Ka-kui survived Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades, but he lost his home and his wife. Their half-melted wedding rings are among the few traces that remain of their lives. A year after the devastating November 26, 2025 fire killed 168 people in a Hong Kong housing estate, survivors and bereaved families are struggling with their loss. AFP spoke to survivors of the world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980: Yip Ka-kui Yip, 68, often finds himself retracing the path to the apartment complex that he used to take with his wife of four decades, Pak Shui-lin, whose death he says he still “cannot accept”. Embed from Getty Images Survivors say Pak saved lives by knocking on neighbours’ doors to alert them to the fire. Simple moments of daily life remind Yip of her absence. It’s as though “she is at home waiting for me to return”, he said. He still sends life updates, such as their granddaughter’s report card, to his wife’s number. Yip also sent their half-melted wedding rings for restoration, hoping that objects salvaged from the ruins can be passed down through generations as a reminder of the incident. Hongkongers pay tribute on December 2, 2025, to the victims who died in the fatal fire in Tai Po Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The government’s apology “lacked sincerity”, he told AFP, adding that he hoped the society would ensure “justice is served”. Chu Chu, 38, recalled a coroner lifting the cloth covering his 76-year-old father’s charred remains recovered from their gutted flat, stirring ashes into the air. Embed from Getty Images “It felt like my dad was actually vanishing into the sands of time,” he said. “I feel like I haven’t found my dad. Not long before the fire, I could still talk to him. “I still can’t fathom what I saw in the mortuary was actually him.” His 45-year-old sister also fears their memories of their father might “drift away” after his belongings were destroyed. She still keeps the milk candies he gave her son for his birthday, six days before the fire. Their father used to work as a vehicle mechanic for the colonial-era British garrison and as a night-shift taxi driver. Among his belongings that survived the fire were a military blade and a jar of 50-cent coins — symbols of his hardworking spirit and unconditional love for the family, the siblings said. Betty Ho Ho, 61, lived in the housing estate for 35 years and spent two decades paying off her apartment. Embed from Getty Images She had just begun to enjoy retirement when she said the fire “took everything away from me”. For Ho, the tragedy revealed “problems with the entire system and the government structure”. Officials, she said, failed to heed residents’ complaints before the fire. She now lives in government-arranged temporary housing, but is reluctant to call it home. Unlike most other residents, Ho did not accept a government buyout and instead called for the housing complex to be rebuilt on the same site — a proposal rejected by authorities. “That home is so close, but you can’t go back,” she said at her current residence, from which she can see her old flat. Ho said she felt “helpless” a year after the disaster. “It’s impossible to think about the next five years, I can’t even imagine it.” Harry Leung Leung was among the last residents to escape the fire. “We didn’t properly say goodbye to a place where we had lived for so long,” said Leung, who was in his late 20s and had lived in the flat since childhood. He said he took the government’s buyout offer out of necessity. Wang Fuk Court on November 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “(The officials) had sugarcoated this as a mutually agreeable transaction,” he told AFP. As part of the buyout scheme, he bought another property but was saddled with more than HK$1 million (US$128,000) in debt. That financial burden was “never part of my life plan”, he added. “I’m still young… but for other residents who have already retired and may have little income, such change is an overburden for them.” Rhodora Alcaraz Tunacao Tunacao, 29, was a Filipino migrant domestic worker widely hailed as a hero for protecting a three-month-old baby girl during the fire one day after starting work in Hong Kong. Embed from Getty Images After being treated in the intensive care unit for smoke inhalation, she returned to the Philippines in December. But she remains under emotional stress, according to Esther Tse, an advocate for workers rights who visits her regularly. Tunacao also suffers from lung problems, requiring regular follow-ups and medication, Tse said. At times, she coughed up black phlegm. She needs depression medication and is easily agitated, but mental health professionals are scarce in her region, Tse added.

title: Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy: Why Hong Kong’s works regulation must break from civil service culture
zh_title: 宏福苑火灾惨案：为何香港的工程规管必须脱离公务员文化
summary: 宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们思考一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第二）
content:
宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们思考一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第一）。然而，我们在宏福苑火灾悲剧和其他与工程相关的丑闻中却表现出了监管的无能。调查火灾的独立审查委员会将监管失误描述为“系统性和普遍性”。香港在金融服务、公共卫生、诚信（反腐败）和其他领域的监管无疑相对较好。因此评价很高。因此，我们不能说工程监管的缺位和/或不力（不仅是宏福苑火灾，还有玛丽医院电梯事件、太宗电梯防火板事件等）代表了整个香港的公共监管。问题是，为什么建筑监管如此草率和参差不齐，明显优先考虑行政便利，或许还保护建筑业？
政府的工务部门历史悠久，是殖民地香港最早的政府职能之一，人员全部由公务员组成。当局于 1843 年设立测量总署。1870 年演变为测量部，并于 1883 年更名为工务署 (PWD)。工务署管理所有工务职能。 1982 年，官员们将这个庞然大物拆分为七个工程部门。它们大多由现任发展局局长监管。报告向我们展示了几十年来一直容忍的监管制度——未能充分优先考虑服务和保护公众。那些领导建筑和建设的人大多是从公务员队伍内部提拔的，公务员队伍分为专业队伍。新入职的公务员在进入时就已经融入了本部门实践中的价值观。团队领导者和团队成员执行非正式规范，指导新进入者应如何行事以及对他们的期望。接受这些非正式规范对于在部门中相处和取得进步是必要的。 “不要破坏现状”的文化占主导地位。官僚问责制度在这些规范内运作。官僚文化具有“粘性”，难以改变。现在想想我们表现良好的监管机构：香港金融管理局、证券及期货事务监察委员会、廉政公署。
在最近的各个时期，这些当局都是在公务员系统之外设立的。在这些当局中，当局优先考虑的是与过去的做法的彻底决裂。独立委员会关于宏福苑火灾的报告副本，2026 年 10 月 29 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。委员会对火灾的审查报告特别指出了住房部门独立检查组（ICU）的行为。独立审查组本应监督宏福苑的外墙翻新及保养工作，批准图则、进行检查并确保符合楼宇安全标准

【原文 English Original】
A year on from the Wang Fuk Court blaze, which claimed 168 lives, let’s consider whether the government’s response is sufficient. Authorities apologised and housing chief Winnie Ho resigned. These are welcome moves, and the focus now is on reform. But one area stands out: Hong Kong’s apparently uneven regulatory quality. Hongkongers pay tribute to victims who died in the fatal fire in Tai Po Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The World Bank rates Hong Kong’s regulatory regime highly. The city ranks eighth out of some 200 territories globally and second in Asia after Singapore (globally ranked as No. 1). And yet we have demonstrated regulatory incapacity in the Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy and other works-related scandals. The independent review committee looking into the blaze described the regulatory failings as “ systematic and pervasive .” Hong Kong regulates financial services, public health, integrity (anti-corruption) and undoubtedly other areas relatively well. Hence the high rating. So, we cannot say that absent and/or poor works regulation (not only the Wang Fuk Court fire disaster, but the Queen Mary Hospital elevator case , the Taizoom elevator fire panel case , etc.) is representative of Hong Kong public regulation as a whole. The question is why building and construction regulation is so sloppy and uneven, apparently prioritising administrative convenience and perhaps protecting the construction industry? The works side of the government is ancient, created among the earliest government functions in colonial Hong Kong and staffed entirely by civil servants. Authorities set up the Surveyor General’s Office in 1843. It morphed into the Survey Department in 1870, and was renamed the Public Works Department (PWD) in 1883. PWD managed all works functions. In 1982, officials broke up this behemoth into seven works departments. They are mostly supervised by the Secretary for Development who is still in her post. The report shows us that a regulatory regime – which had failed to sufficiently prioritise serving and protecting the public – was tolerated for decades. Those leading building and construction are mostly promoted from within the civil service, which is organised into professional streams. Newly hired civil servants are socialised into the values in practice of their department when they enter. Team leaders and team members enforce informal norms that guide new entrants into how they should behave and what is expected of them. Accepting these informal norms is necessary to get along and ahead in the department. A “don’t rock the boat” culture dominates. Bureaucratic accountability systems operate within these norms. Bureaucratic culture is “sticky” and difficult to change. Now consider our well-performing regulators: the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Securities and Futures Commission, the Independent Commission Against Corruption. Each of relatively recent vintage, these authorities were set up outside the civil service. In them, authorities prioritised a sharp break from past practice. Copies of the independent committee’s report on the Wang Fuk Court fire, on October 29, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The committee review report into the fire singles out the behaviour of the housing department’s Independent Checking Unit (ICU). The ICU was supposed to supervise external wall renovation and maintenance work at Wang Fuk Court, approving plans, conducting inspections and ensuring compliance with building safety standards. Authorities classified Wang Fuk Court’s renovation as lower-risk “minor works” although it was an eye-popping HK$330 million project. This reduced the statutory level of ICU oversight required. The unit was also responsible for investigating and addressing residents’ reports and safety complaints. The report noted in particular the ICU’s “lack of sense of crisis, regulatory lapses, systemic blind spots, and enforcement failures.” This is a damning judgement. The ICU is composed of senior professionals including many structural engineers, maintenance surveyors, architects, and technical staff. Not only did the ICU fail in its duty to serve and protect citizens, but the professionals among them failed in their duty to uphold the values of professionalism, integrity, and excellence. The government set up a new public housing building control section which is welcome. But transferring the existing ICU staff who bring with them values in practice that led to the tragedy is a mistake. I urge the government to set up a new body outside the existing works bureaucracy. Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on December 2, 2025, days after a fatal fire engulfed seven of the eight blocks of the residential estate. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Beyond government, action is needed too. Professional bodies should enforce discipline among their members. Many professionals were involved in the various works scandals. Professional bodies such as the Engineers Registration Board should investigate those involved, and if found culpable, take action with consequences, such as suspending or cancelling their licences to practise in Hong Kong.
