title: HKFP Lens: A year of grief and inquiry, after Tai Po blaze
zh_title: HKFP 镜头：大埔大火后悲痛与质询的一年
summary: 宏福苑是一个建于 20 世纪 80 年代靠近吐露港的八座住宅屋村，拥有近 2,000 户家庭。消防处于 2026 年 11 月 26 日对宏福苑致命火灾作出反应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大埔综合楼的家庭辛辛苦苦买了一套舒适的公寓并养育了他们的孩子——其中一些人后来成为了公寓的业主，在同一片土地上养育了第三代。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔致命火灾发生一天后，一名男子站在被毁坏的宏福苑屋苑前。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
content:
宏福苑是一个建于 20 世纪 80 年代靠近吐露港的八座住宅屋村，拥有近 2,000 户家庭。消防处于 2026 年 11 月 26 日对宏福苑致命火灾作出反应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大埔综合楼的家庭辛辛苦苦买了一套舒适的公寓并养育了他们的孩子——其中一些人后来成为了公寓的业主，在同一片土地上养育了第三代。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔致命火灾发生一天后，一名男子站在被毁坏的宏福苑屋苑前。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。它曾是香港梦的缩影，直到去年11月26日下午，社区发生致命火灾。由于当时正在进行大规模翻修工程，火势迅速蔓延到八栋用泡沫板和脚手架网覆盖的建筑物中的七栋。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，家人在辨认大埔大火受害者亲人的尸体后哭泣。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在平常的工作日下午，老年人、儿童、全职妈妈、夜班后休息的爸爸以及家政工人都被困在火灾中。 2025年11月28日，在致命的大埔火灾中失去家园的人们暂时住在广福村的大厅，这是一个公共屋村，靠近遭受火灾的宏福苑。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
这场大火最终夺去了 168 人的生命，导致数千人无家可归，标志着充满无尽悲伤、愤怒和疑问的一年的开始。香港摄影记者回顾了过去一年的照片，我们的摄影记者跟踪了香港数十年来最严重火灾后的重大事件和事态发展。火灾发生后，数以千计的香港人动员线上线下支持受害者。照片显示，2025 年 11 月 27 日，志愿者在宏福法院附近集会，设立摊位，提供免费食物、衣服和生活用品。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，人们在大埔地铁里阅读对火灾受害者的支持信息。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025年12月5日，数千人献花和玩偶，哀悼宏福苑火灾中的遇难者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，一名学生在哀悼死者时流下了眼泪。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，道士为死者举行仪式。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。火灾发生后，宏福苑部分建筑物发现非阻燃脚手架网。后来被证实是导致火势迅速蔓延的原因之一。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。火灾发生后不久，立法会于 2025 年 12 月 7 日举行选举。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 11月底，香港警务处命令义工拆除广福村平台的临时补给站。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
2025 年 12 月 19 日，消防员聚集在一起哀悼在大埔火灾中因公殉职的消防员何伟豪。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。悲剧发生后，2026年1月16日，宏福苑居民江志强（左一）、李家强（中）和叶家驹（右一）回忆起居民如何徒劳地试图报告火灾风险。他们敦促政府调查火灾原因。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2026年2月5日，独立委员会召开了上市前第一次公开会议。

【原文 English Original】
Wang Fuk Court, an eight-block residential estate built in the 1980s near Tolo Harbour, was home to nearly 2,000 households. The Fire Services Department responds to the fatal blaze at Wang Fuk Court on November 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The families at the Tai Po complex had worked hard to purchase a comfortable flat and raise their children – some of whom later became flat owners, bringing up a third generation on the same estate. On November 27, 2025, one day after the fatal Tai Po fire started, a man stands in front of the ravaged Wang Fuk Court housing estate. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. It was the epitome of the Hong Kong dream, until a fatal fire struck the community on the afternoon of November 26 last year. The blaze quickly spread through seven of the eight buildings which were covered with foam board and scaffolding nets, as a large-scale renovation project was underway at the time. On November 27, 2025, family members cry after identifying the bodies of loved ones who fell victim to the fatal Tai Po fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Seniors, children, full-time moms, dads who were taking a break after night shifts, and domestic workers were among those trapped in the fire during the otherwise ordinary weekday afternoon. On November 28, 2025, people who lost their homes in the deadly Tai Po fire stay temporarily in the hall of Kwong Fuk Estate, a public housing estate near the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The fire eventually claimed 168 lives, left thousands homeless, and marked the start of a year of relentless grief, anger and questions. HKFP looks back at images from the past year, as our photojournalist followed the major events and developments surrounding the aftermath of Hong Kong’s worst fire in decades. Following the fire, thousands of Hongkongers mobilised online and offline to support victims. The photo shows volunteers rallying to set up booths to provide free food, clothes and daily necessities near Wang Fuk court on November 27, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. People read supportive messages for the fire victims in a subway in Tai Po on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On December 5, 2025, thousands of people presented flowers and dolls to mourn those killed in the Wang Fuk Court fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A student sheds tears while mourning the deceased on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Taoist priests hold rituals for the deceased on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Following the fire, non-flame retardant scaffolding nets were identified on some buildings of Wang Fuk Court. They were later confirmed as one of the causes leading to the rapid spread of the blaze. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Soon after the fire, the Legislative Council held elections on December 7, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In late November, the Hong Kong Police Force orders volunteers to remove the makeshift supply stations at a podium of Kwong Fuk Estate. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On December 19, 2025, firefighters gathered and mourned Ho Wai Ho, a firefighter who died in the line of duty during the Tai Po fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Following the tragedy, on January 16, 2026, Wang Fuk Court residents Jason Kong (first from left), Garrick Lee (middle) and Yip Ka-kui (first from right) recalled how residents made futile attempts to flag fire risks. They urged the government to investigate the causes of the fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On February 5, 2026, an independent committee held the first public meeting before starting hearings to probe the Tai Po fire. Judge David Lok (3rd left), chair of the committee, is seen walking out of the hearing. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Tony Tsui (centre right), the former chair of Wang Fuk Court owners’ corporation management committee, leaves after attending a public hearing to probe the Tai Po deadly fire on March 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Wang Fuk Court resident talks with the press after attending a public hearing on March 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On April 20, 2026, nearly half a year after the fire, Wang Fuk Court residents are allowed to return to their fire-ravaged homes to retrieve belongings. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wang Fuk Court residents return home to retrieve belongings on May 4, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A resident of Wang Fuk Court is seen in his fire-ravaged flat as he looks to retrieve personal belongings on April 23, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Wang Fuk Court resident finds his wedding rings in his flat at Wang Fuk Court on April 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On July 19, 2026, the administrator of the Wang Fuk Court housing estate hosted a special owners’ meeting at four different venues, after a months-long wait. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Jason Kong, a flat owner of Wang Fuk Court and a former member of the owners’ board, was arrested over alleged fraud in May 2026 and charged in August after he organised a petition for a homeowners’ meeting. The photo shows Kong leaving the Shatin Law Courts Buildings on September 1, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Nearly one year after the tragedy, Hong Kong leader John Lee led top officials to bow in apology as he introduced reforms related to the Tai Po fire. The press conference was held on October 29, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Roman Catholic bishop Joseph Ha offers blessings to Wang Fuk Court residents during a mass at the Immaculate Heart of Mary Church on November 15, 2026. The church revised the theme of the mass from one dedicated to the fire victims to one for “remembering all who had passed away over the past year.” The change came after they reportedly faced police enquiries. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court flat is seen with banners stating “I love Wang Fuk” and “I want to move back” on the window. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A community art exhibition by NGO Forget Thee Not in Central called “Life Goes On” on November 25, 2026. Several Wang Fuk Court residents participated in the show, expressing their feelings and experiences through text and photos. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wang Fuk Court on November 19, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP.

title: Op-Ed: US midterms won’t change mining policy. They’ll change who gets subpoenaed
zh_title: 专栏：美国中期选举不会改变矿业政策。他们会改变被传唤的人
summary: 2026 年美国中期选举不太可能对采矿业产生全面的法定变化，因为行政部门仍保留对许可、公共土地管理、贸易政策、关税或关键矿产融资的控制权。然而，国会控制权的转移决定了谁挥舞木槌，谁举行听证会、发出传票并吸引公众关注。未来两年，委员会将围绕行业面临的几个核心压力加强审查，包括投资和项目选择、政治影响、环境和社会影响以及
content:
2026 年美国中期选举不太可能对采矿业产生全面的法定变化，因为行政部门仍保留对许可、公共土地管理、贸易政策、关税或关键矿产融资的控制权。然而，国会控制权的转移决定了谁挥舞木槌，谁举行听证会、发出传票并吸引公众关注。未来两年，委员会将围绕行业面临的几个核心压力加强审查，包括投资和项目选择、政治影响、环境和社会影响以及中国。其结果不是政策格局的不同，而是对决策、资本配置和绩效的更严格审查。对于矿业公司来说，项目开发、许可和矿产安全的核心政策驱动力仍然处于行政部门的控制之下，不会发生变化。关键矿产仍然是两党的国家优先事项 确保关键矿产的安全被视为国家安全的当务之急。锂、铜、石墨、稀土、钴、镍和铀被广泛视为国防系统、先进制造、人工智能数据中心和电网基础设施的基础。
立法者在国内开采、战略储备、电池回收和联合海外投资的需求以及美国依赖外国供应商的稀土分离、化学精炼和永磁体制造等下游优先事项方面仍然保持一致。这一承诺不太可能随着选举而改变。双方都没有放弃减少美国对外国控制的矿产供应链的依赖，已经适应将矿产视为国家安全资产的投资者和开发商可以预期该框架将保持不变。联邦融资工具和市场势头保持不变 关键的联邦融资机制，包括《国防生产法》第三章拨款、能源部贷款计划办公室的贷款、五角大楼的战略资本计划以及通过进出口银行 (EXIM) 和国际开发金融公司 (DFC) 进行的海外项目融资，仍主要受行政部门控制，并继续享有两党的广泛支持。已经承担的奖励不太可能被收回，而且政府保留很大的自由度来部署这些工具来支持国内开采和联合加工项目。市场基本面强化了政策的推动力。
黄金、铜、银和其他工业金属的价格上涨扩大了经济上可行的项目库，而国家安全优先事项继续吸引整个行业的公共和私人资本。尽管较高的利率和建筑成本仍然受到限制，但支持性大宗商品市场、联邦融资工具和对关键矿产的战略需求的结合创造了势头，无论国会加强监督，这种势头都可能持续下去。改变的不是支持的可用性，而是随之而来的审查。关键矿产投资、豁免和项目选择新成立的委员会将审查联邦支持计划的部署方式以及受益者。监督小组在向政府问责办公室 (GAO) 提出的正式请求的支持下，准备审查政府对快速当局和非交易手段的依赖。

【原文 English Original】
The 2026 U.S. midterm elections are unlikely to produce sweeping statutory changes for the mining sector, as the executive branch maintains control over permitting, public land management, trade policy, tariffs, or critical mineral financing. However, shifting control of Congress determines who wields the gavel—and who holds hearings, issues subpoenas, and commands public attention.   Over the next two years, committees will intensify scrutiny around several core pressures facing the industry, including investments and project selection, political influence, environmental and social impacts, and China. The consequence is not a different policy landscape, but greater scrutiny of decisions, capital allocation, and performance.  For mining companies, the core policy drivers of project development, permitting, and mineral security remain under executive branch control and will not shift.  Critical minerals remain a bipartisan national priority   Securing critical minerals is accepted as a national security imperative. Lithium, copper, graphite, rare earths, cobalt, nickel, and uranium are widely viewed as foundational to defense systems, advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence data centers, and grid infrastructure.   Lawmakers remain aligned on the need for domestic extraction, strategic stockpiling, battery recycling, and allied overseas investments—along with downstream priorities, like rare-earth separation, chemical refining, and permanent magnet manufacturing, where the U.S. depends on foreign suppliers.  That commitment is unlikely to shift with the election. Neither party is retreating from reducing U.S. reliance on foreign-controlled mineral supply chains, and investors and developers who have adapted to treating minerals as national-security assets can expect that framework to remain intact.  Federal financing tools and market momentum remain intact   Key federal financing mechanisms, including Defense Production Act Title III grants, loans from the Department of Energy’s Loan Programs Office, strategic capital initiatives at the Pentagon, and overseas project financing through the Export-Import Bank (EXIM) and International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), remain largely under executive branch control and continue to enjoy broad bipartisan backing.   Already-obligated awards are unlikely to be clawed back, and the administration retains substantial latitude to deploy these tools in support of domestic extraction and allied processing projects.  Market fundamentals reinforce that policy tailwind. Elevated prices for gold, copper, silver, and other industrial metals have expanded the pool of economically viable projects, while national security priorities continue to attract public and private capital across the sector.   Although higher interest rates and construction costs remain constraints, the combination of supportive commodity markets, federal financing tools, and strategic demand for critical minerals has created momentum likely to persist regardless of increased congressional oversight.  What changes is not the availability of support, but the scrutiny attached to it.  Critical mineral investments, waivers, and project selection   Incoming committees will examine how federal support programs have been deployed and who has benefited. Oversight panels—backed by formal requests to the Government Accountability Office (GAO)—are poised to scrutinize the administration’s reliance on expedited authorities and non-traditional deal structures.   Specifically, lawmakers will likely scrutinize whether agencies used Cold War-era Defense Production Act procurement waivers (“without regard to” contracting rules) to bypass competitive bidding, whether conflicts of interest were properly mitigated, and whether underwriting standards were relaxed to accelerate awards.  This scrutiny will extend beyond traditional grants and loans into novel public-private financing vehicles. Committees are likely to audit direct federal equity stakes—such as the Pentagon taking ownership positions in domestic rare-earth producers—alongside multi-billion-dollar EXIM and DFC project loans, DOE financing, and controversial stockpiling mechanisms like EXIM’s $12 billion public-private “ Project Vault .”   For companies receiving substantial federal backing, the burden of proof is shifting: recipients will increasingly be asked to defend both their commercial viability and technical readiness, and the transparency of their selection process, beneficial ownership, and compliance with statutory eligibility rules.  Political influence and mining projects   Few issues are likely to attract congressional attention more quickly than allegations that political relationships, rather than project merit, influenced access to federal support. Public reports have highlighted connections between family members of senior administration officials—and their affiliated firms—and mining and critical mineral ventures.   A June 2026 New York Times investigation identified some 14 critical mineral companies pursuing federal support with financial ties to administration family members, including rare-earth projects in North Carolina and California, a tungsten project in Kazakhstan, and an antimony and gold project in Idaho. Given incoming committees’ intense focus on undue influence and corruption, lawmakers almost certainly will ask how these relationships intersect with federal financing, permitting, and procurement decisions.  In many cases, the central issue may not be legality, but legitimacy. Congressional committees are often as interested in whether decision-making appears transparent and impartial as whether a specific rule was violated. For mining companies, the practical question is not simply whether they can withstand a regulatory review, but how they stand up in a hearing.  Social license, governance and project legitimacy   Congressional attention will focus increasingly on how mining projects affect local communities. Public reports have highlighted government efforts to advance mining projects while weakening or bypassing environmental and social safeguards, domestically and internationally.   Domestically, those include proposed Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land-use overrides, compressed 28-day emergency reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) for energy and mineral projects on federal lands, and the addition of domestic mines and processing facilities to the FAST-41 expedited permitting dashboard.  Internationally, scrutiny is mounting over bilateral critical mineral deals negotiated without enforceable labor, human rights, Indigenous consent, or environmental protections. As an early preview, following the midterms, incoming Democratic majorities have already announced plans to review all 11 Latin American mineral instruments, alongside billions in financing through EXIM and the DFC.   That scrutiny will also target corruption, state capture, and opaque joint ventures in high-risk mineral jurisdictions across Africa, Latin America, and Central Asia — companies operating through local intermediaries or state-linked partners will be tested to show their anti-corruption vetting and governance controls withstand close scrutiny. Expect oversight hearings focused squarely on tribal consultation, sacred sites, Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC), community engagement, and environmental compliance.  China, foreign investment, and midstream chokepoints   Scrutiny of mining is not limited to extraction; congressional oversight is shifting downstream to processing and refining. Even when ore is mined domestically or in allied nations, projects frequently rely on Chinese separation technology, state-backed financing, or Chinese refiners—which still control roughly 90% of global rare-earth processing and over 75% of cobalt and nickel refining.   With the new Congress preparing to exercise heightened oversight, anticipate lawmakers scrutinizing whether federal loans, equity stakes, and permitting fast-tracks are genuinely severing reliance on Beijing or merely subsidizing upstream extraction while leaving the midstream bottleneck intact.  Oversight will likely include joint ventures, licensing agreements, and exposure to Beijing’s expanding export controls on heavy rare earths, permanent magnets, and processing technologies — including extraterritorial rules for foreign products containing trace amounts of Chinese-refined materials. As Beijing restricts supply-chain data, companies will face a widening bind: diligence gets harder at the exact moment regulations, committees, Section 232 probes, and FEOC rules demand visibility into every tier.  Forced labor enforcement and chain-of-custody traceability   Scrutiny is also likely to remain sharply focused on forced labor risks and end-to-end mineral traceability. Lawmakers across both parties increasingly treat supply-chain transparency as a human rights mandate and industrial competitiveness tool—using forced labor enforcement to counter state-subsidized Chinese supply chains.   U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has expanded enforcement of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) beyond polysilicon and aluminum into lithium, battery-grade graphite, steel, and copper, with oversight focusing high-risk processing corridors—including Xinjiang, artisanal cobalt mining in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Chinese-operated nickel hubs in Indonesia.  For mining companies, traders, and downstream manufacturers, traceability is no longer a passive compliance exercise or a reliance on self-reported Tier-1 supplier certifications. Under the UFLPA—and growing disclosure demands from automotive, defense, and clean-energy buyers—companies face border detentions, export-financing disqualifications, and reputational fallout unless they can produce auditable chain-of-custody records. Increasingly, regulators, lenders, and congressional investigators expect firms to map commingled feedstocks across intermediary traders and third-country smelters, proving with verifiable data where raw ore originates and how labor risks are monitored at every step of the value chain.  Tariffs, bilateral frameworks, and mineral trade security   Trade policy will remain central to the mining sector. While unilateral tariff powers under Sections 301 and 232—including the administration’s January 2026 Section 232 critical-minerals proclamation —remain largely within the Executive Branch, incoming committees are poised to scrutinize how import duties, export controls, and price-stabilization mechanisms affect midstream processing bottlenecks and downstream U.S. manufacturers.   Lawmakers are already asking whether broad tariffs shield domestic refiners from Chinese predatory pricing or inadvertently raise input costs for U.S. defense, automotive, and grid-infrastructure projects before domestic refining capacity is ready to scale.  Congressional attention will also focus on the administration’s growing web of bilateral critical-minerals agreements across Latin America, Africa, and the Indo-Pacific. With incoming committee leaders signaling plans to review executive-negotiated mineral pacts, public-private stockpiling initiatives, and allied-country carve-outs, lawmakers will examine whether these frameworks genuinely diversify processing away from China or simply create tariff-free backdoors for foreign-controlled supply chains. For mining companies and traders, securing preferential market access, tariff exemptions, or federal off-take support increasingly requires proving strict rules-of-origin compliance—demonstrating not just where ore is extracted, but where it is refined and how the project measurably reduces strategic reliance on foreign adversaries.  What to watch   Four signposts will define the landscape of what to watch:  Early Subpoenas and GAO Inquiries . Watch the opening oversight agendas of the House Natural Resources, Energy and Commerce, and Oversight committees—alongside pending GAO inquiries—for early document requests targeting EXIM, DFC, DOE, and Pentagon financing awards, particularly deals involving procurement waivers or politically exposed investors.  FEOC and China Stress-Testing . Companies relying on federal loans, tax credits, or defense offtake agreements should expect tighter audits of joint ventures, licensing deals, and third-country refiners to ensure compliance with FEOC rules and resilience against Chinese export-licensing delays.  Litigation Over Permitting . Watch for federal court injunctions and congressional hearings testing whether streamlined reviews came at the expense of defensible tribal consultation and environmental records.  Traceability . Companies that move beyond self-reported supplier certifications toward verifiable, smelter-level traceability will be best positioned to avoid border detentions and secure allied buyer contracts.  Bottom line   With the 2026 midterms, the mining sector is entering a period in which congressional scrutiny may matter almost as much as commodity prices. Permits, financing, and government support should remain available. The harder question is whether companies can demonstrate the transparency, legitimacy, and strategic value needed to withstand close scrutiny.  Jonathan Drimmer, a partner at Steptoe LLP, is former Deputy General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer at Barrick Gold and served as a deputy director in the U.S. Department of Justice’s Criminal Division .

title: Cyclic Materials picks Germany for first European plant
zh_title: 循环材料公司选择德国作为第一家欧洲工厂
summary: 稀土回收商 Cyclic Materials 在德国选择了一个地点作为其首个欧洲磁体回收设施，这标志着其国际扩张的一个里程碑。这家私营公司周四表示，在莱比锡附近施科保的陶氏价值园签署了一项设施土地预留协议。拟建工厂将为欧洲稀土回收网络奠定基础，有可能满足欧盟多达 15% 的稀土需求。 “欧洲知道可以通过国内循环稀土和关键矿产经济来实现经济弹性
content:
稀土回收商 Cyclic Materials 在德国选择了一个地点作为其首个欧洲磁体回收设施，这标志着其国际扩张的一个里程碑。这家私营公司周四表示，在莱比锡附近施科保的陶氏价值园签署了一项设施土地预留协议。拟建工厂将为欧洲稀土回收网络奠定基础，有可能满足欧盟多达 15% 的稀土需求。 Cyclic 首席执行官 Ahmad Ghahreman 在声明中表示：“欧洲知道通过国内循环稀土和关键矿产经济可以带来经济弹性。”这一扩张正值欧洲对稀土磁体的需求预计在未来十年内将增加一倍以上，而中国占全球加工稀土的 90%。回收可以帮助欧盟实现汽车、技术和国防工业必需材料的供应多元化，而无需开发新矿山。在微软（纳斯达克股票代码：MSFT）、亚马逊（纳斯达克股票代码：AMZN）和宝马（法国股票代码：BMW）等投资者的支持下，Cyclic 计划在德国工厂每年处理 25,000 吨磁力轴承废料。该工厂将为中央化学加工中心提供原料，回收的磁铁材料将在其中精炼并分离成稀土氧化物。 Ghahreman 告诉路透社，这家德国工厂是计划在欧洲建立的五个工厂中的第一个，预计于 2028 年开始运营。
该公司还在探索向中国以外的亚洲市场扩张。经过 17 个月的开发，Cyclic 于 9 月在亚利桑那州梅萨开设了第一家商业规模的磁体回收设施。该公司还在南卡罗来纳州建设一个综合回收园区。成本优势 Schkopau 工厂将使用 Cyclic 专有的 MagCycle 技术从废弃的电动机、硬盘、无人机和工业设备中提取永磁体。年产量可达 750 吨磁精矿、14,000 吨钢、4,600 吨铝和 3,000 吨铜。实地考察：Cyclic Materials 在亚利桑那州开设商业规模的稀土回收工厂 据路透社报道，额外金属的回收支撑了 Cyclic 的成本竞争力，非稀土材料占收入的 40% 至 50%。与 MP Materials（纽约证券交易所股票代码：MP）等已获得美国政府最低价格保证的生产商不同，Cyclic 表示，其生产成本使其无需类似支持即可运营。该公司还与电子产品回收商 ERI 合作，通过其美国收集网络确保原料安全，而其 REEPure 技术则在 10 月份登上《时代》杂志 2026 年最佳发明排行榜。当被问及潜在的首次公开募股时，Ghahreman 告诉路透社，Cyclic 此前已筹集 7500 万美元用于扩大其美国业务，并有多种筹集额外资金的选择。

【原文 English Original】
Rare earth recycler Cyclic Materials has selected a site in Germany for its first European magnet recovery facility, marking a milestone in its international expansion. The privately held company signed a land reservation agreement for a facility at the Dow ValuePark in Schkopau, near Leipzig, it said Thursday. The proposed plant would lay the groundwork for a European rare earth recovery network with the potential to meet as much as 15% of the EU’s rare earth needs. “Europe knows the economic resilience that can be delivered through a domestic, circular rare earth and critical mineral economy,” Cyclic CEO Ahmad Ghahreman said in the statement. The expansion comes as European demand for rare earth magnets is projected to more than double over the next decade, while China accounts for 90% of global processed rare earths. Recycling could help the European Union diversify its supplies of materials essential to the automotive, technology and defence industries without developing new mines. Backed by investors including Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and BMW (FRA: BMW), Cyclic plans to process 25,000 tonnes of magnet-bearing scrap annually at the German facility. The plant would feed a central chemical processing hub, where recovered magnet material would be refined and separated into rare earth oxides. The German facility, the first of five planned for Europe, is slated to begin operations in 2028, Ghahreman told Reuters. The company is also exploring expansion into Asian markets outside China. Cyclic opened its first commercial-scale magnet recovery facility in Mesa, Arizona, in September following 17 months of development. It is also building an integrated recycling campus in South Carolina . Cost advantage The Schkopau plant would use Cyclic’s proprietary MagCycle technology to extract permanent magnets from discarded electric motors, hard drives, drones and industrial equipment. Annual output could reach 750 tonnes of magnet concentrate, alongside 14,000 tonnes of steel, 4,600 tonnes of aluminum and 3,000 tonnes of copper. Site visit: Cyclic Materials opens commercial-scale rare earth recycling plant in Arizona The recovery of additional metals underpins Cyclic’s cost competitiveness, with non-rare earth materials accounting for 40% to 50% of revenue, according to Reuters. Unlike producers such as MP Materials (NYSE: MP), which has secured minimum price guarantees from the US government, Cyclic says its production costs allow it to operate without similar support. The company has also partnered with electronics recycler ERI to secure feedstock through its US collection network, while its REEPure technology earned a spot on TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 list in October. Cyclic previously secured $75 million to expand its US operations and has several options for raising additional capital, Ghahreman told Reuters when asked about a potential initial public offering.

保护西藏环境。保护我们共同的未来。西藏的河流养活了数百万人。谁来保护他们的来源？西藏是亚洲一些最重要河流的源头。它的冰川、雪地和水道为下游约 14 亿人口提供了生存保障。然而，这一至关重要的环境正面临着越来越大的威胁。 2026年，尼藏边境发生的一场灾难，引发了国际社会对西藏面临的环境风险的关注。这是一个鲜明的提醒：西藏环境发生的变化所产生的后果远远超出了西藏的边界。我们要保护西藏的环境。我们需要保护我们共同的未来。十多年来，澳大利亚西藏理事会和世界各地的西藏团体一直对西藏冰川加速融化和环境破坏发出警报。气候变化正在加速冰川融化，增加洪水和其他环境灾害的风险。与此同时，中国无节制的大规模采矿、水坝建设、引水和其他大型开发项目正在改变西藏的景观和水道。澳大利亚西藏委员会正在争取全球暂停西藏的采矿和大型开发。我们呼吁停止这些项目，直到藏人能够自由决定他们的土地会发生什么，并且可以表示同意或拒绝同意，而不必担心被捕、监禁或酷刑。这不仅仅是一场环保运动。
这是一项争取西藏人民权利的运动，旨在保护他们的土地、河流和他们的未来。 呼吁捐款表 如果您希望通过直接存款的方式捐款，请参阅下面的银行详细信息： 账户名称：澳大利亚西藏委员会 BSB：063 147 帐号：1001 0643 请务必在参考资料中注明“EOYA26”和您的姓名 通过向澳大利亚西藏委员会的年终呼吁捐款，您将帮助我们：按澳大利亚西藏委员会政府对西藏发生的环境破坏采取更强硬的立场。增加国际社会对全球暂停西藏采矿和大型开发项目的支持。要求科学家、研究人员、记者和人道主义组织独立进入西藏。提高藏人为他们的环境发声的声音。几个世纪以来，西藏人民一直在管理着喜马拉雅山这一独特的环境，但他们对这里发生的事情没有任何有意义的发言权。西藏处于中国的占领之下。我们相信西藏人民有权保护他们的环境免受中国采矿、筑坝和大型开发项目造成的破坏。他们的权利必须得到尊重，决不能将可能产生不可逆转后果的决定强加给他们。请支持我们保护西藏独特环境的工作。尼泊尔-西藏灾难提醒世界，西藏的环境未来并不是一个遥远或孤立的问题。
河流、冰川和生态系统的健康关系到亚洲数以百万计的人民以及我们共同的未来。但保护西藏的环境必须从承认西藏人民的权利开始。他们必须有保护自己土地并决定其未来的自由。请立即向澳大利亚西藏委员会的年终呼吁捐款。您的贡献将有助于将西藏的环境问题保留在国际议程上，加强我们的全球暂停行动，并使各国政府对使其面临风险的决定负责。齐心协力，我们就能站稳脚跟

【原文 English Original】
Protect Tibet’s environment. Protect our shared future. Tibet’s rivers sustain millions. Who will protect their source? Tibet is the source of some of Asia’s most important rivers. Its glaciers, snowfields and waterways sustain approximately 1.4 billion people downstream. Yet this vital environment is under growing threat. In 2026, a disaster along the Nepal-Tibet border brought international attention to the environmental risks facing Tibet. It was a stark reminder that what happens to Tibet’s environment has consequences far beyond its borders. We need to protect Tibet’s environment. We need to protect our shared future. For more than a decade, Australia Tibet Council and Tibet groups around the world have been sounding the alarm about the accelerating glacial melt and environmental destruction taking place in Tibet. Climate change is accelerating glacial melt and increasing the risk of floods and other environmental disasters. At the same time, China's unchecked large-scale mining, dam construction, water diversion and other mega-development projects are transforming Tibet’s landscape and waterways. Australia Tibet Council is campaigning for a global moratorium on mining and mega-development in Tibet. We are calling for these projects to stop until Tibetans can freely decide what happens to their land and can give or refuse their consent without fear of arrest, imprisonment or torture. This is not simply an environmental campaign. It is a campaign for the rights of the Tibetan people to protect their land, their rivers and their future. Appeal Donation Form If you would prefer to donate via direct deposit, please see bank details below: Account name: Australia Tibet Council BSB: 063 147 Account number: 1001 0643 Please make sure to include 'EOYA26' & your name in the reference By donating to Australia Tibet Council’s End of Year Appeal, you will help us: Press the Australian Government to take a stronger stand on the environmental destruction taking place in Tibet. Grow international support for a global moratorium on mining and mega-development projects in Tibet. Demand independent access to Tibet for scientists, researchers, journalists and humanitarian organisations. Raise the voices of Tibetans speaking up for their environment. Tibetan people, who have stewarded this unique Himalayan environment for centuries, have no meaningful say in what happens to it. Tibet is under Chinese occupation. We believe the Tibetan people have the right to protect their environment from the destruction caused by China's mining, damming and mega-development projects. Their rights must be respected, and decisions with potentially irreversible consequences must never be imposed on them. Please support our work to help protect Tibet's unique environment. The Nepal-Tibet disaster reminded the world that Tibet’s environmental future is not a distant or isolated concern. The health of its rivers, glaciers and ecosystems matters to millions of people across Asia and to the future we all share. But protecting Tibet’s environment must begin with recognising the rights of the Tibetan people. They must have the freedom to protect their own land and determine its future. Please donate to Australia Tibet Council’s End of Year Appeal today. Your contribution will help keep Tibet’s environment on the international agenda, strengthen our campaign for a global moratorium and hold governments accountable for the decisions that put it at risk. Together, we can stand with the Tibetan people and defend their right to protect their land and their future.

title: Ahead of Taiwan’s Local Elections, China’s Interference Looms Large

summary: 台湾地方选举前，中国的干涉迫在眉睫——阿富汗-巴基斯坦边境阴影下的外交官读得像《外交官》：2026年假期版26/11后18年，印度最终赢得反恐战争吗？中亚如何修复最危险的边界 罗辛亚社区的新希望时刻 韩国煤炭使用量激增 — — 不仅仅是因为伊朗战争 国际法院作出历史性判决：缅甸对罗兴亚人犯有种族灭绝罪 在亚太经合组织峰会上，北京展示了其对新技术大都市的愿景 新民主党国会是什么
content:
台湾地方选举前夕，中国的干预日益凸显 – 《外交官》
在阿富汗-巴基斯坦边境的阴影下
像《外交官》一样阅读：2026 年假日版
26/11 18年后，印度最终赢得反恐战争吗？

北京通过亚太经合组织峰会展示其对新技术大都市的愿景
新民主党国会多数对特朗普的亚太政策意味着什么
台湾定于11月28日星期六举行地方选举，也称为“九合一”选举。选民将选出台湾所有22个市县的市长和县长。活动重点关注住房、福利、交通和环境等当地问题，而不是台湾与中国大陆有争议的关系。
然而，由于北京试图干涉台湾选举所造成的威胁越来越大，它已成为房间里的大象。
中国企图颠覆台湾地方选举并控制台湾国内政治并不新鲜。北京破坏台湾11月选举的战略依赖于恐吓和利诱——通过将台湾的治理定性为“不稳定”来取消台湾国民政府的合法性，在台湾周围举行军事演习以操纵公众看法，为支持与中国统一的候选人提供竞选资金，以及为在中国的台商返回台湾投票支持中国的候选人提供机票补贴。
但随着技术的进步，中共对台湾地方选举的干预活动变得更加复杂。在 11 月 28 日投票之前，台湾官员向 Meta 标记了近 2,700 个与中国有关的账户，这是中共精心策划的信息战活动的一部分，目的是散布不信任、阻止投票并煽动公众对执政党民进党 (DPP) 的愤怒。这些账户最初冒充普通台湾用户分享日常生活片段以获取信任，然后转变策略发起政治攻击并敦促选民“弃权”。
台湾陆委会副主任沉玉中警告说，北京在人工智能（AI）和人工智能生成的深度造假方面的进步使得“渗透方法变得越来越复杂”。人工智能现已成为操纵选举的工具，使其“更容易产生误导性内容”并进行影响力操作。
沉说，对中国干预选举的调查显示，中国已经利用人工智能来运行“大规模面部识别系统”，这可以帮助北京收集台湾人民日常生活的数据。这些数据，特别是面部图像，可以与人工智能生成的内容相结合，以躲避社交媒体平台用于识别和删除虚假帐户的检测系统。专家警告说，通过收集详细的个人背景信息，中共可以精确地针对特定个人，例如与军队有联系的人或倾向于特定政党的人，以传播虚假信息和执行认知战行动。
中共的网络渗透策略一直在不断变化。在线操作

【原文 English Original】
Ahead of Taiwan’s Local Elections, China’s Interference Looms Large – The Diplomat
In the Shadow of the Afghanistan-Pakistan Border
Read Like The Diplomat: 2026 Holiday Edition

Taiwan is scheduled to hold local elections, also called the “nine-in-one” elections, on Saturday, November 28. Voters will select city mayors and county magistrates throughout all of Taiwan’s 22 cities and counties. Campaigns focus on local issues, such as housing, welfare, transport, and the environment, rather than Taiwan’s contentious ties with China.
Beijing, nevertheless, has become the elephant in the room due to the increasing threat posed by its attempts to interfere in Taiwan’s elections.
China’s attempts to subvert Taiwan’s local elections and control the island’s domestic politics are not new. Beijing’s strategy to undermine Taiwan’s November elections relies on both intimidation and inducements – delegitimizing Taiwan’s national government by framing its governance as “unstable,” holding military exercises around Taiwan to manipulate public perception, offering campaign financing for candidates supporting unification with China, and subsidizing airfare for Taiwanese businesspeople based in China to return to Taiwan to vote for pro-China candidates.
But Chinese Communist Party (CCP) interference activities in Taiwan’s local elections have become more complex as technology advances. Ahead of the November 28 vote, Taiwanese officials flagged nearly 2,700 China-linked accounts to Meta as part of an information warfare campaign orchestrated by the CCP to sow distrust, discourage voting, and incite public anger against the governing party, the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP). These accounts initially posed as ordinary Taiwanese users sharing snippets of daily life to gain trust, before shifting tactics to launch political attacks and urge voters to “abstain from voting.”
Beijing’s advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-generated deepfakes make “methods of infiltration increasingly sophisticated,” warned Shen Yu-chung, deputy head of Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council (MAC). AI has now become a tool for election manipulation, making it “easier to produce misleading content” and conduct influence operations.
Shen said investigations into China’s election interference show that China has utilized AI to operate “massive facial recognition systems,” which could help Beijing collect data on Taiwanese people’s daily lives. This data, specifically facial images, could be combined with AI-generated content to dodge detection systems used by social media platforms to identify and remove fake accounts. Experts have warned that, by gathering detailed personal background information, the CCP could precisely target specific individuals, such as those with ties to the military or those who lean toward a particular party, for the dissemination of disinformation and the execution of cognitive warfare operations.
The CCP’s online infiltration tactics have been steadily changing. Online operations have gradually shifted from the use of crude, fraudulent identities that can be easily detected to the cultivation of accounts that appear to have legitimate personas. When these personas infiltrate online communities, the artificially generated “buzz” can be mistaken for real public sentiment. This can sway how people think about political issues.
For instance, the deliberate spread of messages like “voting is pointless” or “all candidates are the same” can discourage the electorate’s eagerness to participate. Such tactics will eventually erode public trust in the government and democratic institutions, thus diminishing the credibility of Taiwan’s democratic electoral system.
AI-generated social media campaigns rely primarily on non-political content, such as food, animals, celebrities, or sexually suggestive “clickbait” videos, while interspersing these with political messages that are pro-China or support unification. This technique of using messages anchored in “unrelated, celebrity-focused feeds” but aimed at political purposes was also observed during the U.S. midterm elections.
Certain fake accounts directly attack Taiwan’s ruling party, accusing it of corruption and belittling its governance. Others pose as DPP supporters, “liking” and sharing content from pro-China accounts that otherwise struggle to gain traction, thereby helping to amplify Beijing’s messaging.
To establish credibility, the CCP has also co-opted prominent public figures and influencers to adopt a nuanced strategy of “minor criticism, major backing” – offering minor, superficial critiques of China while advancing narratives that align with CCP policies and interests.
Beyond social media posts, Beijing also hires private investigators and uses public “wanted” lists as a form of cognitive warfare. The China & Taiwan Update, co-published by the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) and the American Enterprise Institute (AEI), revealed that officials from the Shanghai Public Security Bureau recruited a Taiwanese private investigator to surveil two prominent Taiwanese YouTubers and political commentators, “Ba Jiong” (八炯, Wen Tzu-yu) and “Min Nan Lang” (閩南狼, Chen Po-yuan) – both famous for exposing CCP United Front (the CCP department tasked with advancing Chinese influence abroad) tactics targeting Taiwan – while also gathering their personal information.
Furthermore, by subjecting individuals – such as Puma Shen, the DPP’s mayoral candidate for Taipei, online influencers, pro-Taiwan figures, and military personnel – to public “wanted” lists, doxxing, and surveillance, Chinese authorities and affiliated entities have conducted cognitive warfare in Taiwan. This campaign aims to instill a sense of defeatism among the public, fostering the perception that Beijing can infiltrate Taipei and monitor or punish opponents at any time. This “punishment and intimidation” tactic allows Beijing to “create a chilling effect in Taiwan, making voters afraid to openly support particular candidates or parties.”
Taiwan’s media environment is among the freest in Asia, with a diverse and vigorous press, ranking 28th out of 180 countries and territories in Reporters Without Borders’ 2026 World Press Freedom Index. Yet, it remains susceptible to prevalent disinformation campaigns, which usually get more intense during election seasons and evolve in tandem with social media developments. As AI has expanded rapidly and the threat of AI-generated manipulative content targeting candidates is rising, experts in Taiwan have advised the public to “stop, look, and listen” before consuming any information.
To navigate the hazard of influence and interference from China, Taiwan treats foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) as a national threat, shares experience and knowledge with counterparts in the United States, and strikes a balance between respecting civil liberties and strengthening its media ecosystem. In February, Taiwan’s National Security Bureau (NSB) launched its “9-in-1” Election Security Project – a dedicated security taskforce aimed at bolstering Taiwan’s democratic system and ensuring the November electoral process remains free from external interference. The Taiwanese government, legislators, and news outlets have also stepped up efforts to raise public awareness by warning against election disinformation and keeping citizens informed about tactics aimed at disseminating inaccurate information and provoking a societal backlash.
At the same time, Taiwan-based digital investigation and media literacy organizations, such as MyGoPen (麥擱騙), Taiwan FactCheck Center (台灣事實查核中心), Doublethink Lab (台灣民主實驗室), and FactLink (數位素養實驗室), have invested tech expertise and resources to pre-bunk, debunk, track information flows, and expose Chinese AI-generated propaganda and disinformation operations. Additionally, they have provided practical advice that could be used for fact-checking accounts, videos, images, stories, posters, and rumors across multiple platforms, including Threads, TikTok, and Facebook.
Ultimately, bolstering Taiwan’s resilience requires exposing Chinese malign tactics. Cultivating a transparent environment regarding Taiwan’s local elections is a crucial step toward safeguarding a democratic society. Encouraging people to discuss conspiracies they see online is another helpful way to counter information manipulation. Denunciations can help expose Beijing’s pre-election interference and bring greater attention to its influence operations.
On top of that, Taiwan must demonstrate resolve to push back against any forces that use political pressure to sway voters’ decisions. It is only with the unwavering determination to stand “resolute at the ballot box” that the Taiwanese people can sustain their morale in making independent judgments and defending Taiwan’s democracy.

title: Couple arrested for allegedly tampering with Hong Kong passport after viral claim of missing pages
zh_title: 夫妇因涉嫌篡改香港护照因丢失页面而被捕
summary: 香港入境事务处逮捕了一对涉嫌篡改护照的夫妇。这名女子声称页面丢失，法医分析显示未经授权的篡改，随后逮捕了她。香港入境事务处。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。这对年龄分别为27岁和34岁的夫妇周四晚在蓝田被捕，罪名是涉嫌未经合法授权涂改香港护照、使用和管有涂改后的旅行证件以及误导入境官员。负责外部调查的首席入境事务官邓伟业表示
content:
香港入境事务处逮捕了一对涉嫌篡改护照的夫妇。这名女子声称页面丢失，法医分析显示未经授权的篡改，随后逮捕了她。香港入境事务处。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。这对年龄分别为27岁和34岁的夫妇周四晚在蓝田被捕，罪名是涉嫌未经合法授权涂改香港护照、使用和管有涂改后的旅行证件以及误导入境官员。负责外部调查的首席入境事务官邓伟业在周四的新闻发布会上表示，政府法医测试证实护照已被篡改，并且在旅行证件中发现了“纸屑”。 “根据记录，这本护照是2018年签发的，多年来持证人一直用它去各地旅行，没有任何问题。”唐补充道。拒绝入境 这名女子周二在一个疯传的帖子中声称，由于护照缺失页面，她被日本拒绝入境，并被下一趟航班送回香港，随后被捕。她用中文写道：“我的护照是2018年签发的，疫情结束后我用它去韩国、泰国和台湾旅行，没有任何问题。” 2026 年 11 月 24 日，一名 Threads 用户在一篇病毒式帖子中发布了有关其护照缺失页面的信息。照片：kellyyyy3.3，来自 Threads。
她声称，当她周一试图进入日本时，边境官员发现她的护照第15页至第18页缺失。她说，被拒绝入境导致她在酒店预订和航班方面遭受经济损失。她还声称，在她返回香港后，一名入境官员告诉她，缺失的页面是由于“制造缺陷”造成的，她可以寻求赔偿。不排除进一步逮捕的可能性 唐周四表示，当这名女子前往移民总部发表声明时，她改变了自己的说法，并表示不是移民官员承认她护照上缺少几页。唐说，移民官员对她的说法产生了怀疑，展开了调查，后来将护照送到政府法医实验室进行检查。虽然实验室测试证实护照已被篡改，但唐表示，调查人员仍在努力确定旅行证件被篡改的原因和方式。他不排除进一步逮捕的可能性。邓警告说，根据香港的《入境条例》，未经合法授权更改旅行证件属严重罪行，最高可被罚款15万港元和监禁14年。他说，教唆犯罪的人同样有罪。同时，误导入境官员可被处以最高 10,000 港元罚款和六个月监禁。
他说，护照是重要文件，敦促公众妥善保管护照，不要进行未经授权的涂改。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong’s Immigration Department has arrested a couple for allegedly tampering with a passport. The arrests came after the woman claimed pages were missing, only for forensic analysis to show an unauthorised alteration had been made. Hong Kong Immigration Department. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The couple, aged 27 and 34, were arrested on Thursday night in Lam Tin on suspicion of altering a Hong Kong passport without lawful authority, using and possessing the altered travel document, and misleading immigration officers. Tang Wai-yip, chief immigration officer for outside investigation, told a press conference on Thursday that government forensic tests confirmed that the passport had been tampered with and that “paper scraps” were found inside the travel document. “According to records, this passport was issued in 2018, and its holder had been using it to travel to various places over the years without any issue,” Tang added. Denial of entry The arrests came after the woman claimed in a viral Threads post on Tuesday that she had been denied entry to Japan and sent back to Hong Kong on the next flight due to missing pages in her passport. “My passport was issued in 2018 and I have used it to travel to Korea, Thailand and Taiwan after the pandemic without a problem,” she wrote in Chinese. A Threads user posts about missing pages in her passport in a viral post on November 24, 2026. Photo: kellyyyy3.3, via Threads. She claimed that when she tried to enter Japan on Monday, border officers found that pages 15 to 18 were missing from her passport. The denied entry had caused her financial losses on hotel bookings and flights, she said. She also claimed that, upon her return to Hong Kong, an immigration officer told her the missing pages were due to a “manufacturing defect” and that she could seek compensation. Further arrests not ruled out Tang said on Thursday that, when the woman went to the Immigration Headquarters to give a statement, she altered her claim and said that it was not an immigration officer who acknowledged the missing pages in her passport. Tang said immigration officers grew suspicious about her claim, launched an investigation and later sent the passport to a government forensic lab for examination. While lab tests confirmed that the passport had been altered, Tang said investigators were still working to determine why and how the travel document was tampered with. He did not rule out further arrests. Tang warned that, under the city’s Immigration Ordinance, altering a travel document without lawful authority is a serious offence that carries a maximum penalty of a HK$150,000 fine and 14 years in jail. People who abet an offence are equally culpable, he said. Meanwhile, misleading an immigration officer can be punished by up to a HK$10,000 fine and six months in jail. He said a passport is an important document, urging members of the public to keep it safe and refrain from making unauthorised alterations.

title: Hong Kong gov’t defends moving Wang Fuk Court fire tributes on first anniversary of deadly blaze

summary: 政府表示，为去年宏福阁致命火灾的遇难者献花的地点已于周四迁移，以便为更多哀悼者腾出空间。 2026 年 11 月 26 日晚，民众安全服务人员在大埔宏福苑附近重新摆放鲜花，一年前，宏福苑发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港人日日夜夜聚集在烧焦的大埔住宅区对面的广福休憩处，此时正好是 168 人在这场悲惨大火中丧生的一年之后。民众安全服务队人员重新布置花艺
content:
政府表示，为去年宏福阁致命火灾的遇难者献花的地点已于周四迁移，以便为更多哀悼者腾出空间。 2026 年 11 月 26 日晚，民众安全服务人员在大埔宏福苑附近重新摆放鲜花，一年前，宏福苑发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港人日日夜夜聚集在烧焦的大埔住宅区对面的广福休憩处，此时正好是 168 人在这场悲惨大火中丧生的一年之后。 2026 年 11 月 26 日晚，民众安全服务人员在大埔宏福苑附近重新摆放鲜花，一年前，宏福苑发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。人们经常看到民众安全服务人员在搬运鲜花，一些哀悼者似乎对他们的匆忙感到愤怒。其他人则开始亲自搬运贡品。 2026 年 11 月 26 日晚，民众安全服务人员在大埔宏福苑附近重新摆放鲜花，一年前，宏福苑发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四晚间的一份政府声明表示，官员们正在寻求“妥善保存各部门的哀悼”。 2026 年 11 月 26 日晚，民众安全服务人员在大埔宏福苑附近重新摆放鲜花，一年前，宏福苑发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
政府发言人表示，悼念活动将逐步转移至宗教场所：“此前，考虑到现场放置了大量花束，且傍晚可能会有更多人抵达，部分花束和悼念物品暂时放在塑料盒内，移至附近草坪，以便腾出更多空间，让市民继续献花表达哀悼，确保每一份善意的举动都得到尊重。” 2026 年 11 月 26 日晚，哀悼者聚集在大埔宏福苑附近，一年前，宏福苑发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。早些时候，当局排除了举办官方纪念活动的可能性。 2026 年 11 月 26 日，哀悼者聚集在大埔宏福苑附近，一年前，宏福苑发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四，在安全负责人警告不要进行可能构成“煽动叛乱”的行为后，警方在大埔遗址周围保持低调。安全负责人邓克里斯（Chris Tang）表示，只要合法，纪念活动都是允许的，但警告说，可能有人别有用心地试图“劫持”活动。

【原文 English Original】
Floral tributes for the victims of last year’s deadly Wang Fuk Court fire were relocated on Thursday to make room for more mourners, the government has said. Civil Aid Service personnel rearrange floral tributes near to Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on the evening of November 26, 2026, one year after a blaze at the complex left 168 people dead. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Hongkongers gathered around Kwong Fuk Sitting-out Area , opposite the charred Tai Po housing estate, throughout the day and evening, exactly a year after 168 people died in the tragic blaze. Civil Aid Service personnel rearrange floral tributes near to Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on the evening of November 26, 2026, one year after a blaze at the complex left 168 people dead. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Civil Aid Service officers were regularly seen moving flowers, with some mourners appearing angered by their haste. Others took to moving the tributes themselves . Civil Aid Service personnel rearrange floral tributes near to Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on the evening of November 26, 2026, one year after a blaze at the complex left 168 people dead. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A government statement late on Thursday said the officers were seeking to “properly preserve the condolences from various sectors.” Civil Aid Service personnel rearrange floral tributes near to Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on the evening of November 26, 2026, one year after a blaze at the complex left 168 people dead. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A government spokesperson said the tributes would be progressively relocated to religious venues: “Earlier, considering that a large number of bouquets had been placed at the scene and there might be more people arriving in the evening, some bouquets and mourning items were temporarily placed in plastic boxes and moved to the lawn nearby in order to vacate more space for members of the public to continue laying bouquets to express their condolences, ensuring that every gesture of goodwill is respected.” Mourners gather near Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on the evening of November 26, 2026, one year after a blaze at the complex left 168 people dead. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Earlier, the authorities ruled out hosting an official commemoration. Mourners gather near Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on November 26, 2026, one year after a blaze at the complex left 168 people dead. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Police maintained a low-key presence around the Tai Po site on Thursday, after the security chief warned against acts that may amount to “sedition.” Security chief Chris Tang said memorial events are permitted as long as they are lawful, but warned that there might be people who seek to “hijack” the event with ulterior motives.

title: From declaration to feasibility: America, China, Russia and the future of nuclear talks
zh_title: 从宣言到可行性：美国、中国、俄罗斯和核谈判的未来
summary: 封面图片：图片联盟/共同社 11 月 19 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在深圳与中国领导人习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京会面后承认，“一旦拥有核武器，就很难不拥有核武器”。这一困难体现在他们的“共同和平宣言”中关于这一主题的谦虚和不置可否的语言，三位领导人重申了里根-戈尔巴乔夫的声明，即“核战争不可能获胜，也决不能打”，并同意“就减少核风险和防止核战争爆发进行对话”。
content:
封面图片：图片联盟/共同社 11 月 19 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在深圳与中国领导人习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京会面后承认，“一旦拥有核武器，就很难不拥有核武器”。这一困难体现在他们的“共同和平宣言”中关于这一主题的谦虚和不置可否的语言，三位领导人重申了里根-戈尔巴乔夫的声明，即“核战争不可能获胜，也决不能打”，并同意“就减少核风险和防止核武器扩散进行对话”。这并不完全是特朗普在峰会前推动的“无核化”谈判。尽管如此，世界三大核大国罕见的共同语言可能有助于为更实质性的接触奠定一些政治基础。随着中国扩大其核武库以及所有三个国家都进行核现代化，就避免误解和误判的措施达成三边协议将符合每个人的利益。存在与声明中的语言相匹配的合理步骤。然而，正如特朗普所发现的那样，中国需要大量说服才能放弃其对与美国签署核协议的传统反对态度。欧洲两个拥核国家英国和法国也不愿参与，但这样做可能有助于让中国加入。从小事做起 这一切来得太早了。
《新削减战略武器条约》（New START）对美国和俄罗斯的战略核力量设定了具有约束力的限制，该条约于 2026 年 2 月到期，尽管两国继续实施冷战期间谈判达成的一系列核风险削减措施。北京与莫斯科签署的此类协议少得多，与华盛顿签署的此类协议也几乎没有。除了其内在价值外，旨在减少核风险的新三边协议将有助于履行三个国家在《核不扩散条约》下的义务，即“承诺就停止核军备竞赛的有效措施进行谈判……”。更可行的短期选择之一是三边导弹发射前通知（PLN）协议，该协议通过在使用某些导弹和太空运载火箭（SLV）之前告知对方，帮助各国避免误解和误判。美国和俄罗斯有这样的协议，中国和俄罗斯也有这样的协议。尽管北京方面驳斥了承诺遵守任何新的PLN协议的呼吁，但它还是主动向美国和其他国家通报了其于2024年和2026年两次向太平洋进行潜射弹道导弹的试验，这表明它看到了这项措施的价值。
为了确保潜在的PLN快速、安全地到达，并提供危机沟通渠道，中国还可以同意建立一个相当于美国和俄罗斯已有的核风险降低中心的国家级中心。这些中心昼夜不停地运作，例如在2001年9月11日被用来向克里姆林宫领导人保证美国的防御姿态并非针对俄罗斯。未来，三方可能会更加雄心勃勃地同意限制可供使用的洲际导弹和轰炸机的数量。正如军控学者杰弗里·刘易斯 (Jeffrey Lewis) 指出的那样，中国不太可能突破已过期的《削减战略武器条约》中规定的 700 辆部署车辆的限制，即使要装载

【原文 English Original】
Cover image: picture alliance / Kyodo “Once you have the nuclear weapons, it’s very hard to not have them,” conceded US president Donald Trump after his meeting in Shenzhen with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian president Vladimir Putin on November 19th. This difficulty was reflected in the modest and non-committal language on the topic in their “ joint declaration towards peace ”, with the three leaders reaffirming the Reagan-Gorbachev statement that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought” and agreeing to “conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons”. This was not quite the “denuclearisation” talks that Trump had pushed for in the run-up to the summit. Nevertheless, the rare joint language from the world’s three biggest nuclear powers could help lay some political foundations for more substantial engagement. As China expands its arsenal and all three countries undertake nuclear modernisation, trilateral agreements on measures to avoid misperception and miscalculation would be in everyone’s interest. Plausible steps exist to match the language in the declaration. Yet, as Trump has found, it will take a lot of persuasion for China to drop its traditional opposition to nuclear agreements with America. Europe’s two nuclear-armed states, Britain and France, will also be reluctant to participate—but doing so may help get China on board. Starting small This would not come a moment too soon. The New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START), which set binding limits on American and Russian strategic nuclear forces, expired in February 2026, though the two countries continue to implement a range of nuclear-risk reduction measures they negotiated during the cold war. Beijing has far fewer such agreements with Moscow and barely any with Washington. Besides their intrinsic value, new trilateral agreements to reduce nuclear risk would constitute progress towards fulfilling the three countries’ obligation under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty to “undertake to pursue negotiations… on effective measures relating to cessation of the nuclear arms race”. Among the more feasible short-term options is a trilateral missile pre-launch notification (PLN) agreement, which helps states avoid misperception and miscalculation by telling each other ahead of their use of certain missiles and space-launch vehicles (SLV). America and Russia have such an agreement, so do China and Russia. Even though Beijing has rebuked calls to commit to any new PLN agreements, it voluntarily pre-notified America and other countries of its two tests of submarine-launched ballistic missiles into the Pacific Ocean in 2024 and 2026, suggesting it sees value in the measure.   To ensure potential PLNs arrive quickly and securely, and to provide a channel for crisis communications, China could also agree to establish a national equivalent of the nuclear risk reduction centres that already exist in the US and Russia. These centres operate around the clock, and were used, for example, on September 11th 2001 to reassure leaders in the Kremlin that America’s defensive posture was not aimed at Russia. In the future, and far more ambitiously, the three parties could agree to limit the numbers of intercontinental missiles and bombers that are ready for use. As arms-control scholar Jeffrey Lewis notes , China is unlikely to cross the limit of 700 deployed vehicles specified in the expired START, even if it were to load all of its launchers with missiles. As such, a voluntary trilateral commitment to observing this limit could be palatable to the country. Without a formal verification system, however, such an agreement could become unstable. The missing side of the triangle Measures like these could help Trump move closer to fulfilling his longstanding arms-control ambitions. During his first term, he tried unsuccessfully to bring China into trilateral arms-control talks. More recently, citing China’s nuclear build-up, second Trump administration officials once again called for multilateral talks with a view to negotiating a successor to New START. The second administration’s engagement with China on nuclear-risk reduction constitutes a continuation of the Biden agenda . US and Chinese delegations met in November 2023 for what China termed “consultations” on arms control and non-proliferation, where the US side pushed for greater Chinese nuclear transparency and efforts to reduce strategic risks. These talks reportedly yielded little progress and China later suspended them citing US arms sales to Taiwan. Chinese officials have repeatedly pointed to the smaller size of China’s nuclear arsenal relative to those of America and Russia, and the resulting “special and primary responsibilities” of the other two powers to reduce their arsenals first But Beijing has also long maintained a more fundamental aversion to nuclear arms control with Washington. Chinese officials have repeatedly pointed to the smaller size of China’s nuclear arsenal relative to those of America and Russia, and the resulting “special and primary responsibilities” of the other two powers to reduce their arsenals first. China’s 2025 white paper on arms control acknowledges its interest in nuclear risk reduction but its answer to the challenge has been a proposal for adoption of China’s policy of nuclear no-first-use across the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, which has been criticised as unenforceable and potentially counterproductive. Where Europe comes in The nuclear point in the Shenzhen declaration does not call for the inclusion of Britain and France (the other two permanent Security Council members) in risk-reduction dialogue. But Russian officials have previously pushed for their inclusion in any multilateral arms-control talks. Like China, however, the two European powers have been historically reluctant to agree to any such talks outside the existing process among the five permanent members, mainly because of their comparatively smaller nuclear arsenals. In the coming years, even accounting for the announced increases in both the British and the French arsenals, China’s projected nuclear force will far surpass both. In addition, a (seemingly well-founded ) fear for Europeans will be whether any US engagement on arms control with Russia comes at the cost of concessions on Ukraine. Still, Britain and France joining the measures outlined above would be relatively low-cost and a net positive, and could perhaps help bring China on board. Britain and France already pre-notify their missile and SLV launches voluntarily through the Hague Code of Conduct against Ballistic Missile Proliferation mechanism . Establishing risk reduction centres in Europe would bring a new secure crisis-communications channel, which would be especially useful given tensions with Russia. A limit on missiles and launchers would not meaningfully constrain the two European countries because of differences in their force structures. But it would still be unlikely to prove politically acceptable to them, at least in the short term. *** With no more formal limits on US and Russian strategic arsenals, the imperative to pursue nuclear risk-reduction measures is only intensifying. But it will indeed be “very hard” to turn political declarations into agreements, and any future dialogue may well get stuck on the countries’ varying perceptions of nuclear responsibilities and the origins of nuclear risk. Still, the Trump administration is highly motivated to pursue arms control, and—despite the symbolism and subtext of the Shenzhen meeting—this aspect of the resulting declaration may ultimately benefit Europeans, who also have an interest in persuading China to join trilateral measures. 这是《大西洋日报》的一个版本，是一份时事通讯，可引导您了解当天最大的故事，帮助您发现新想法，并推荐最好的文化。在这里注册。更新于下午 2:05美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 27 日 间谍，至少目前，重新回到公众视野：罗伯特·帕丁森 (Robert Pattinson) 是新的詹姆斯·邦德 (James Bond)——对此我已经说了所有我要说的话——而 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 承认与所谓的中国情报资产有亲密关系，所以我们再次考虑间谍活动。但冷战结束后，除了一些值得注意的例外，包括永恒的007系列，娱乐业大部分对间谍失去了兴趣。在电视上，他们只在偶尔的节目中重新出现，比如精彩的《慢马》，这是一部关于一群敬业但往往无能的军情五处特工的连续剧。这太糟糕了，因为美国文化中间谍无处不在的日子真是太棒了。流行间谍热潮的鼎盛时期是从 20 世纪 60 年代初到 70 年代中期。其中一些产品非常值得重新审视，不仅作为娱乐，而且作为美国在对抗克里姆林宫的斗争中领导自由世界的时代的迷人文化艺术品。 （鉴于美国目前的外交政策状况，你可以想象我为什么会怀念这样的时代。）在那段间谍热潮中，美国文化主要从间谍惊悚片的祖国英国进口产品。
（早在 1954 年，哥伦比亚广播公司就播出了第一部改编自伊恩·弗莱明小说的电视剧，这是《皇家赌场》的一个版本，主角是美国詹姆斯·邦德（名字叫吉米·邦德，我没骗你），由巴里·纳尔逊饰演。）但对间谍的文化迷恋在 20 世纪 60 年代中期真正兴起，此时肖恩·康纳利 (Sean Connery) 将 007 确立为国际电影英雄。为什么我们如此迷恋间谍活动在摇摆的 60 年代？冷战显然与此有很大关系。美国人第一次面对敌人的超级大国，但在原子时代，战争的代价太高，他们不得不在暗处与对手作战。这个间谍时代也是解放时代风气的产物。尤其是电影，被允许变得更加血腥，间谍片很快就以英俊的流氓欢快地参与大量的性和暴力为特色。邦德和他的同事们代表了一种刚毅和睿智的新形象，摆脱了紧张的 20 世纪 50 年代的束缚。但他们也公然拒绝 60 年代更为进步的变革。女权主义？刑事权利？忘了它。这些新间谍有执照可以杀人，可以像玩具一样使用女人，可以像疯子一样开车，可以赌博，可以喝酒，可以做任何一个有男子气概的男人认为拯救世界所必需的事情。英国间谍剧更注重欧洲间谍活动的现实，通常比好莱坞化的邦德电影更加坚韧、不那么浮华。然而，其中一些在出口到更狂热的美国观众面前时变得性感起来。
例如，从 1960 年到 1961 年，帕特里克·麦高汉 (Patrick McGoohan) 在《危险人》(Danger Man) 中扮演约翰·德雷克 (John Drake)，他是一名为某个模糊的北约情报机构工作的特工。随着邦德热潮的蔓延，该系列于 1964 年重新推出，失去了一些黑色电影元素，取而代之的是更多 007 的影响。德雷克被调到英国情报部门，该节目被重新命名为美国辛迪加的秘密特工，约翰尼·里弗斯演唱了一首新的主题曲，成为 60 年代的经典。 《特工》于 1967 年底结束拍摄后，麦高汉于 1968 年推出了《囚徒》，这是一部间谍小说（间谍与间谍小说）。

【原文 English Original】
This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. Updated at 2:05 p.m. ET on November 27, 2026 Spies, at least for now, are back in the public eye: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond—I’ve said all I’ll say on that — and the Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang, confessed to canoodling with an alleged Chinese-intelligence asset, so we’re thinking about espionage again. But after the Cold War, with a few notable exceptions, including the eternal 007 series, the entertainment industry lost interest in spies for the most part. On television, they have reemerged only in occasional treats such as the wonderful Slow Horses , a series about a bunch of dedicated but often incompetent MI5 operatives. And that’s too bad, because the days when spies were everywhere in American culture were a blast. The heyday of pop-spy mania ran from the early 1960s to about the mid-1970s. Some of these offerings are well worth revisiting, not only as entertainment but also as fascinating cultural artifacts of an era when America was leading the free world in the fight against the Kremlin. (Given the current state of U.S. foreign policy , you can imagine why I am nostalgic for such times.) During that spy craze, American culture mostly imported products from the spy-thriller mother country, the United Kingdom. (As early as 1954, CBS ran the first television adaptation of an Ian Fleming novel, a version of Casino Royale that features an American James Bond—named Jimmy Bond, I kid you not—played by Barry Nelson.) But the cultural obsession with spies really took off in the mid-1960s, by which point Sean Connery had established 007 as an international film hero. Why were we so infatuated with espionage during the swingin’ ’60s? The Cold War obviously had a lot to do with it. Americans for the first time faced an enemy superpower, but in the atomic age, when the price of war was too high, they had to fight their opponents in the shadows. This era of spies was also a product of the liberated mores of the times. Movies, especially, were allowed to be racier, and spy flicks soon featured handsome cads cheerfully engaging in plenty of sex and violence. Bond and his colleagues represented a new image of virility and savoir faire, freed from the uptight 1950s. But they also defiantly rejected the more progressive changes of the ’60s. Feminism? Criminal rights? Forget it. These new spies had a license to kill, to use women like toys, to drive like maniacs, to gamble, to drink, and to do anything else a manly man thought was necessary to save the world. British spy shows, more grounded in the reality of European espionage, were generally grittier and less flashy than the Hollywood-ized Bond movies. Some of them, however, were sexed up when exported to more gung-ho U.S. viewers. From 1960 to 1961, for example, Patrick McGoohan played John Drake on Danger Man , an agent who works for some nebulous NATO intelligence agency. As Bond mania grew, the series was revived in 1964, losing some of its film-noir elements in favor of more 007 influences. Drake was moved over to British intelligence, the show was retitled Secret Agent for U.S. syndication, and Johnny Rivers performed a new theme song that became a ’60s classic. After Secret Agent ended its run in late 1967, McGoohan followed it up in 1968 with The Prisoner , a kind of spy-fi (spy-and-science-fiction mash-up) series about an agent who tries to retire and is sent to a secret halfway house for wayward spooks. The series, which is still a cult favorite, calls his character only “Number Six”—but we all knew it was Drake. Likewise, when The Avengers premiered in the U.K. in 1961, it was mostly a pedestrian private-eye show. But soon, it turned into a spy-fi romp, with John Steed (Patrick Macnee) and his female colleague Mrs. Gale (Honor Blackman) as the agents who served Queen and country. In a case of spy-fiction cross-pollination, Blackman left to play Pussy Galore in Goldfinger , the 007 adventure about a plot to blow up America’s gold reserves in Kentucky. After Diana Rigg arrived as Steed’s new partner, Emma Peel, the show winked at the audience: In a 1965 episode, she hands Steed his mail, including a Christmas card from Gale. “How nice of her to remember me,” Steed says. “What can she be doing in Fort Knox?” The next year, the series was snapped up by America’s ABC, and Rigg, in her leather catsuits , and Macnee, in his bowler hat and Pierre Cardin suits, became spy-fiction icons. Spies quickly flooded U.S. television screens after what must have been an endless stream of high-concept pitches: “James Bond, but in the old American West as a Secret Service agent, against supervillains with names such as Dr. Loveless and Count Manzeppi.” ( The Wild Wild West .) “James Bond, but as an incompetent boob in a comedy.” ( Get Smart! ) “James Bond, but he’s a Black American tennis coach.” ( I Spy . The series’ co-star, Bill Cosby, now lives in shame, but back in 1965, it was groundbreaking to get Americans to accept a Black man as a hero instead of a sidekick.) The Man From U.N.C.L.E. , a show that first hit TV screens in 1964, was spy-fi from the start. Not only was it derived from the Bond successes, but Fleming reportedly helped develop an early pitch for the show; U.N.C.L.E. Agent Napoleon Solo was even named for a Bond character. Solo and his Soviet partner, Ilya Kuriakin, work for U.N.C.L.E., a kind of international superagency that battles the psychos from T.H.R.U.S.H., an obvious stand-in for Fleming’s baddies, SPECTRE. ( U.N.C.L.E. producers came up with these names because they sounded hip; they filled in what the acronyms meant later.) The Americans had their own homegrown spies, too. In 1966, Mission: Impossible premiered on CBS featuring a team of operatives so secret that the U.S. government hides their instructions on a tape recorder in a telephone booth or a vending machine and other wacky places, after which the tape self-destructs into a hissing, smoky mess. (The Tom Cruise Mission: Impossible reboots, much like the Jason Bourne movies, are fine as generic action flicks, but for some Cold War spy fun, treat yourself to the original series.) Even cartoons got in on the act. Everyone remembers Bullwinkle’s enemies, Boris and Natasha, and you might remember Secret Squirrel, but do you remember Cool McCool, a 1966 Saturday-morning secret agent drummed up by Bob Kane, a co-creator of Batman? Probably not, and that’s fine, because Cool McCool is terrible. (But not as terrible as “Lancelot Link, Secret Chimp” a 1970 spy spoof for kids that had a cast of, yes, live chimpanzees.) Eventually, the spy craze got out of hand, as all fads do. James Coburn and Dean Martin both signed up for spy spoofs, and saw varying results: Coburn’s two outings as Derek Flint, an agent of Z.O.W.I.E. (don’t ask), are fine, but Martin’s Matt Helm movies are unwatchable—at least they provided some raw material for Mike Myers when he created Austin Powers . After the 1960s, the cynical ’70s were upon us, and the fascination with spies dissipated. Events such as Watergate made government spookery seem a lot less admirable; in 1975, a congressional committee outed a lot of the CIA’s uglier tricks to the American public. Bond movies thrived, but 007 had much of the spy-genre field to himself at the theaters and on television. It was a great ride, and you can catch many of these programs on stations that run vintage TV shows, random YouTube channels , or a few streaming platforms. That’s your assignment over this holiday weekend, Agent Reader, and remember: This newsletter will self-destruct in five seconds. Graham’s tumultuous journey across the Atlantic on a wind-powered cargo ship Orwell has become what he despised, Stephen Marche argues. Here comes Santa Claude, Evening Read Black Friday shoppers at a Toys “R” Us in Fort Worth, Texas, in 2009 Tom Pennington / Getty Black Friday Nostalgia ( From 2025 ) By Annie Joy Williams Every Thanksgiving when I was growing up, my family held a Wacky Tacky Talent Show so needlessly competitive that at least one kid inevitably cried. And on the same special tablecloth we used every year, we would list with a felt-tip marker what we were most grateful for: I’d write my dog and American Girl doll; my mother would write me and my sisters; my college-aged cousin would write her boyfriend du jour (there were many crossed-out names on the fabric). Then I would sit down with a pile of buttered mashed potatoes and wait for midnight, when the real holiday would begin, the one that made my mini shopaholic’s heart beam: Black Friday. The following is a summary of major ship movements and exercises in the Western Pacific over the last week. In Singapore Wasp-class amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) pulls in to Commander, Fleet Activities, Yokosuka, Japan, Oct. 26, 2026. US Navy photo Amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) and amphibious transport dock USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26) departed Tuesday from Sembawang, Singapore, according to local ship spotters and AIS data. The two amphibious ships, embarked with elements of the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, sailed into the Malacca Strait toward the Indian Ocean. Makin Island and John P. Murtha , with amphibious transport dock USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and the embarked 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, form the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group (ARG). Anchorage remains docked at Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka (CFAY), Japan. In the South China Sea Philippine Coast Guard patrol vessel BRP Cabra (MRRV-4409) directs a Chinese Maritime Militia CMMV to leave the vicinity of the Philippines’ Panata Island on Nov. 23, 2026. Philippine Coast Guard image On Monday, Chinese Maritime Militia CMMV 11098 and CMMV 11086 were involved in a dangerous maneuver incident with Philippine Coast Guard patrol vessel BRP Cabra (MRRV-4409) in the vicinity of the Philippines’ Panata Island, located within the Spratly Islands chain. PCG spokesperson Rear Adm. Jay Tarriela said that CMMV 11098 and CMMV 11086 were anchored approximately 5.1 and 5.2 nautical miles, respectively, from Panata Island, within the Philippine’s territorial sea. Cabra issued radio challenges directing both vessels to leave. CMMV 11086 weighed anchor and headed directly toward the starboard quarter of Cabra at about 10 knots, closing to approximately 200 yards. The PCG ship took evasive action and avoided a possible collision. The same CMMV then attempted to close in on the Cabra’s Rigid Hull Inflatable Boat, which had eight PCG personnel onboard and likewise evaded safely. No injury or damage was sustained. Both CMMVs subsequently moved away from Panata Island. China Coast Guard ship 4109 was also monitored in the vicinity during the operation. Cabra continues monitoring the Chinese ships, said Tarriela. In the Sulu Sea A Philippine Navy AW109 Helicopter conducts vertical replenishment on BRP Diego Silang (FFG7) during the 3rd Philippines-France Bilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity (MCA) in the Sulu Sea on November 21, 2026. Philippine Navy photo The Armed Forces of the Philippines and the French Armed Forces carried out the third bilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity (MCA) in the Sulu Sea from Nov. 20 to Sunday . French Navy frigate FS Vendémiaire (F734) and its embarked Dauphin helicopter conducted a series of drills with Philippine Navy frigate BRP Diego Silang (FFG7) and its embarked AW109 helicopter, Philippine Coast Guard patrol vessel BRP Sarangani (MRRV-6177), a Philippine Air Force (PAF) C-208B Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance aircraft and PAF S-70i Blackhawk helicopters. Exercise activities included communications exercises, personnel exchanges, cross-deck vertical replenishment, division tactics and officer-of-the-watch maneuvers and cross Visit, Board, Search, and Seizure exercises. Vendémiaire , based in Noumea, New Caledonia, is on deployment under Mission Himantura, the French Navy’s annual operational deployment in the Asia-Pacific region. On Monday , Vendémiaire docked in Davao City for a port visit. In Surabaya, Indonesia U.S. Navy Capt. Alfonza White, right, chief of staff, Commander, Task Force (CTF) 76 and Indonesian Navy First Admiral Endra Hartono, Commander of Naval Combat Task Group 2nd Fleet Command conduct a press conference with local media during Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Indonesia 2026 in Surabaya, Indonesia, Nov. 25, 2026. US Navy photo U.S. 7th Fleet and the Indonesian Navy commenced the 32nd iteration of Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Indonesia on Wednesday in Surabaya, Indonesia. The at-sea phase will involve anti-submarine warfare drills, mine countermeasures best practices and surface action group coordination by U.S. Navy mine countermeasures ship USS Warrior (MCM-10), a P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft from CTF-72. Also participating are Indonesian Navy corvettes KRI Diponegoro (365), KRI Sultan Iskandar Muda (367) and KRI Frans Kaisiepo (368) and mine countermeasures ships KRI Pulau Fani (731) and KRI Pulau Fanildo (732). In Ream Port, Cambodia The People’s Liberation Army Ground Force deployed tanks and armored fighting vehicles for the bilateral Golden Dragon 2026 exercise at Cambodia-China Ream Port Joint Support and Training Center, which kicked off Nov. 25, 2026. PLA photo China and Cambodia on Wednesday kicked off the bilateral Golden Dragon 2026 exercise at Cambodia-China Ream Port Joint Support and Training Center. The eighth iteration of the bilateral exercise will run until Dec. 9, totalling 15 days covering a wide range of land, sea and air drills. The exercise involves around 1,600 Cambodian and 1,300 Chinese military personnel. The People’s Liberation Army Ground Force has deployed tanks and armoured fighting vehicles for the drills while the People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) has deployed three ships – frigate CNS Xuchang (536) amphibious transport dock CNS Kunlunshan (998) and fleet oiler CNS Wulunguhu (893). In the Gulf of Tonkin A joint patrol fleet of Chinese and Vietnamese vessels conducted a joint search and rescue exercise on Nov. 20-21. PLA photo China and Vietnam carried out the 41st joint patrol in the Gulf of Tonkin from Nov. 20 to Saturday. The patrol was conducted by People’s Liberation Army Navy corvettes CNS Wuzhou (626) and CNS Enshi (627) and Vietnam Coast Guard patrol vessels Ship 8002 and Ship 8004. The joint patrol spanned 32 hours and covered a total distance of 351 nautical miles. During the patrol, the two countries conducted a search and rescue exercise. In Saipan Submarine tender USS Frank Cable (AS-40) pulled into Saipan on Saturday for a port visit. A U.S. Navy news release said the submarine tender’s visit was part of an ongoing effort with leaders to bring more U.S. Navy ship visits to the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). “The visit reflects continued collaboration between Joint Region Marianas and the Office of the Governor, Commonwealth Bureau of Military Affairs, Marianas Visitors Authority, and Saipan Chamber of Commerce, who have expressed interest in hosting Navy ships more often,” reads the release. In Yokosuka, Japan Royal Canadian Navy frigate HMCS Regina (FFH334) departed on Monday from Yokosuka, according to local ship spotters. Regina arrived Nov. 19 for a port visit and is on deployment under Operation Horizon and Operation Neon, the Canadian Armed Forces’ forward presence deployment to the Indo-Pacific and surveillance and monitoring operations on North Korean maritime sanctions violations. The Royal Canadian frigate carried out Operation Neon from late September to early November . U.S. sailors assigned to San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock ship USS Anchorage (LPD-23) prepare to moor the ship during sea and anchor detail as the ship pulls into Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka, Japan, Oct. 26, 2026. US Navy photo Anchorage, of the Makin Island ARG, remains docked at Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka (CFAY), Japan. The amphibious transport dock arrived there Nov. 16. In the Osumi Strait PLAN cruiser CNS Lhasa (102), destroyer CNS Xining (117), frigate CNS Yanchang (546) and fleet oiler CNS Kekexilihu (903) on Nov. 24, 2026, near the Osumi Strait. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Tuesday at 4 a.m. local time, PLAN cruiser CNS Lhasa (102), destroyer CNS Xining (117), frigate CNS Yanchang (546) and fleet oiler CNS Kekexilihu (903) were sighted sailing northwest 70 kilometers – 44 miles – southeast of Cape Toi. The four PLAN ships then sailed west through the Osumi Strait, which separates Kyushu from Tanegashima Island to enter the East China Sea. The four ships transited on Oct. 27 southeast through the Miyako Strait to enter the Philippine Sea, according to Japan’s Joint Staff Office. Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force JS Mikuma (FFM-4) and a JMSDF P-1 Maritime Patrol Aircraft shadowed the PLAN ships. In the Sea of Japan A Russian Tu-160 bomber over the Sea of Japan on Nov. 24, 2026. Russian state media image Two Russian Tu-160 bombers escorted by Su-35 and Su-30sm fighter aircraft carried out a 10-hour flight over the Sea of Japan on Tuesday, prompting scrambles by South Korea as they entered the Korean Air Defense Identification Zone. “At certain stages of the route, the aircraft were escorted by foreign fighter jets. Crews of long-range aviation regularly conduct flights over the neutral waters of the Arctic, the North Atlantic, the Pacific Ocean, Black and Baltic seas. All Russian Aerospace Forces aircraft flights are carried out in strict compliance with international rules on the use of airspace,” reads a Russian Ministry of Defense news release. Seoul scrambled fighters when the Russian aircraft appeared close to entering territorial airspace over Ulleung Island, though the Russian aircraft did not violate territorial airspace. The South Korean Ministry of National Defense issued a protest to the Russian Defense Attache in Seoul over the incident. Russia’s embassy in Seoul issued a statement through state media Tass on the same day. “As in previous cases of this kind, clarifications were provided that Russia acts in compliance with international law. It was emphasized that Seoul had unilaterally established the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone, which means this does not impose any legal obligations on aircraft from other countries,” reads the Russian statement. In the East China Sea A Chinese Y-9 over the East China Sea on Nov. 25, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Wednesday, a Chinese Y-9 Electronic Intelligence aircraft flew in from China to as far as the area south of the Danjo Islands over the East China Sea, before turning around and heading back toward China. Also on Wednesday, a Chinese TB-001 reconnaissance/attack Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (TB-001) flew in from China and then altered its course near the Danjo Islands and subsequently flew back toward China. In response to both flights, the Japan Air Self-Defense Force scrambled fighter jets. This post was written by Dzirhan Mahadzir.
