Philippines renews nuclear ambitions after Bataan delay | The Straits Times
Philippines renews nuclear push, 40 years after mothballing Bataan plant
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Completed in 1984, the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant was left idle in 1986, the year a popular uprising toppled Ferdinand Marcos Sr’s dictatorship.
Published Nov 28, 2026, 12:30 PM
Updated Nov 28, 2026, 12:44 PM
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr has renewed the Philippines' push for nuclear power, with the government exploring foreign technologies and identifying seven potential sites across five provinces.
The mothballed Bataan Nuclear Power Plant remains a possible candidate for rehabilitation, but its ageing infrastructure, safety concerns and the cost of bringing it up to modern standards pose significant challenges.
The country still needs to complete key regulatory, emergency-response and radioactive-waste arrangements, while local activists remain opposed to the plant's revival.
BATAAN, Philippines – Time seems to have stood still inside the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant (BNPP), where a vision of the Philippines’ energy future has lain dormant for four decades.
Some of the machinery remains wrapped in the plastic it came in, while much of the original paintwork remains intact. Elsewhere, rust has crept over metal stairways and cobwebs have gathered, marking the passage of time in a facility that has never generated electricity commercially.
In some parts of the plant, the lights are switched on only when visitors come through. Some original fittings have been replaced with energy-saving LED bulbs, a small concession to modernity in a facility that has otherwise remained largely unchanged since the 1980s.
Now, 40 years after the plant was mothballed, the Philippines is making one of its most concerted pushes yet for nuclear energy. The government is exploring foreign nuclear technologies, identifying potential sites and drawing up plans to award a nuclear power project by the end of 2027.
But the shadows of the past loom over President Ferdinand Marcos Jr’s renewed nuclear ambitions: the legacy of his father’s dictatorship, allegations of corruption that dogged the construction of the power plant, and longstanding safety concerns that have fuelled resistance to its revival.
In the decades since it was mothballed, the Philippines’ only nuclear power plant has found another purpose: educating people about the technology the country has yet to harness. It continues to draw university students, journalists, politicians and nuclear energy experts from overseas.
During a visit by The Straits Times on Nov 10, BNPP employee Mc Reynold Layug led a tour of the containment building housing the reactor, offering a rare glimpse into areas that would ordinarily be inaccessible to the public at an operational nuclear power plant.
He explained how the building’s metre-thick concrete walls and steel lining were designed to contain radioactive material in case of an accident, contrasting its design with that of the reactor involved in the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster, which lacked a comparable containment structure.
“Here, we have a containment building. So if an accident were to happen, the radiation would be contained. Nothing would escape to the environment,” Layug asserted, his voice echoing across the chamber.
Bataan Nuclear Power Plant employee Mc Reynold Layug (left) and National Power Corporation division manager Noel Germano in the plant’s main control room.
Whether these protective measures meet modern-day nuclear safety standards, however, would have to be established before the BNPP could be revived.
But, while the staff spoke enthusiastically about the inner workings of the facility, they were noticeably more circumspect when questions touched, even indirectly, on the politics surrounding its revival. Their standard response was to refer such queries to more senior government officials.
For now, their job is to preserve the plant. Its future lies in the hands of others.
Marcos has made little secret of his disappointment over the Philippines’ decision to mothball the nuclear power plant built under his father’s administration (1965-1985).
During a visit to the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute on Oct 10, Marcos lamented that the Philippines had already made considerable headway in its nuclear programme by 1986, including training professionals whose expertise was never put to use in operating a nuclear power plant.
“We already managed to do the first and the second (phases), and too bad, they stopped it,” he told reporters then.
Marcos also argued that the need to lower electricity prices, among the highest in South-east Asia, was changing public attitudes towards nuclear energy despite longstanding safety concerns.
“We don’t care where our power comes from, but bring it more cheaper,” he said, describing the sentiment among Filipinos grappling with rising electricity bills.
His renewed push for nuclear energy, reaffirmed in his State of the Nation Address in July, has taken on greater urgency amid the Iran war and disruptions to oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
The energy crisis has exposed the Philippines’ vulnerability to imported fossil fuels and given fresh impetus to nuclear discussions elsewhere in South-east Asia, including Singapore and Malaysia, as governments seek to diversify their energy sources and reduce their exposure to global fuel supply shocks.
The dawn of a global renaissance in nuclear energy
ST Explains: What are S-E Asia’s nuclear ambitions and why should S'pore care?
But rehabilitating the BNPP is not the only option being explored by the Marcos administration.
The Philippines is also looking at newer technologies, including small modular reactors, which have smaller generating capacities than conventional nuclear reactors and can be deployed incrementally as electricity demand grows.
On Nov 20, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin told reporters that the Philippines was exploring nuclear technologies from the United States, Russia, Canada, Japan and South Korea, including those offered by Russian state-owned nuclear energy corporation Rosatom.
The Department of Energy (DOE) has also identified seven potential nuclear power plant sites across five provinces – Bataan, Palawan, Masbate, Pangasinan and Camarines Norte – although none has been formally selected. One of the proposed sites in Bataan is the location of the mothballed BNPP.
Patrick Aquino, director of the DOE’s Energy Utilization Management Bureau, told ST that the Philippines was moving beyond policy discussions towards institution building and project preparation.
Under a draft timetable, the government aims to invite companies to bid for a nuclear power project in June 2027 and select the winning bidder by December that year, with the first delivery of electricity targeted for 2038.
The Philippine Energy Plan (2023-2050) envisions 1,200MW of nuclear capacity initially, rising to 4,800MW by 2050, alongside expanded wind and solar power.
US firm plans to build small nuclear power plants in the Philippines
Philippines seeks to have nuclear plants in operation by 2032
While a law enacted in 2025 established the Philippines’ independent nuclear regulator, its staffing and licensing regulations remain unfinished. The country has also yet to finalise its nuclear emergency response arrangements or develop the necessary infrastructure to manage spent nuclear fuel and radioactive waste.
Aquino said a large nuclear power project would require several billion dollars in investments, with the government exploring private sector participation and public-private partnerships.
“The objective is straightforward: make the project bankable without writing a blank cheque either to the developer or to taxpayers,” he said.
Whether rehabilitating the Bataan plant would prove more economical than building a new one remains an open question, experts say.
Construction of the 620MW facility, designed by American firm Westinghouse, began in 1976 under Ferdinand Marcos Sr. Completed in 1984, the plant was left idle in 1986, the year a popular uprising toppled his dictatorship.
Since then, the state-run National Power Corporation (Napocor) has been tasked with preserving the facility.
Today, just 15 Napocor personnel are assigned to the plant, supported by 46 utility workers and about 50 security staff who guard the property 24/7.
A mannequin in a protective suit, the kind workers would have worn inside the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant, stands behind glass in one of the facility’s corridors.
Napocor division manager Noel Germano, a mechanical engineer, told ST that the government spends between 40 million (S$810,000) and 50 million pesos annually maintaining the plant.
Until 2017, personnel could still power up some of its equipment. But after the electricity supply needed for these activities was cut as a cost-saving measure, maintenance was largely reduced to inspections, greasing and manually rotating machinery.
“It is not being tested now, but the preservation work we do continues throughout the year,” Germano said.
He said South Korean assessments in 2010 and 2017 had estimated that rehabilitation would cost around US$1 billion (S$1.3 million) and take four years, he added, although those estimates are now dated.
Aquino stressed that reviving BNPP is not a predetermined outcome. The plant would have to meet modern safety standards and compete favourably with newer nuclear technologies on cost and construction timelines.
“The same principle applies to BNPP: safety first, then technical viability, economics and financing. If a project fails any of those fundamental tests, the appropriate decision is not to force it through but to consider another technology, site or project structure,” he said.
For activists in Bataan, however, the renewed nuclear push has reopened old wounds.
Derek Cabe, 53, who joined the Nuclear-Free Bataan Movement in 2008, said the geological hazards that fuelled opposition to the plant decades ago remain a concern. These include its proximity to dormant volcano Mount Natib and geological fault lines.
Activist Derek Cabe said the geological hazards that fuelled opposition to the plant decades ago remain a concern.
The activist also questioned the safety of burying radioactive waste underground in areas exposed to geological hazards, and whether surrounding communities were sufficiently prepared for a nuclear emergency.
These concerns are compounded by the plant’s history of alleged corruption and questions over the quality of its construction, Cabe said, adding: “I think this is also a matter of trust.”
Catholic priest Mon Mariano, who has campaigned against the plant’s rehabilitation since 2010, pointed to the devastating 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo after centuries of inactivity. He argued that Mount Natib’s dormant status should not be grounds for dismissing the risks.
He also expressed concerns over the deterioration of the ageing facility, given its coastal location and decades of exposure to salty sea air, which can accelerate corrosion.
“At this present time, would you use a 40-year-old car for your daily commute?” he said.
Catholic priest Mon Mariano has campaigned against the plant’s rehabilitation since 2010.
BNPP personnel, however, said during ST’s visit that the facility had withstood the 1990 Luzon earthquake and the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo without suffering major structural damage, based on their assessments.
On how potential nuclear power plant sites would be selected, Aquino said site-specific investigations of seismic and volcanic hazards would be required before any site could be approved.
“The Philippines has existing disaster response and radiological capabilities, but nuclear power-specific emergency arrangements still have to be completed and demonstrated before an operating licence can be issued.”
Such arrangements include evacuation plans, radiation monitoring systems and regular emergency exercises, as well as infrastructure for the disposal of radioactive waste.
For the engineers tasked with preserving BNPP, however, the intervening decades have been a source of regret.
They point to similar nuclear power plants built around the same period in South Korea, Brazil and Slovenia that are now generating electricity, while the Philippine facility has remained idle.
“We have been left behind,” Napocor’s Germano said.

summary: 香港公屋轮候时间创10年新低4.4年 |中国劳工布告栏 星期六, 2026年11月28日·香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港公屋轮候时间创10年来新低至4.4年 香港公屋平均轮候时间已降至4.4年，为十年来最低。一个新的监管部门取代了独立检查部门，现有 300 名员工分布在现有建筑和新建筑中。政府成立了公共住房建筑控制单位来取代以前的独立检查单位。代理菲娜
content:
香港公屋轮候时间创10年新低4.4年 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港公屋轮候时间创10年新低4.4年
香港公屋平均轮候时间已降至4.4年，为十年来最低。一个新的监管部门取代了独立检查部门，现有 300 名员工分布在现有建筑和新建筑中。
政府成立了公共住房建筑控制单位来取代以前的独立检查单位。署理财政司司长兼署房屋署署长黄伟礼在电台节目中表示，该单位已于周一开始运作，共有300名员工。一半分配给现有建筑物，其余则处理新建筑。黄表示，与之前的部门不同，新的控制部门采取项目式的方式，提供宏观视角和服务导向，并由联络官进行解释。
最新公布的公租房平均轮候时间为4.4年，创十年来新低。黄指出，本财政年度还剩两个季度，政府尚未宣布提前实现目标，但他相信有很大机会实现目标。他说，在本届政府的五个财政年度里，传统公共住房的供应量已超过10万套，平均每年2万套。新增简易公房3万套，年均供应量达到2.6万套。
黄还指出，仅传统公租房的平均轮候时间就达5.3年。不过，他对未来的供应充满信心，并表示以2026/27财年为例，竣工量预计将超过36,000套，为25年来的最高水平。

Hong Kong public housing waiting time hits 10-year low of 4.4 years | China Labour Bulletin Board
Saturday, 28 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong public housing waiting time hits 10-year low of 4.4 years
Hong Kong's average waiting time for public rental housing has fallen to 4.4 years, the lowest in a decade. A new regulatory unit has replaced the Independent Check Unit, with 300 staff split between existing and new buildings.
The government has established the Public Housing Building Control Unit to replace the former Independent Check Unit. Acting Financial Secretary and Acting Housing Director Michael Wong Wai-lai said on a radio programme that the unit began operations on Monday, with a total of 300 staff. Half are assigned to existing buildings, while the remainder handle new construction. Wong said that unlike the previous unit, the new control unit takes a project-based approach, offering a macro perspective and a service-oriented view, with liaison officers providing explanations.
The latest average waiting time for public rental housing stands at 4.4 years, a ten-year low. Wong pointed out that there are still two quarters left in the current financial year, so the government has not yet declared that it has met its target ahead of schedule, but he believes there is a high chance it will. He said that over the current administration's five financial years, the supply of traditional public housing has exceeded 100,000 units, an average of 20,000 per year. Adding 30,000 simple public housing units brings the average annual supply to 26,000 units.
Wong also noted that the average waiting time for traditional public rental housing alone is 5.3 years. However, he expressed confidence in future supply, saying that in the 2026/27 financial year, for example, completions are expected to exceed 36,000 units, the highest in 25 years.

香港授予466人荣誉，包括为消防员追授英勇奖章中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港颁授荣誉予466人，包括为消防员追授英勇勋章
行政长官李家超于 11 月 28 日在礼宾府颁发国家勋章。在 466 名获奖者中，消防员何伟豪因 2024 年 11 月在平火中丧生而被追授勇敢金质奖章。其他最高奖项颁给了立法者、学者和商界人士。
行政长官李家超于 11 月 28 日在礼宾府举行的颁奖仪式上向 466 人颁发国家勋章。
三人获颁最高荣誉大紫荆勋章：行政会议成员兼调查大埔宏发苑火灾独立委员会委员陈健波；经济学家刘遵义、中文大学前校长；福建同乡会名誉会长、中银国际副董事长林光兆。
八人获颁金紫荆星章，包括民盟主席、立法会议员陈克勤；卢月明，中文大学校长；以及医院管理局主席范鸿龄。
消防局人员何伟豪于2024年11月在大埔宏发苑发生的第五级火灾中丧生，被追授金英勇勋章。弟弟何伟坚与未婚妻代表他领奖，全场掌声约30秒。政府早些时候宣布，追授何鸿燊奖是为了表彰何鸿燊的勇敢、奉献和无私服务，称他的行为是勇气的最高典范。
根据政府早前公布的消息，共有19人获颁银紫荆星章，40人获颁铜紫荆星章，6人获颁铜英勇勋章。 61人获纪律奖章或廉署立功奖章或嘉许奖章，104人获荣誉勋章，224人获行政长官社区服务奖或公共服务奖。后者包括在第十五届全运会上表现出色的人士、参与组织第十五届全运会、第十二届全国残疾人运动会和第九届特奥会的人士，以及协助筹备启德体育公园开幕的人士。

Hong Kong awards honours to 466, including posthumous gallantry medal for fireman
Chief Executive John Lee presented state honours at Government House on 28 November. Among the 466 recipients, fireman Ho Wai-ho received a posthumous Gold Medal for Bravery for his death in a November 2024 flat fire. Other top awards went to lawmakers, academics and business figures.
Chief Executive John Lee presented state honours at a ceremony at Government House on 28 November, awarding decorations to 466 people.
Three people received the Grand Bauhinia Medal, the highest honour: Chan Kin-por, a member of the Executive Council and a member of the independent committee investigating the Tai Po Wang Fat Court fire; economist Lawrence Lau, former vice-chancellor of Chinese University; and Lam Kwong-siu, honorary chairman of the Fujian Clansmen Association and vice-chairman of BOC International.
Eight people received the Gold Bauhinia Star, including Chan Hak-kan, chairman of the Democratic Alliance for the Citizens and a lawmaker; Lo Yuet-ming, president of Chinese University; and the chairman of the Hospital Authority, Fan Hung-ling.
Fire station officer Ho Wai-ho, who died in a fifth-alarm fire at Tai Po's Wang Fat Court in November 2024, was posthumously awarded the Gold Medal for Bravery. His brother Ho Wai-kin and his fiancée accepted the award on his behalf, prompting about 30 seconds of applause from the audience. The government announced earlier that the posthumous award recognised Ho's bravery, dedication and selfless service, calling his conduct the highest example of courage.
According to earlier government announcements, 19 people received the Silver Bauhinia Star, 40 the Bronze Bauhinia Star and six the Bronze Medal for Bravery. Sixty-one people received disciplinary or ICAC meritorious or commendation medals, 104 received the Medal of Honour, and 224 received Chief Executive's Community Service Awards or Public Service Awards. The latter group included people who performed well at the 15th National Games, those involved in organising the 15th National Games and the 12th National Games for the Disabled and the 9th Special Olympics, and those who helped prepare the opening of the Kai Tak Sports Park.

content:
前加密货币交易所职员在法庭上承认诈骗 900 万港元 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
前加密货币交易所职员在法庭上承认900万港元的贿赂骗局
11 月 28 日，香港一家加密货币交易所的一名前员工承认收受贿赂，将价值近 900 万港元的客户交易转移到未经授权的钱包。廉署调查后根据《防止贿赂条例》提出指控。
香港一家加密货币交易连锁店的一名前员工周四认罪，承认收受贿赂，将价值近 900 万港元的客户交易转移到未经授权的数字钱包。
被告31岁洪伯轩在粉岭裁判法院承认一项串谋代理人接受利益罪名。廉政公署调查后，根据《防止贿赂条例》第 9(1)(a)条及《刑事罪行条例》第 159A 条提出这项指控。裁判官梁雅恩将被告还押惩教署，并押后至12月11日判刑，等待提交背景报告。
法庭获悉，Hung 受聘为 One Satoshi Trading (Hong Kong) Limited 的客户服务和运营助理，该公司在全市经营多家场外加密货币交易网点，提供现金兑换加密货币交易。洪先生驻扎在该公司上水分行，根据公司政策，必须严格通过公司加密钱包执行所有客户采购和销售。
2023 年 8 月至 11 月期间，Hung 与两名身份不明的男子合谋拦截希望交易加密货币的零售客户。 Hung 没有通过 One Satoshi 的授权账户发送订单，而是利用两名同伙提供的外部数字钱包私下处理交易。
在三个月的时间里，Hung 使用未经授权的钱包执行了多次现金交易，处理的交易涉及超过 110 万个 Tether 代币，价值近 900 万港元。作为将业务从雇主手中转移的交换条件，洪从这两人处收受了总计 5,600 港元的贿赂。

Ex-crypto exchange clerk admits HK$9m bribery scam in court | China Labour Bulletin Board
Saturday, 28 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Ex-crypto exchange clerk admits HK$9m bribery scam in court
A former employee of a Hong Kong cryptocurrency exchange pleaded guilty on 28 November to accepting bribes to divert customer transactions worth nearly HK$9 million to unauthorised wallets. The ICAC investigation led to charges under the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance.
A former employee of a Hong Kong cryptocurrency exchange chain pleaded guilty on Thursday to accepting bribes to divert customer transactions worth nearly HK$9 million to unauthorised digital wallets.
The defendant, 31-year-old Hung Pak-hin, entered a guilty plea at Fanling Magistrates' Courts to one count of conspiracy for an agent to accept an advantage. The charge was brought under Section 9(1)(a) of the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance and Section 159A of the Crimes Ordinance following an investigation by the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC). Magistrate Frances Leung Nga-yan remanded the defendant in the custody of the Correctional Services Department and adjourned sentencing to December 11, pending the submission of a background report.
The court heard that Hung was employed as a customer service and operations assistant by One Satoshi Trading (Hong Kong) Limited, which operates several over-the-counter cryptocurrency exchange outlets across the city providing cash-for-cryptocurrency transactions. Hung was stationed at the company's Sheung Shui branch and was required under company policy to execute all client purchases and sales strictly through corporate crypto wallets.
Between August and November 2023, Hung conspired with two unidentified men to intercept incoming retail customers wishing to trade cryptocurrency. Instead of routing the orders through One Satoshi's authorised accounts, Hung utilised external digital wallets supplied by the two accomplices to process the deals privately.
Over the three-month span, Hung executed multiple cash trades using the unauthorised wallets, processing transactions involving more than 1.1 million Tether tokens valued at nearly HK$9 million. In exchange for diverting the business away from his employer, Hung received a total of HK$5,600 in bribes from the two men.

content:
香港敲定亚投行办事处细节，预计很快将修改法律 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港敲定亚投行办事处细节，预计很快将修改法律
香港正在与亚洲基础设施投资银行就设立一个全功能办事处进行谈判，但需要修改法律。财经事务及库务局局长许正宇表示，此举将丰富金融市场，支持“一带一路”项目。
中国财政部与亚洲基础设施投资银行（亚投行）近日签署协议，在香港设立亚投行办事处。财经事务及库务局局长许正宇在11月28日的电台节目中表示，此举意义重大。虽然亚投行已在阿拉伯联合酋长国首都阿布扎比设有办事处，但许表示，香港办事处将成为该行最全面的海外办事处。
许表示，亚投行已在香港使用多项金融服务，包括发行港元债券。他表示，与商业银行不同，亚投行更愿意为各地的长期战略基础设施项目提供贷款。随着亚投行落户香港，银行金融市场将更加多元化，对亚洲及“一带一路”地区产生较强的引领作用。
政府目前正在与亚投行讨论细节。这涉及法律修正案以授予特殊权利，以便亚投行能够作为一个多边组织在香港运作。许先生表示，他希望尽快完成立法修改。
另外，许先生最近访问欧洲后表示，那里的机构对香港的兴趣超出预期，因为它们正在寻求减少对单一经济体的依赖并实现配置多元化。关于黄金清算结算体系，许先生表示，年底前将成立行业协会，香港联交所将公布人民币黄金期货的细节，结算公司将于明年第一季度正式开始运营。
对于现货市场结算周期缩短为T+1，许先生表示，目标是在2028年底或下半年实现，给市场留出适应的时间。他还表示，香港作为亚洲第一金融中心，已承诺要求大型上市公司和金融机构最迟于2028年遵守全球绿色披露标准。

Hong Kong finalises details for AIIB office, law changes expected soon | China Labour Bulletin Board
Saturday, 28 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong finalises details for AIIB office, law changes expected soon
Hong Kong is in talks with the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank to set up a full-function office, requiring legal amendments. Secretary for Financial Services and Treasury Christopher Hui said the move will enrich the financial market and support Belt and Road projects.
The Ministry of Finance of China and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) recently signed an agreement to establish an AIIB office in Hong Kong. Secretary for Financial Services and Treasury Christopher Hui said on a radio programme on 28 November that the move is significant and important. While the AIIB already has an office in Abu Dhabi, capital of the United Arab Emirates, Hui said the Hong Kong office will be the bank's most comprehensive overseas office.
Hui noted that the AIIB already uses many financial services in Hong Kong, including issuing Hong Kong dollar bonds. Unlike commercial banks, he said, the AIIB is more willing to lend money for long-term strategic infrastructure projects in various places. With the AIIB establishing a presence in Hong Kong, the banking and financial market will become more diversified, which will have a strong guiding effect on Asia and the Belt and Road region.
The government is now discussing details with the AIIB. This involves legal amendments to grant special rights so that the AIIB can operate as a multilateral organisation in Hong Kong. Hui said he hopes the legislative changes can be completed as soon as possible.
Separately, Hui said after a recent visit to Europe that institutions there showed greater interest in Hong Kong than expected, as they are seeking to reduce dependence on a single economy and diversify their allocations. On the gold clearing and settlement system, Hui said an industry association will be launched before the end of the year, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will announce details of renminbi gold futures, and a settlement company will officially start operations in the first quarter of next year.
Regarding the settlement cycle for the spot stock market being shortened to T+1, Hui said the target is to implement this by the end of 2028 or in the second half of that year, allowing time for the market to adapt. He also said Hong Kong, as Asia's first financial centre, has committed to requiring large listed companies and financial institutions to comply with global green disclosure standards no later than 2028.

欧盟就代币化政策和绿色金融寻求香港的建议 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
欧盟就代币化政策和绿色金融寻求香港的建议
香港财经事务及库务局局长许正宇表示，欧盟对香港的代币化法规和绿色金融模式感兴趣，希望学习其经验。欧洲官员还寻求有关数字绿色债券和人民币国际化的见解。
香港财经事务及库务局局长许正宇表示，欧盟官员对香港近期的代币化政策和法规，以及绿色金融和资本市场发展表达了浓厚的兴趣。许先生在最近访问欧洲后于11月28日在一个电台节目中发表上述言论。
许表示，欧洲正在寻求绿色转型，旨在通过可持续金融更好地促进当地发展。他指出，欧洲国家也在考虑将存款从传统上由银行和保险公司主导的金融体系转向更多地利用资本市场。许表示，香港在这两个方面都比较先进，可以分享经验，互惠互利。
许表示，欧盟对香港与中国大陆的互联互通、绿色金融举措以及香港最近的代币化政策和法规特别感兴趣。他补充说，欧洲官员希望学习香港的做法，并推出类似措施来推动自身发展。
在国家层面，许先生表示，他会见了比利时和卢森堡的财政部长，官员们希望了解和参考香港最新的金融举措，例如数字绿色债券。他还表示，欧洲本土企业和智库正在研究人民币国际化问题，旨在更好地参与中国和亚洲的发展。
许表示，这次访问反映了欧洲对亚洲的浓厚兴趣，以及希望寻求香港的观点和方法，以帮助他们更多地参与该地区的活动。他表示对双方未来深化合作充满信心。

EU seeks Hong Kong's advice on tokenisation policy and green finance
Hong Kong's Secretary for Financial Services and Treasury Christopher Hui said the EU is interested in the city's tokenisation regulations and green finance model, hoping to learn from its experience. European officials also sought insights on digital green bonds and renminbi internationalisation.
Hong Kong's Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Christopher Hui, said that European Union officials have expressed strong interest in the city's recent tokenisation policies and regulations, as well as its green finance and capital market development. Hui made the remarks on a radio programme on 28 November, following his recent visit to Europe.
According to Hui, Europe is seeking a green transition and aims to better promote local development through sustainable finance. He noted that European countries are also considering shifting their deposits from a financial system traditionally dominated by banks and insurance companies towards greater use of capital markets. Hui said Hong Kong is relatively advanced in both areas and can share its experience for mutual benefit.
Hui said the EU is particularly interested in Hong Kong's connectivity with mainland China, its green finance initiatives, and the city's recent tokenisation policy and regulations. European officials want to learn from Hong Kong's approach and introduce similar measures to drive their own development, he added.
At the national level, Hui said he met with finance ministries in Belgium and Luxembourg, where officials wanted to understand and reference Hong Kong's latest financial initiatives, such as digital green bonds. He also noted that local enterprises and think tanks in Europe are studying the issue of renminbi internationalisation, aiming to better participate in China's and Asia's development.
Hui said the visit reflected Europe's keen interest in Asia and a desire to seek Hong Kong's views and methods to help them engage more with the region. He expressed confidence that both sides can deepen cooperation in the future.

香港财政司长率代表团访问荷兰医疗技术中心 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港财政司长率代表团访问荷兰医疗技术中心
香港财政司司长陈茂波率团访问埃因霍温，参观飞利浦研发园区，探讨人工智能在医疗保健领域的应用。陈先生推广香港的创新计划，并鼓励荷兰企业加深与香港研究机构的联系。
2026 年 11 月 28 日 09:00 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 28 日 09:18 · 阅读时间 2 分钟
香港财政司司长陈茂波昨日率代表团前往荷兰埃因霍温，参观大型医疗科技公司飞利浦位于贝斯特的研发园区。该园区是飞利浦全球最大的园区之一，也是其医疗技术创新的重要基地，涵盖诊断成像、图像引导治疗、人工智能 (AI) 驱动的患者监测和治疗，以及医疗数据和数字健康。
在飞利浦管理层的陪同下，陈先生一行参观了园区研发创新展厅，了解公司在诊断影像、影像引导治疗和人工智能医疗应用等方面的最新技术。随后，双方举行了交流会，讨论了医疗技术研发以及如何通过与医院和研究机构的合作更好地将研究和创新应用于临床。
会上，陈肇始概述了香港第一个五年规划的发展方向和目标，重点介绍了香港建设国际科技创新中心的努力，特别是推动人工智能发展和建立国际医疗创新中心的措施，包括临床试验和药品器械审批制度的更新。代表团成员还介绍了各自机构的业务和研发工作。陈茂波欢迎飞利浦加大在香港的研发创新投入，加强与香港研发机构和大学的合作，共同推动医疗技术创新和商业化，造福更多患者。
中午，陈与代表团出席荷兰一家大银行举办的午餐交流会，了解欧洲最新经济形势和银行业务发展情况，共商合作机遇。同日上午，陈茂波还会见了一家全球大型另类投资和资产管理机构的管理层，了解其在欧洲、亚洲和香港的业务，并就私募股权和资产管理市场交换了意见。陈先生介绍了香港资产及财富管理行业的最新发展以及吸引基金、家族办公室和高净值人士的政策措施，鼓励该机构以香港为平台，帮助客户拓展亚洲业务。
部分代表团成员还出席了荷兰外国投资局主办的早餐介绍会，了解荷兰营商投资环境及相关政策，探讨两地投资合作机遇。陈先生及代表团今日（阿姆斯特丹时间11月28日）结束对荷兰的访问，启程前往香港，预计明日上午（香港时间11月29日）抵达。

Hong Kong finance chief leads delegation to Dutch medical-tech hub
Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan led a delegation to Eindhoven, visiting Philips' R&D campus and discussing AI in healthcare. Chan promoted Hong Kong's innovation plans and encouraged Dutch firms to deepen ties with Hong Kong research institutions.
28 Nov 2026 at 09:00 HKT · updated 28 Nov, 09:18 · 2 min read
Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan yesterday led a delegation to Eindhoven, the Netherlands, visiting the R&D campus of major medical-technology company Philips in Best. The campus is one of Philips' largest globally and a key base for its medical-technology innovation, covering diagnostic imaging, image-guided therapy, artificial-intelligence (AI)-powered patient monitoring and treatment, as well as medical data and digital health.
Accompanied by Philips management, Chan and the delegation toured the campus's R&D and innovation showroom, learning about the company's latest technologies in diagnostic imaging, image-guided therapy and AI medical applications. The two sides then held an exchange meeting, discussing medical-technology R&D and how to better apply research and innovation in clinical settings through collaboration with hospitals and research institutions.
At the meeting, Chan outlined the development directions and goals of Hong Kong's first five-year plan, focusing on the city's efforts to build an international innovation and technology hub, particularly measures to promote AI development and establish an international medical innovation centre, including updates on clinical-trial and drug-and-device approval systems. Delegation members also introduced their respective institutions' business and R&D work. Chan welcomed Philips to increase its research and innovation investment in Hong Kong and strengthen cooperation with Hong Kong R&D institutions and universities to jointly drive medical-technology innovation and commercialisation, benefiting more patients.
At noon, Chan and the delegation attended a lunch exchange hosted by a major Dutch bank, hearing about the latest European economic situation and the bank's business developments, and discussing cooperation opportunities. On the same morning, Chan also met with management of a large global alternative-investment and asset-management institution, learning about its business in Europe, Asia and Hong Kong, and exchanging views on the private-equity and asset-management market. Chan introduced the latest developments in Hong Kong's asset and wealth management industry and policy measures to attract funds, family offices and high-net-worth individuals, encouraging the institution to use Hong Kong as a platform to help clients expand in Asia.
Some delegation members also attended a breakfast briefing hosted by the Netherlands Foreign Investment Agency, learning about the Dutch business and investment environment and related policies, and discussing investment cooperation opportunities between the two places. Chan and the delegation completed their visit to the Netherlands today (28 November Amsterdam time) and departed for Hong Kong, expected to arrive tomorrow morning (29 November Hong Kong time).

台湾竞选活动以大型集会结束，中国战机飞近岛屿
周五，台湾地方选举活动以拥挤的集会结束，中国向台湾派遣了 30 架军用飞机。沉彪马与蒋万安的台北市长竞选备受关注。对台湾拥有主权的北京谴责沉是“分裂分子”。预计周六结果
据路透社报道，周五，在北京密切关注的地方选举竞选活动的最后一天，数万人聚集在台湾举行集会，台北国防部报告称，中国空军活动再次激增。
全台22个市县的市长和县长竞选活动都集中在交通和环境等地方问题上。尽管选举结果不会直接影响对华政策，但北京方面已多次介入。中国谴责了在首都台北市市长关键选举中执政的民进党候选人沉普马。沉因“分裂国家”被中国警方通缉。他本月早些时候告诉路透社，他们从未寻求联系他。
北京声称台湾是自己的领土，并加大了对台湾的压力，要求其接受其主权主张，但台北拒绝了这一要求，包括每天进行空军和海军巡逻。台湾国防部表示，已发现30架中国军机在台湾周边活动，其中26架越过台湾海峡中线，与军舰进行“联合战备巡逻”。中国国防部没有立即回应置评请求。它周四表示，“统一”是不可阻挡的趋势，台湾人民可以因为有“英雄的人民军队保护他们”而感到更安全。
沉从文是一位学者出身的立法者，也是中国信息战专家，他向反对党国民党的现任蒋万安提出了严峻的挑战。当蒋介石在夜间国民党户外集会中召集支持者时，沉因担心交通拥堵而取消了集会计划，并举行了一场在线活动，吸引了超过 50 万 YouTube 观众。相反，总统赖清德在首都邻近城市新北的一次集会上带领支持者高呼沈沉的名字，该党也希望与前总理苏贞昌的女儿苏娇惠一起推翻国民党。
赖先生说：“我恭请大家走完最后一公里，让苏巧慧高票当选，也让彪马沉高票当选。”蒋介石在台北的集会上说，比赛非常接近。他补充说，我们的对手阵营正在全面、有力地动员起来。 37岁的安东尼·黄(Anthony Huang)表示，他投票给蒋介石，因为他在过去四年里为这座城市的发展做了很多好事。他在参加蒋介石的集会时说，我觉得他的对手是一个相当不合格的候选人。 49岁的安吉拉·王(Angela Wang)从加拿大飞来，她说她会投票给沉。 “最重要的是，我发现他是一个非常真诚的人，这在任何政治家中都很难见到，”她在他的竞选总部外说道。

Taiwan election campaigning ends with large rallies, Chinese warplanes fly near island | China Labour Bulletin Board
Saturday, 28 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Taiwan election campaigning ends with large rallies, Chinese warplanes fly near island
Taiwan's local election campaigning concluded with packed rallies on Friday, as China sent 30 military aircraft near the island. The Taipei mayoral race between Puma Shen and Chiang Wan-an is closely watched. Beijing, which claims Taiwan, denounced Shen as a 'separatist'. Results are expected Saturd
Tens of thousands of people packed rallies in Taiwan on Friday on the final day of campaigning for local elections closely watched by Beijing, as Taipei's defence ministry reported another surge in Chinese air force activity, according to Reuters.
Campaigns for mayor and county magistrate in all Taiwan's 22 cities and counties have focused on local issues such as transport and the environment. But while the results will not directly affect China policy, Beijing has repeatedly weighed in. China has denounced Puma Shen, the governing Democratic Progressive Party's (DPP) candidate in the key election for mayor of the capital Taipei. Shen is wanted by Chinese police for 'separatism'. He told Reuters earlier this month they had never sought to contact him.
Beijing, which claims Taiwan as its own territory, has ramped up pressure on Taiwan to accept its sovereignty claims, which Taipei rejects, including with daily air force and navy patrols. Taiwan's defence ministry said it had detected 30 Chinese military aircraft operating around the island, 26 of which crossed the Taiwan Strait's median line, carrying out a 'joint combat readiness patrol' with warships. China's Defence Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It said on Thursday that 'reunification' is an unstoppable trend and that Taiwan's people could feel safer with a 'heroic people's army to protect them'.
Shen, an academic-turned-lawmaker and an expert on China's information warfare, has put up a stiff challenge to incumbent Chiang Wan-an from the opposition Kuomintang (KMT). While Chiang rallied his supporters at an evening outdoor KMT rally, Shen, who cancelled plans for a rally owing to fears of traffic congestion, held an online event, attracting more than 500,000 viewers on YouTube. President Lai Ching-te instead led supporters in chanting Shen's name at a rally in New Taipei, the capital's neighbouring city where the party is also hoping to unseat the KMT with Su Chiao-hui, daughter of former premier Su Tseng-chang.
'I respectfully ask all of you to complete the final mile, and let Su Chiao-hui be elected with a high vote, and let Puma Shen also be elected with a high vote,' Lai said. Chiang told his rally in Taipei that the race was very close. 'Our opponent's camp is mobilising fully and forcefully,' he added. Anthony Huang, 37, said he was voting for Chiang as he had done good things for the city's development in the past four years. 'I feel that his opponent is a fairly unqualified candidate,' he said, attending Chiang's rally. Angela Wang, 49, who flew in from Canada, said she would vote for Shen. 'Above all, I find that he's a very genuine person, which is hardly seen in any politicians,' she said outside his campaign headquarters.
Polls will be open from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. (0000-0800 GMT) on Saturday, with results expected early in the evening. At the last local elections four years ago, the KMT thrashed the DPP, winning 14 cities and counties to 5 for the DPP. Other parties or independents won the other three. Manoeuvring for presidential and parliamentary elections, to be held early in 2028, will begin in earnest after Saturday's vote. While Lai will almost certainly stand for a second term, the maximum allowed under the constitution, the KMT has not confirmed its candidate. Its likely frontrunner is former journalist Lu Shiow-yen, mayor of the central city of Taichung.
The KMT traditionally favours close ties with Beijing, whose government refuses to talk to Lai, labelling him a 'separatist'. Lai says only Taiwan's people can decide their future. KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun visited Beijing in April and met Chinese President Xi Jinping.

content:
夫妇因护照页丢失被捕，在香港保释中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
夫妇因护照页丢失被捕，在香港保释
一对因涉嫌撕毁特区护照四页而被捕的香港夫妇已获保释。法医测试显示这些页面被强行移除，这与该妇女关于工厂缺陷的说法相矛盾。两人面临更改旅行证件和误导移民局等指控
一对香港夫妇因特区护照缺失四页而被捕（法医检验证实护照被强行撕毁），在被拘留过夜后已获保释，等待进一步调查。
这名27岁女地产代理及其34岁男友均为香港居民，周五晚上9时10分左右，没有回答传媒提问，就步行前往将军澳地铁站。
两人周四晚在蓝田平田村平春楼被捕，涉嫌未经合法授权涂改旅行证件、管有和使用非法涂改旅行证件，以及误导入境事务处人员。
这名女子在本周早些时候的一次生日旅行中被拒绝入境日本，并因护照上缺少四页而被遣送回同一航班，随后引发了一场备受瞩目的争议，此次逮捕引发了一场备受瞩目的争议。返回香港后，她在社交媒体上疯传的帖子中声称，缺失的页面是由于工厂装订缺陷造成的。
移民官员在周四晚上的新闻发布会上透露，政府实验室的法医检查发现，在被撕下的页面上发现了人为篡改留下的纸纤维残留物，证明这本小册子被强行篡改了。官员还指出，该护照是八年前的 2018 年签发的，旅行记录证实该女子此前曾使用同一份文件前往多个目的地，没有任何问题，这表明该护照在签发时完好无损。

Couple arrested over missing passport pages released on bail in Hong Kong | China Labour Bulletin Board
Saturday, 28 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Couple arrested over missing passport pages released on bail in Hong Kong
A Hong Kong couple arrested for allegedly tearing four pages from an SAR passport were released on bail. Forensic tests showed the pages were forcibly removed, contradicting the woman's claim of a factory defect. The pair face charges including altering a travel document and misleading immigration s
A Hong Kong couple arrested over four missing pages in an SAR passport—which forensic tests confirmed were forcibly torn out—have been released on bail pending further investigation after being detained overnight.
The 27-year-old female property agent and her 34-year-old boyfriend, both Hong Kong residents, walked out of the Immigration Department headquarters in Tseung Kwan O at around 9.10pm on Friday without answering media questions before heading on foot toward Tseung Kwan O MTR station.
The pair were arrested at Ping Chun House, Ping Tin Estate in Lam Tin on Thursday evening on suspicion of altering a travel document without lawful authority, possessing and using an unlawfully altered travel document, and misleading Immigration Service members.
The arrests followed a high-profile controversy sparked after the woman was denied entry to Japan and sent back on the same flight during a birthday trip earlier this week because four pages were missing from her passport. Upon returning to Hong Kong, she claimed in viral social media posts that the missing pages resulted from a factory binding defect.
Speaking at a press briefing on Thursday night, immigration officials revealed that forensic examination by the Government Laboratory detected paper fiber residues left by human tampering where the pages had been removed, proving the booklet had been forcibly altered. Officials also noted that the passport had been issued eight years ago in 2018 and that travel records confirmed the woman had previously used the same document to visit multiple destinations without issue, showing the booklet was intact when issued.

content:
坑口单车场外发现老人身亡 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 28 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
老人在坑口单车场外被发现死亡
周六凌晨，一名70多岁的男子被发现死在坑口香港单车馆外的空地上。警方正在调查死因和该男子的身份。
警方称，周六凌晨，一名70多岁的男子被发现死在坑口香港单车馆外的空地上。
警方于凌晨1时左右接获路人举报，称一名男子躺在宝康路105至107号场地外的地上，不省人事。
急救人员赶到现场，宣布该男子当场死亡。太平间工作人员随后将尸体移走。网上流传的图片显示，警察和护理人员用白布覆盖尸体。
警方正在调查以确定死者的身份和确切的死因。

Saturday, 28 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Elderly man found dead outside Hang Hau velodrome
A man in his 70s was discovered dead in an open area outside the Hong Kong Velodrome in Hang Hau early on Saturday. Police are investigating the cause of death and the man's identity.
A man in his 70s was found dead in an open area outside the Hong Kong Velodrome in Hang Hau early on Saturday morning, police said.
Officers received a report from a passer-by at around 1am about an unconscious man lying on the ground outside the venue at 105–107 Po Hong Road.
Emergency personnel arrived at the scene and pronounced the man dead on the spot. Mortuary workers later removed the body. Images circulating online showed police officers and paramedics covering the body with a white cloth.
Police are investigating to establish the deceased's identity and the exact cause of death.
